title: A GripForge project (project.gripforge by default) (complete: syntax and kits)
description: The entry point of a game, like project.godot: the kits it needs and installs, their settings, its data, and the list and flow of its scenes, written inline in it. Optional: a game may use the kits from its code alone. JSON, owned by the game, without a version field. This schema is the reference of the syntax. Complete schema assembled by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs: the syntax schema plus the fragment of each kit, referred to as gripforge.kit/<kit id> (GENERATED, do not edit).

$schema.description: For editors only: the path of the schema the file follows (core/scene-format/schema/gripforge.full.schema.json); never read by a kit.

sources.description: The Rust files of the game's own code, declared by the project (the only entry: no file is taken by convention). Paths relative to the folder of the project file, with /, each once. gripforge-build adds them to the game's own compiled module (native and wasm); one of them declares the module of the game (`pub struct X;` with `impl KitModule for X`). The development mode compiles nothing and only reads them.

includes.description: Other .gripforge files merged under this one, in order (resolved first by core/scene-format, crate::include): their kits, variables, data and scenes; this file wins on its own kits' config and keys.

installed.description: The kits installed, in order, with their settings.

version.description: Exact version; read from the kit when packing in the repository.

config.description: The kit's settings (its configSchema).

variables.description: The game's variables and their start values. A start value may read another variable ({ "$var": "<path>" }), to relay an include's parameter.

bindings.description: Asset slots bound to files of the Library.

data.description: The game's documents by collection (archetypes, scenes, scripts, hooks, mods...).

scenes.description: The scenes and their flow (game.engine), each written inline (requires, nodes, kits, on, meta: the keys of #/$defs/scene), or naming a sub-scene carried in data.scene_files (file). The kit game.engine also describes its document form (gripforge.kit/game.engine#/$defs/data/scenes).

file.description: Path of a sub-scene carried in data.scene_files. Without it, the scene is written inline (nodes).

enabled.description: A disabled scene leaves the flow (read at the start).

scene_files.description: The sub-scenes the project carries, by path (instanced by scene nodes, or named by a scene's file).

run.description: What the packer puts in the game.json: seed, fixedHz, physics.

fixedHz.description: The action tick in Hz; absent: game.engine tick.hz, else 30. Never the physics step (tick.physicsHz, 60 by default).

meta.description: Free meta-information of the project (author, description, notes of the tool that wrote it); kept as written, never read by a kit.

schema.description: The id of the project block of a game.json (gripforge.gameproject/1), when the project is taken from one; kept as written.

preset.description: The preset of the project block of a game.json, when the project is taken from one; kept as written.

scene.description: The content of a scene, written inline in data.scenes[] (or carried as a sub-scene in data.scene_files): a tree of typed nodes, its sub-scenes, the kits' sections, its bindings. Read with tolerance (docs/dev-builder.md, docs/ecrire-un-projet.md).

$schema.description: For editors only: the path of the schema a scene file follows (gripforge.full.schema.json, #/$defs/scene); never read.

on.description: The bindings of the scene itself: entered, left, event.

meta.description: Free, for the editor; never read by a kit.

requires.description: The kits this whole file needs (never per node). Not an installation: a missing kit refuses the scene with what to install; the build, the CLI and the MCP read it to propose the kits.

binding.description: Interactivity without code: when something happens, run game.engine verbs.

when.description: enter/leave: a trigger; interact: a model or shape; entered/left: the scene (its own on); event: a named event (event).

event.description: The event that runs the binding, with when: event.

do.description: game.engine verbs: emit, call, set_var, inc_var, load_scene, push_scene, show, hide... A verb's "on" may name a node by path (../Crate).

props_model.description: A 3D model file of the project, given to game.engine as an instance (its archetype, or one made from these properties).

asset.description: Path of the model file in the project (models/crate.glb); its passport in asset.meta stays its identity.

material.description: A material name of the game, or { color, metallic, roughness, ... } laid over the file's materials.

props_shape.description: A simple shape drawn natively by each engine, given to game.engine as an instance.

size.description: box: [x, y, z] or one number; plane: [x, z].

radius.description: sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone, torus.

tube.description: torus: the radius of the tube.

material.description: A material name of the game, or { color, metallic, roughness, ... }.

props_light.description: A light declared by the game, placed by dev.builder through core.light (adopted at its path in the engine's tree, else made there).

kind.description: The kind of light; a directional light shines along its -Z axis.

intensity.description: In the units of core.light, which places the light: lux for a directional light, lumens for a point or spot light; unset: core.light's default for the kind.

range.description: point and spot: the distance where the light ends, in metres.

angle.description: spot: the outer angle of the cone, in degrees.

props_camera.description: A camera of the scene, placed by dev.builder through core.camera (adopted at its path, else made), with the fixed preset looking along its -Z axis.

fov.description: The vertical field of view, in degrees.

current.description: Whether this camera draws when the scene is entered.

props_trigger.description: A trigger zone (game.engine zones): bindings run when something enters or leaves it.

size.description: box: its size in metres.

radius.description: sphere: its radius in metres.

watch.description: The tags of the entities the zone watches (empty: the player).

props_sound.description: A sound of the scene, played by the sound kit when there is one.

asset.description: Path of the sound file in the project.

spatial.description: A 3D voice placed at the node.

props_hud.description: A HUD slot of core.webui (<kit>/<slot>) and the HUD asset it shows.

asset.description: Path of the HUD asset package in the project; empty: the asset the kit recommends.

props.description: The properties given to the asset.

node.description: A node of the scene. Unknown keys are kept and reported; a value that does not fit warns and takes its default, never an error.

name.description: Unique among its siblings: the link of the node's path (Hall/Door).

id.description: Optional stable identifier, unique in the scene: it survives renames and moves, a binding, an override or a command may name the node by it, and it is the id game.engine receives (prefixed by the instance node inside a sub-scene).

position.description: Metres, relative to the parent; right-handed, +Y up.

rotation.description: By default Euler angles in degrees [x, y, z], applied Y, X, Z (yaw, pitch, roll), relative to the parent; a quaternion { x, y, z, w } is accepted too.

scale.description: Per axis, or one number for all three.

visible.description: Hidden with its children when false; bound to a variable with { "$var" } (followed at render through the reflection).

overrides.description: scene nodes: { "<path in the sub-scene>": { <keys to merge> } }; name and children cannot be overridden.

scene.description: scene nodes: the path of the instanced sub-scene (carried in data.scene_files).

entity.description: The entity of the element (docs/entites-et-rendu.md, the writing of game.engine): its states (kept in the game.engine entity, or derived) and the render values bound to a state. A node with states counts for the game: it gets an entity (a group too: a light entity holding the states), and it can be used (on: interact).

states.description: The states, as a game.engine archetype declares them (given to it as written): { values, default? } (an enumeration, default the first), { default } (a stored value) or { derived: { var | component | expr | hook } } (computed, never stored).

bind.description: Render values of nodes of the element's subtree that follow a number state, after the rules (game.engine's bind, plus node).

node.description: The node of the look it names (a bone): its last name is looked up.

offset.description: The grip under that node: position (metres), rotation (degrees), scale.

sockets.description: The points others hang on (docs/attache-sur-un-os.md): a name (hand_r, head) to a node of the look and a grip.

reflect.description: The table state → reflection (game.engine's reflect, per node of the subtree): rules that act on any node of the element's subtree (its children: models, sounds, lights, particles, HUD slots, sub-scenes), resolved by game.engine's resolver and posed by dev.builder in the engine's tree. What has no way yet (a model change, a clip, a sound, spin, on, the tween of a transition) is listed in dev.builder.reflect's pending.

bind.description: Which values of the render the entity drives (position, yaw), property by property: bound, an edit changes the entity and the render follows; free, the value is the render's own. Default: position bound, rotation and scale free. A render value that follows a state goes in entity.bind of its element.

position.description: The node's position ↔ the entity's x, y, z; null: free.

yaw.description: The node's heading (its -Z axis around Y) ↔ the entity's yaw; null (the default): free.

variables.description: The node's game variables and their start values, named <id>.<name> (the node needs an id); a start value may be { "$var" }.

quat.description: A rotation as a unit quaternion { x, y, z, w } (the form of the editor and of the site's commands); normalised when read.

state.description: A state of the element besides its default one (the first, « no change », which every entity has), written as a game.engine archetype declares it: an enumeration (values, default), a stored value (default), or derived, never stored (derived).

default.description: The value when the game has not set it; the first of values when left out.

values.description: The enumeration of the values (a bool is [false, true]).

derived.description: Computed from one source, never stored, saved nor synchronized (its source is): var (a game variable path), component (a component of the entity, or { name, field }), expr ({ var, op?, value? }, { all }, { any }, { not }, a constant), hook (true: game.engine's hook game.engine.state.derive answers).

state_bind.description: A render value bound to a number state (game.engine's bind, plus node).

node.description: The path of the node under the element; empty or left out: the element itself.

property.description: Degrees for a rotation axis, a factor for a scale, metres for an offset; laid under the node's pose in the file.

from.description: The state it follows (declared in entity.states).

reflect_rule.description: A rule of the reflection (game.engine's): when the states match (partial: only the states named, one value each; empty: always), set the given properties on nodes of the element's subtree. Every matching rule applies, in order: a later one wins on the same property.

set.description: { <path relative to the element, "" the element itself>: { visible, rotation, scale, offset, material, anim, slot, shape, morphs, fade, light, play, playing, spin, on } }: game.engine's fields (a pose laid under the node's pose in the file, as game.engine lays a rule under a root's base pose: rotation in degrees, scale, offset in metres), plus the props of that node's type, play (a sound once), playing (a sound in a loop), spin ({ rpm, clockwise }: a turn that never stops), on (bindings active).

transition.description: Optional: { duration (s, 0 to 60), ease, play (a sound at its start) }, played at the render, never at the first reflection.

play.description: The sound node played at its start.

$var.description: The path of a game variable: a root variable (an included file's prefixed <as>.<name>) or a node's (<id>.<name>).

varRef.description: Reads a variable; allowed in visible, in a variable's start value and in data.scenes[].enabled.

file.description: A complete .gripforge, relative to the file that includes it.

as.description: Prefix of what comes from the file: its root variables (<as>.<name>) and its scene file paths (<as>/<path>). Default: the file name without extension.

variables.description: Start values of the included file's root variables (unknown name: include_unknown_variable).

scenes.description: Scene ids taken out of the flow (and of game.engine's startScene).

nodes.description: <scene id>:<path> or <scene id>:#<id>, set visible: false.

overrides.description: <scene id>:<path> or <scene id>:#<id> → keys merged into the node, as the overrides of a sub-scene.

gripforge.kit/ai.combat.title: ai.combat in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.combat.description: What the kit ai.combat adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The combat genres { brain, params } by id (melee, ranged, boss, horde by default); a kit, the game or a mod adds or overrides one, registerGenre does it at run time. melee, the default genre, is a base entry.

Genres by name: { brain: <a core.ai brain: team, sight, hearing, order…>, params: <the orders' parameters> }. The game's genres are added to the kit's defaults (a genre of the same name replaces the default).

defaultGenre.description: The genre of an order run by a brain given none.

forgetSeconds.description: Seconds after which an entity no more seen counts for nothing (certainty 0).

players.description: Tags of the players (distances, the horde's bands).

allyRadius.description: Radius in which fighters of the same team count as allies (retreat when outnumbered).

coverTag.description: Tag of the entities that are covers (their radius: component `cover.radius`, else coverRadius).

coverRadius.description: Radius of a cover without its own.

health.description: Where the health is in the business states: { key, max, full } (ratio key / max, or / full).

damageTopic.description: The event of a hit { target, source, amount, ranged } that feeds the threat tables; empty: none.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of ai.combat (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/ai.creature.title: ai.creature in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.creature.description: What the kit ai.creature adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

profiles.description: The species by id (config profiles, declareProfile): base, deer, wolf, fish, bird built in; diet, temperament, speeds, radii, needs, herd, predators and prey, taming, all in data.

genres.description: The brain genres by id (config genres, declareGenre): the profile and the core.ai brain (sensors, standing order, interrupts with their priority) a creature of this genre gets.

creatures.description: The creatures the game declares: [{ tag | entity, genre, pack, home, brain: { team, sight, … over the genre's } }]. An archetype may carry the same object as its `creature` component.

profiles.description: Species profiles the game adds or replaces: [{ id, inherit, diet, temperament, space, walkSpeed, runSpeed, runHold, senseRadius, dangerRadius, safeRadius, predators, prey, taming: { … }, … }], key by key over the inherited one (base by default).

genres.description: Brain genres the game adds or replaces: [{ id, inherit, profile, brain: { team, sensors, order: { kind, interrupts } } }].

threats.description: Entities every creature fears besides its predators: [{ tag | entity, severity }]. Empty: only predators by profile.

food.description: The tags of the entities that are plants, meat and water for the creatures.

autoResolve.description: Whether a bite, a sip or a strike is resolved by the kit as soon as it is asked (through the hooks ai.creature.consume and ai.creature.strike). Off: the game resolves it (resolve) once its own kit applied it.

senseEvery.description: core.ai's period of the kit's sensors, in ticks (1: at every thought of the brain; more: read again at the first thought once that many ticks have passed). The answers are worked out at the kit's own tick; a sensor call only reads them.

seed.description: The seed of the creatures' random streams (mixed with each entity id).

registerOrders.description: Whether the kit registers its orders and sensors with core.ai at ready.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of ai.creature (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/ai.gather.title: ai.gather in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.gather.description: What the kit ai.gather adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

nodes.description: The node genres by id (config nodes, declare('nodes', def)): tree, rock, bush, vein built in; a game, a mod or a player adds its own in data.

jobs.description: The jobs by id (config jobs, declare('jobs', def)): gatherer, hauler, builder built in.

plans.description: The building plans by id (config plans, declare('plans', def)): hut, fence built in.

seed.description: The seed of the scatter: same seed, same nodes, on every target.

nodes.description: Node genres the game declares besides the built-in ones (tree, rock, bush, vein): [{ id, inherit?, item, count, uses, tool, respawnSeconds, harvestSeconds, size, weight, extractable }]. An existing id is replaced; `inherit` starts from another genre, key by key.

jobs.description: Jobs besides gatherer, hauler, builder: [{ id, inherit?, tasks: [build|haul|harvest], capacity, carrySlow, speed, reach, items, preferNeeded, harvestRate, buildRate }].

plans.description: Building plans besides hut and fence: [{ id, inherit?, materials: { item: count }, workSeconds }].

scatter.description: Nodes laid at the start, seeded: [{ genre, count, center: [x, z], radius, spacing (2.5) }].

clearSpawn.description: No scattered node nearer than this to `spawn` (where the player starts).

spawn.description: Where the player starts, kept clear by the scatter.

sites.description: Building sites laid at the start: [{ plan, at: [x, y, z] }].

depots.description: Entities that take loads: [{ entity | tag, accepts: [item] (empty: all) }].

workers.description: Entities that work: [{ entity | tag, job, tools: [item], brain: { team, sight, … } }]. Each gets a core.ai brain whose standing order is ai.gather.work with its job.

extractors.description: Machines that extract from the nearest extractable node: [{ entity | tag, rate (1) }].

extract.description: How far a machine finds its node, and whether a node never wears out under a machine.

registerOrders.description: Whether the kit registers its orders with core.ai at `ready` (off: the game registers what it wants itself).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of ai.gather (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/ai.navigation.title: ai.navigation in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.navigation.description: What the kit ai.navigation adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

cellSize.description: Size in metres of one grid cell of the bake. Smaller cells pass narrower doors but cost more cells.

padding.description: Margin in metres added around the start and the goal when the region to bake is chosen.

maxCells.description: Largest number of grid cells one bake may hold; a larger region fails with budget_exceeded or outside.

maxLayers.description: Most walkable floors stacked in one grid cell (ground, bridge, upper storey).

layerOverflow.description: A cell with more floors than maxLayers: block makes that cell non-navigable (routes go elsewhere), reject fails the whole bake.

plansPerTick.description: Most routes planned in one tick; the next callers get waiting and are served on a later tick.

approach.description: Metres: a goal inside a body or off the floor ends at the nearest reachable floor within this distance; 0 keeps exact goals only (unreachable).

sharedBakeCells.description: A world of at most this many cells (within maxCells) is baked once for every agent instead of one window per request.

retrySeconds.description: An actor whose route is not ready asks again when its goal or the static world changes, otherwise at most every retrySeconds once it changed cell or moving bodies moved.

smooth.description: Straighten the grid steps into segments checked like baked edges (floor, collision, moving blockers).

bakeCellsPerTick.description: On the tick (no loop of its own), heavy work is spread over ticks while the actor waits: this many cells, then nodes, per tick; 0 does everything at once.

bakeBudgetMs.description: On the tick, milliseconds of each frame the bakes may spend, on the wall clock; 0, or a host without a clock (a replay), uses bakeCellsPerTick instead (deterministic).

bakeTile.description: Metres: the region a route is baked on is widened to whole tiles of this size, so nearby goals reuse a baked region; 0 bakes regions as asked.

drive.description: The pilot of the entities this kit drives in core.control (driver owner ai.navigation): it writes control.move@1 and control.wanted_dir@1 toward ai.navigation.next@1 at each tick, and core.locomotion moves them.

arrive.description: Metres to the goal (horizontal) under which the intents are zero: the entity stops.

slow.description: Metres to the goal under which the wanted move shortens with the distance left (0: full speed up to arrive).

agent.description: Default size of a walking actor when the caller gives none.

radius.description: Agent radius (m).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of ai.navigation (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/ai.social.title: ai.social in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.social.description: What the kit ai.social adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

roles.description: The roles by id (config roles, declare('roles', def)): base, villager, pedestrian, guard, shy, companion built in.

activities.description: The activities of a schedule by id (config activities, declare('activities', def)): work, eat, sleep, stroll built in.

genres.description: The genres by id (config genres, declare('genres', def)): ai.social.habitant, pedestrian, guard, shy, companion built in; each a role and a core.ai brain.

characters.description: Characters declared by the game: [{ entity | tag, genre (ai.social.habitant), role, places: { home: [x, y, z], work, square… }, leader, brain: { team, sight, order… } }]. Each gets the core.ai brain of its genre. An archetype may carry the same as its component `social`.

roles.description: Roles besides the built-in ones (base, villager, pedestrian, guard, shy, companion): [{ id, inherit?, walkSpeed, greet: { radius, cooldown, duration, topic }, reaction: greet|watch|avoid|ignore, watchRadius, walkAway, wander, companion, schedule: [{ from, to, activity, place }] }].

activities.description: Activities besides work, eat, sleep, stroll: [{ id, inherit?, order (pushed at the place; empty: go there and use it), speed, sociable }].

genres.description: Genres besides ai.social.habitant, pedestrian, guard, shy, companion: [{ id, inherit?, role, brain: <a core.ai brain> }].

notice.description: The tags of whom a character notices (greets, watches, avoids).

senseEvery.description: core.ai's period of the kit's sensors, in ticks: read again at the first thought of a brain once that many ticks have passed.

registerOrders.description: Whether the kit registers its orders and sensors with core.ai at `ready` (off: the game registers what it wants itself).

spacing.description: Metres between two slots of a formation (ai.social.form_up), unless the order says its own `spacing`.

formUp.description: The formation of ai.social.form_up. Read at each thought: changed while the game runs, it holds at the next one.

radius.description: Metres from `to` at which the escort is done.

keep.description: Metres the escort keeps from the one it escorts (it waits when farther).

leash.description: Metres beyond which the escorted one is far: the escort goes back to it.

lostAfter.description: Seconds the escorted one may stay unseen before the escort fails (lost).

escort.description: The defaults of ai.social.escort, each field over the kit's; an order's own arguments win. Read at each thought (live).

slowWithin.description: Metres from its target under which a character slows down (its intent shortens with the distance left).

minPace.description: The shortest intent while slowing down, a fraction of the full pace (0 to 1).

steer.description: How the served orders turn a move into core.ai's intent. Read at each thought (live).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of ai.social (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/ai.stealth.title: ai.stealth in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.stealth.description: What the kit ai.stealth adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The stealth genres { brain, params } by id (guard, stalker by default); a kit, the game or a mod adds or overrides one, registerGenre does it at run time. guard, the default genre, is a base entry.

Genres by name: { brain: <a core.ai brain: team, sight, hearing, order…>, params: <the orders' parameters> }. The game's genres are added to the kit's defaults (a genre of the same name replaces the default).

defaultGenre.description: The genre of an order run by a brain given none.

forgetSeconds.description: Seconds after which an entity no more seen counts for nothing (certainty 0).

players.description: Tags of the players (distances, the horde's bands).

senseEvery.description: Ticks between two awareness senses of a brain (the sensor's period in core.ai).

defaultLight.description: Light on an entity that says none (business state `light`, 0..1).

noiseRadius.description: Radius of a noise of loudness 1 for the gauge.

traces.description: Trails: { tags, every, strength, maxAge, max } (who leaves traces, how often, kept how long).

health.description: Where the health is in the business states: { key, max, full }.

gripforge.kit/ai.vehicle.title: ai.vehicle in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/ai.vehicle.description: What the kit ai.vehicle adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

profiles.description: The driver profiles by id (config profiles.<id>, declareProfile): default, commuter, calm, racer and rival built in; a game or a mod adds its own in data, inheriting key by key, never in code.

Driver profiles the game declares, by id: { inherit, <keys of a profile> } (cruise, laneOffset, steerGain, lookahead, skill, aggression...). An id already known (built in: default, commuter, calm, racer, rival) is replaced; a profile changes only the keys it gives over the one it inherits (default when it names none).

defaultProfile.description: The profile of a driver whose order names none.

world.description: The roads and places the drivers use: { lanes: { nodes: { id: [x,y,z] }, links: [[a,b]] }, tracks: { id: { points: [[x,y,z]], closed, width } }, spots: { id: { pos, yaw, size } }, arena: { center, radius } }. Changed live by setWorld.

drivers.description: The drivers the game declares: [{ entity | tag, profile, order: { kind, args }, team }]. Each gets a brain of core.ai at ready (brainFor) running its order; empty (the default): no driver.

obstacleTags.description: The tags of what a driver sees around it (all are obstacles in its lane).

vehicleTag.description: The tag of a vehicle: only vehicles hold a crossing, a lane, or are chased.

playerTag.description: The tag of what the player drives (a chase prefers it by the profile's playerWeight).

outTag.description: The tag of a vehicle out of play (never chased).

senseRadius.description: How far a driver sees the bodies around it (m).

traffic.description: The traffic population: off by default. On: every `every` seconds it looks at the vehicles tagged `tag` (`takenTag`: taken by the player or a driver), asks for cars (event ai.vehicle.traffic, do = spawn | recycle | release) to keep density x maxVehicles around the player, and gives each new one a brain that roams the lane graph with `profile`.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. enabled.description: Off: nothing is kept; every visit downloads the files (once each).

quotaMB.description: Megabytes the store may hold; past it the entries leave in the order of eviction. 0 keeps nothing.

version.description: Generation of the store: a store written with another one is emptied when it opens (raise it to empty every player's cache).

store.description: auto: IndexedDB in a page, the cache folder in native; memory: this run only; off: nothing kept.

eviction.description: Which entries leave when the quota is reached: lru (read longest ago), fifo (written first), none (a full store keeps nothing more).

minBytes.description: Files smaller than this are not kept (they download fast anyway); 0 keeps every file.

folder.description: Native: the cache folder, under the engine's own cache or user data folder (Bevy: the platform cache folder; Godot: user://; Unity: Application.temporaryCachePath; Unreal: the project's saved folder). A relative name, no '..'.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. config.description: The settings of asset.cache (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

passport_sections.description: The passport fields: asset.meta's own blocks (base, never removed), the sections the game or a mod declares in the config key passport_sections (read at setup, they replace a section of the same name), and those the loaded kits hand at ready() (expose entries for passport, only when asset.meta is loaded). A section has one owner.

The passport sections the game or a mod declares (registry passport_sections): { "<section>": { kit?, fields: [{ key, type, default, column?, version?, write?, read? }] } } or a list of { id, kit?, fields }. A section given here replaces the fields of the same section (asset.meta's own blocks keep their place); its owner is kit (game when absent), and a kit that exposes the same section later does not take it over.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of asset.meta (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

id.description: The slot (or slot:variant, or Library id) the passport describes.

passport.description: The resolved mesh passport: { etalon, orientation, scale, rig, colliders, anim, landmarks, fits, kits: { <section>: … } } (plain data, metres, +Y up). Its blocks and the kit sections are declared by the expose entries for passport (docs/exposer-au-passeport.md).

gripforge.kit/asset.preload.title: asset.preload in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/asset.preload.description: What the kit asset.preload adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

cellTriggers.description: The genres of trigger that decide the ring of a cell (near, around, far): zones, distance and scenes (base, never removed nor replaced), the config key cellTriggers of a game or a mod, then registerCellTrigger at run time ({ service, method } asked (scene, spec)). declareCell and declareLoader are not registries: a cell is a scene of game.engine (its section, the config cells.list), and declareLoader is the announcement of the engine adapter.

cells.description: 2.1: the world loaded by cells (docs/design/monde-par-cellules.md): the defaults of every cell. A cell is a scene of game.engine declared in its section kits["asset.preload"], in list, or in code (declareCell).

trigger.description: The trigger of a cell that names none: auto (zones when world.zones is in the game and the cell names a zone, else distance when it has a center, else scenes) or a genre of cellTriggers.

everyTicks.description: Action ticks between two decisions (a declaration, a zone entered or a call decides at the next tick).

preload.description: The around ring of the distance trigger: radius x preload.

keepS.description: Seconds a far cell stays loaded before it is unloaded and its files given back.

maxLoaded.description: At most this many cells put in game.engine at once: the far ones go first, then the around ones; a near cell is never unloaded for it.

mode.description: A near cell whose files are not in: background (the game goes on, the cell appears when ready) or screen (a step of game.engine holds the game: the loading screen comes back with the progress).

focus.description: The entity followed (empty: the entity tagged player); setFocus changes it.

items.description: A cell: scene, then the fields of the section kits["asset.preload"].

list.description: Cells declared in the config (the sections of the scenes come after and win).

refine.description: 2.1: progressive textures. A file a glob names is loaded light first (its copy of the family made by tools/texture-compress, <root>.<family>/<rest>, in the phase of the file) and whole behind the game; asset.preload.refined then names both once and the adapter swaps it in place. Leave it off on Unity and Unreal (they stream their mip levels themselves).

family.description: The family of the light copies.

match.description: Globs on the path or the id of a file (* within a folder, ** across).

enabled.description: Off: the plan is empty; files are loaded only when asked (still once each).

defaultPhase.description: The phase of a file the plan cannot place (a game without scenes, a file of no scene). first: the game starts once everything is in (the behaviour before the kit).

nextScenes.description: auto: on each scene entered, the files of the scenes after it (game.engine order) are loaded ahead in phase next; none: never ahead.

aheadScenes.description: How many scenes ahead auto prepares.

concurrency.description: Files in the loader's hands at once, on every engine and on the web: attachNative and takeNext hand at most this many.

backgroundConcurrency.description: Of those places, at most this many for the files behind the game (background, next): what the game waits for (phase first, wantScene, request) always finds room.

memoryMB.description: Megabytes of downloaded files kept in memory for late callers (asset.cache keeps the rest).

verify.description: Check the SHA-256 of every file that has one, also when it comes from the cache.

warm.description: Wait for the engine's pipelines and shaders still building (counted by core.shader) before the first frame (first_ready) and before a scene is ready: nothing stutters the first time it is drawn.

progressEveryMs.description: At most one asset.preload.progress event per this many milliseconds (the variables are always current).

match.description: A glob on the path or the id of a file: * within a folder, ** across folders.

rules.description: Patterns of files placed by the game before the documents: [{ match: "assets/hud/*", phase: "first", priority: 5 }], in order (a later rule wins).

loader.description: Who loads the files. auto: the engine of the target when its adapter announces its loader (declareLoader; bevy names itself by its target), else the plan is told in at the first update; engine; page: a web page loader attaches (attachNative) and gives the bytes to the player; none: nobody, the files are there and the plan is told in at once. While a loader is expected the loading stays open until it attaches: no count, no wait.

retries.description: How many times a file that fails to load is loaded again before it is given up and shown as failed (asset.preload.failed with retry false, the progress names it in failures). 0: a failure is final at once.

retryDelaysMs.description: The pause in milliseconds before the 1st, 2nd, 3rd new try of the same file, read by the page loader and by the bridge of the web player (the last one repeats). A dropped request is not asked again at once.

modelsAtOnce.description: How many models the bridge of the web player hands to the player at once (docs/memoire-lecteur.md): the next one goes when the player says one is loaded. Fewer keeps the memory peak of the tab lower, more loads a large scene sooner.

modelsStallMs.description: How long in milliseconds the bridge of the web player waits for a model it handed before it hands the next ones anyway: a player that stays silent never blocks the loading.

modelsHoldMs.description: How long in milliseconds the bridge of the web player holds the models back while the player runs but no entity waits for one yet, so the nearest ones go first once it says which (models_wanted). 0: no hold.

cellTriggers.description: 2.1: the genres of cell trigger a game or a mod adds (registry cellTriggers), by id: { "<id>": { service, method } }, asked (scene, spec) at each decision, answers near, around or far; a cell names it in trigger. The base genres zones, distance and scenes (and auto) are never replaced. registerCellTrigger adds one at run time.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of asset.preload (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

sceneSection.description: What asset.preload reads on a scene.

element.description: Which element of asset.preload this section is (cell when left out).

then.title: Cell
then.description: 2.1: this scene is a cell of the world: put in beside the current scene when the player is near (shown) or around (loaded, hidden and inert), unloaded when far.

element.description: Which element of asset.preload this section is (cell when left out).

zone.description: The zone of world.zones that makes it near (trigger zones).

preloadZone.description: The zone that makes it around.

neighbours.description: Scenes around it: around whenever it is near (and the trigger scenes).

center.description: [x, z] or [x, y, z]: its centre for the trigger distance.

radius.description: Metres around center for the near ring.

mode.description: background or screen; empty: the config mode.

trigger.description: A genre of cellTriggers (empty: the config trigger).

then.title: Cell
then.description: 2.1: this scene is a cell of the world: put in beside the current scene when the player is near (shown) or around (loaded, hidden and inert), unloaded when far.

element.description: Which element of asset.preload this section is (cell when left out).

zone.description: The zone of world.zones that makes it near (trigger zones).

preloadZone.description: The zone that makes it around.

neighbours.description: Scenes around it: around whenever it is near (and the trigger scenes).

center.description: [x, z] or [x, y, z]: its centre for the trigger distance.

radius.description: Metres around center for the near ring.

mode.description: background or screen; empty: the config mode.

trigger.description: A genre of cellTriggers (empty: the config trigger).

id.description: Id of the document (and of an added file).

asset.description: The file it is about: an asset id or slot of the game, or its path. Absent = id.

path.description: Path or URL of a file the game does not list (added by the game or a mod).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of an added file, 64 hex digits (checked, and the key of the cache).

scene.description: The scene the file belongs to (for the scenes ahead).

remove.description: True: out of the plan, loaded only when asked.

blendSeconds.description: The seconds of a glide of the blend.

rooms.description: The rooms: [{ id, min: [x, y, z], max: [x, y, z], mixState, ambience }].

portals.description: The portals: [{ id, a, b (rooms or outside), at: [x, y, z], open (0 to 1), occlusion (a profile of core.audio) }].

areas.description: The areas: [{ id, sound (a sound of core.audio's bank, played in a loop), at ([x, y, z], the centre), radius (heard at full volume within; 0: everywhere), fade (metres beyond the radius to silence, default 10), volume (0 to 2) }]. ambiences.description: The named ambiences: { name: [{ sound, volume (0 to 2) }] }, layers of looping sounds cross-faded by setAmbience.

initial.description: The named ambience on at the start ("": none).

bus.description: The bus of core.audio the ambience plays on.

seconds.description: The seconds of a fade (an area that starts, moves or stops; a change of ambience without its own seconds).

gainStep.description: How much the gain of an area moves before it is told again to core.audio (a few changes while walking, never one per frame).

volume.description: The player's volume of the ambience (a setting: the settings kit sets it, else this default).

cues.description: The cues: [{ event, action (play, stop, param; default play), sound (a sound of core.audio's bank; "" with play: the event is silenced), when, unless, ifVar (plain values that must be equal), volume (0 to 4), pitch (0.25 to 4), unique (play only when the voice this cue holds is not playing: a loop an event starts, proposed name), key (the payload field naming the holder of the voice, default the entity of the event), param, range, pitchRange, volumeRange (param), spatial (false: always 2D) }]. gripforge.kit/audio.music.title: audio.music in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/audio.music.description: What the kit audio.music adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

playlists.description: The playlists: { id: { tracks: [sound ids of core.audio's bank], shuffle (false), loop (true) } }. A single looping track loops by itself; a playlist that does not loop ends in silence.

states.description: The music states: { state: playlist } ("": silence). A state going to the playlist already playing lets it go on.

fade.description: The seconds of a cross-fade between two tracks.

initial.description: The music state at start ("": none until the game sets one).

seed.description: The seed of the shuffle (the same seed, the same order: replays).

menuStates.description: The music states the player's setting menus silences when it is off.

menus.description: The music of the menu states is heard (the player's setting audio.music.menus).

level.description: The level of the music in its bus, from 0 to 1 (the player's setting audio.music.level).

gripforge.kit/audio.speech.title: audio.speech in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/audio.speech.description: What the kit audio.speech adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: What the voice moves on a speaker, by id (config genres.<id>, registerGenre): face, jaw and none shipped; a kit, a mod or the game adds its own in data (a robot whose lights pulse, a radio) or changes one field by field.

speakers.description: The speakers by name (config speakers.<name>, addSpeaker): their genre, entity, rig, visemes, expressions, channels and voice; a game or a mod declares or replaces one, its origin (config, call) is kept for the debugger.

The speakers by name: { genre, entity (default: the name), rig: { headBone, eyeBones, chain, forward, up, jawBone, jawAxis, jawMaxAngle }, visemes (the morphs of each class of viseme), expressions (the morphs of each emotion), blink: { left, right }, gestures: { clip }, channels, voice: { bus, volume, spatial } }. A name no speaker declares is an entity of defaultGenre.

genres.description: Genres added or laid over the shipped ones (face, jaw, none), by id: { mouth: { kind, params, morphs }, gaze: { kind, params }, blink: { kind, params }, expressions: { <emotion>: { morph: weight } }, gestures: { clip }, letters, phonemes, channels }. The kinds are core.animation's procedural kinds.

channels.description: The kit's defaults of the channels, under the genre, the speaker and the line: { mouth, expressions, gaze, gestures: false | an intensity 0..1 | { on, intensity } ; gaze also maxYaw, maxPitch (degrees) ; priority (a number or game, dialogue, cinematic) ; fade (s) }.

priorities.description: Named priorities added to game 200, dialogue 600, cinematic 800 (the priority of the sources and of the gesture on core.animation's layer upper).

defaultGenre.description: The genre of a speaker that declares none (none: the voice and its timing only).

cueLines.description: A timed line is said as a dated intention of core.audio (cue, key audio.speech:<speaker>:<n>): the mouth then follows the voice really heard (lipsync heard). Off by default while core.audio does not read the cues at its tick (the voice is then not in core.audio.voices: no ducking, no out-of-context rule); on: the speaker A or B plays it.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }.
