gripforge.kit/camera.photo.title: camera.photo in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/camera.photo.description: What the kit camera.photo adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

filters.description: The filters by name: none, mono, sepia, warm, cool, vivid, noir and dream shipped (logic/filters.json); a game or a mod adds or replaces one in data (config filters.<name>) or in code (registerFilter), and lists those offered (order).

radius.description: How far the free camera may fly from where the player stands (metres).

minHeight.description: The lowest height of the camera above the player's feet (metres): it never passes under the ground they stand on (a large negative value: no floor).

fov.description: Field of view when the mode opens and nothing better is known (degrees).

speed.description: Flight speed of the camera with the axes move and rise or the pad of the overlay (metres per second).

lookSpeed.description: Turn speed of the camera with the axis turn, a stick or keys (radians per second at full tilt).

move.description: A vector action of core.input: x right, y forward, -1..1.

rise.description: An axis action of core.input: up, -1..1.

turn.description: A vector action of core.input: the look held, x right, y up, -1..1, at lookSpeed.

axes.description: The named axes of core.input the mode reads in place at each update (no action heard, no call per press). The kit declares them without keys, in the context of the mode, unless the game declared them itself; the game gives their keys. An empty name: not read.

look.description: The name of a PointerFollow block published in the zone (core.input.look.0: the look of player 0) read in place to turn the camera with the pointer, at lookSensitivity. Empty (the default): the pointer is the overlay's (a drag turns the camera, the cursor is free).

lookSensitivity.description: Radians of turn per unit of the pointer's look (look).

filters.description: Filters added to (or replacing by name) the shipped ones (registry filters): { <name>: { css, label?, labels?: { fr }, exposure? } }; css is a CSS filter list (grayscale(1) sepia(0.4)…) the overlay previews and the capture applies.

order.description: The filters offered, in this order (names of the registry; none is always first).

context.description: The context of game.engine the mode pushes (declared by the kit when missing).

priority.description: Priority of the camera take of game.engine.takeover (above a dialogue, under the debugger).

shotWidth.description: Width of a picture when shoot() is given none.

shotHeight.description: Height of a picture when shoot() is given none.

keep.description: How many pictures the kit keeps (picture(ticket)); older ones are dropped.

hud.description: The game's HUD while the mode is open: `hide` (the default) lets core.webui's rule hide it with the `default` context, `keep` leaves it shown (what the rule shows in `default`; an element hidden for another reason, a scene or a menu, stays hidden) and gives it back to the rule on closing. Needs core.webui, else nothing changes. It is also the default of the `hud` option of shoot (the HUD on the picture).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of camera.photo (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.ai.title: core.ai in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.ai.description: What the kit core.ai adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The brain genres a brain naming genre starts from; an ai.* kit, the game or a mod adds one (registerGenre at run time).

orders.description: The order kinds { call } a kit serves; registerOrder at run time.

actions.description: The actions { call, args } | { button } | { input }; use, pickUp, putDown and useItem are given by the kit and never removed; registerAction at run time.

sensors.description: The sensors { when, every } | { call, every }; registerSensor at run time.

brains.description: The brains the game declares: [{ entity | tag, team, sight, hearing, vigilance, sensors: [id…], order }]. An archetype may also carry its brain as the component `ai` (same fields). Empty: no brain, the kit rests.

genres.description: Brain genres by name: { genre: <brain declaration> }; a brain naming `genre` starts from it (registerGenre does the same from a kit).

orders.description: Orders declared in data, by kind: { kind: { order: <spec, `$$name` takes the order's argument> } } or { kind: { call: "service.method" } } (a kit serves it). A base order's kind cannot be taken.

actions.description: The registry of actions, by name: { call: "service.method", args: ["$entity", "$target", "$<arg>"…] } (a kit's service), { button: name } (a button intent of core.control), { input: name } (an action of core.input fed for the actor). move, face and look are core.control's intents. Not registered: a button of core.control by that name, else core.input's action.

sensors.description: Sensors by id: { when: <condition>, every } (a state of the game read as the fact id) or { call: "service.method", every } (a kit's sense, called with (entity, [x, y, z])). every: the ticks between two readings (default 10), read at the first thought of the brain once they have passed, whatever its period.

sight.description: The sight a brain has when its declaration says nothing: { range, angle (full, degrees), eye, obstacles (a line of sight asked to core.physics), tags (what it looks at, besides the other brains), contact (felt under this distance whatever the cone), every (thoughts between two looks) }.

hearing.description: The hearing a brain has when its declaration says nothing: { range (m, for a noise of loudness 1), threshold }.

vigilance.description: What raises and lowers the vigilance: { sight (per second while a hostile is in sight, times its nearness), hearing (per noise, times its loudness), decay (per second), levels [[name, threshold]…], forget (seconds) }.

teams.description: The team of an entity without a brain, by tag.

attitudes.description: The table: { teamA: { teamB: friendly | neutral | hostile } }. Same team: friendly.

defaultAttitude.description: Between two teams the table does not name.

lod.description: The LOD of the brains: the first row whose `within` (m) holds the nearest entity of `lodFrom` gives `every` (ticks between two thoughts).

lodFrom.description: The tags the LOD measures from (the players).

controlPriority.description: The priority core.ai claims an entity with in core.control (a cinematic or a player above it takes the hand).

view.description: The AI view (drawn by core.ai's presentation module, at the render): on, the brain followed (follow: an entity, empty: every brain), the team shown (empty: every team), ticks between two refreshes (every), rays of a sight cone cut by the walls (rays, 2 to 64), and the layers (sight, hearing, noises, memory, target, path, orders, box). Off by default: nothing is built. The debugger shows these switches as buttons (entry core.ai.view).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.ai (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.animation.title: core.animation in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.animation.description: What the kit core.animation adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

tables.description: The tables state to clip by name (config tables.<name>, registerTable).

states.description: The action states and their layer: the built-in ones of core.locomotion (base, never removed), then those the game or a mod declares in the config key states, then each kit's (registerState: reload, attack.light, mount.ride).

sourceKinds.description: The kinds of procedural source (the kit ships spring, gaze, blink, lipsync, footstep, lean, breath and footIk as data; config sourceKinds.<id>, registerSourceKind): a kit or a game adds look_at, handIk, recoil, cloth... without a mandatory dependency (a source of a kind nobody registered is reported, the rest plays).

outOfContext.description: What an entity animated does while the context on top of game.engine's stack is not one of its contexts (docs/hors-contexte.md): a behaviour (freeze: the clip holds its frame and takes up where it was, the default; stop: held on the first frame, played again from its start; continue; end: read as stop), or { behavior, contexts } (contexts: those of an entity that names none; absent: default). Each animated entry and the options of animate take their own contexts and outOfContext. Nothing without game.engine.

tables.description: Tables by name, schema gripforge.animation.table/1: { layers: { <layer>: { mask, priority } }, rows: [{ state, clip, loop, fade, rate: { from, per }, hold, holdMoving, layer, priority, when, fallback }] (no movement: a row with movement or moveScale is refused, the kit of the action publishes it with its state), fallback: { <state>: <state> }, procedural: [{ id, kind, targets: { bones, chains, nodes, morphs }, phase, layer, priority, weight, fade, when, exclusive, params }] }. The first row of a state whose when holds wins. when: <value> <op> <number> joined by &&; values speed, along, down, vertical, takeoff, air_time, direction, grounded, crouched (read in place in the columns locomotion.*: along is the speed along the ground at the touch on land, at the take-off otherwise; takeoff the along speed at the take-off of the air phase, 0 after a fall from a ledge); ops < <= > >= == !=; evaluated at a change of state only. hold: seconds the row keeps playing while the body stays on the ground (holdMoving: the shorter hold when the body moves on). fallback of a row: the clips tried, in order, before the common names. The table default is the built-in one (the clip choice of the former controller kits); a table of the game named default replaces it.

clipNames.description: Common clip names tried for a state after the row's own fallback (case ignored, as the players match): a standard model (the 43 clips of a Quaternius Universal Animation Library pack: Idle_Loop, Walk_Loop, Jog_Fwd_Loop, Crouch_Idle_Loop, Crouch_Fwd_Loop, Jump_Start, Jump_Loop, Jump_Land, Roll, Swim_Idle_Loop, Swim_Fwd_Loop...) plays without a line written. Data, moddable: the game's list of a state replaces the default one.

animated.description: The entities animated at start: [{ entity | tag, table, mode: publish }]. Empty: the game calls animate.

layers.description: The layers a state is published on, by name: { mask (a mask of the animation layers: full, upper, lower, arms... by humanoid region or by bone), priority }. At most 4, named from body, upper, additive, face (Damien, #869): body takes the whole body; upper plays over it (reload while running); additive adds over the others (a flinch); face plays the face (expressions, lips). 2 by default (body and upper): a layer not listed is not read.

archetypes.description: The clip of an element by ARCHETYPE (the game.engine archetype of the node of the element core.animation.clips, or of the instance that spawned): { "<archetype>": { state: the name of a business state of the instance (game.engine), clips: { "<value>": "<clip>" | { clip, fade, speed } }, loop: a clip looped from the pose when no value picks one (a prop without states), speed (0: 1) } }. An instance of a listed archetype gets its element when it spawns (game.engine.instance.spawned). The key "*" is the rest pose of every other instance drawn with a model slot: { loop: "idle" } by default (the model's idle, its rest pose without one); { loop: "" } or null turns it off. Order: the kit's default < archetypes.<archetype> < what the node writes (not neutral) < the hook core.animation.map_state. Never a clip name in the entity: the clip goes in the reflection.

bone.description: The node of the model the eyes hang on (found by its name, else by its name after a colon, underscore, dot or dash: mixamorig:Head); no such node: under the root, with a warning.

boneOffset.description: Where the middle of the eyes is, in the frame of the node `bone` (m): the eyes follow it when the bust leans. `height` and `forward` are used only under the root (a model without that node, a bare capsule).

eyes.description: Two simple eyes on the front of the entities (a test bench, a prototype without a face), so that one sees where they look: enabled (false by default) gives them to every entity animated by the kit; setEyes(entity, params | false | null) to any entity. height (m above the root), spacing (between the eyes), radius, forward (in front of the axis), color, pupil, bone and boneOffset. The render side draws them on the node `bone` of the model (the head), else under the entity's root (presentation module of the blank players; the kit's Bevy crate keeps the root), NEVER on a model that has eyes already (a node named oeil or eye), and turns them toward the target of the entity's look source (lookAt), else along the front of the body. Read in the var core.animation.eyes, written only when they change.

clipSounds.description: The sound markers of the clips, by clip name: { length (s, the loop; 0: the clip plays once), marks: [{ at (s in the clip), sound (core.audio's bank), volume, pitch, late, lateMax }] }. Scheduled ahead from the clock line of the base clip and posed as dated intentions of core.audio (cue, clock tick): the sound comes out when the image that shows the marker is displayed. A new decision stops what is not out yet. Without core.audio nothing is posed.

clipSoundsAhead.description: Seconds of the clock line of a base clip whose markers are posed ahead at each tick.

mode.description: publish, the only mode: the kit publishes the states and their reflection (clip, fade, rate, fallback chain, action over the body) in its own memory, never in the entity, never saved nor synchronised; a render module applies it to the drawn model (reflectEpoch, then reflections), or the game's own graph (AnimationTree, Animator, AnimBP) plays the states. The mode play was removed (game.engine retired.json, docs/retraits.md): game.engine says it as an error at the mount, the kit plays publish.

procedural.description: The procedural sources: enabled (on by default, Damien #869: a declared source runs; nothing runs and nothing is computed for an entity without a declared source; false turns every source off), passport (the sources the model's passport declares are applied too), phases (the order they run in at the render after the clips: pose, aim, secondary by default; a source names its phase, sources of one phase run by priority then declaration order). sources (proposed name: the sources the game gives every animated entity, each as in a table's procedural block, with an optional tags: [...] that limits it to the entities carrying one of them; the sources of the entity's table come after, and win on the same id: a face is declared once for the characters that have one). lookAtSource / winkSource / expressionSource (proposed name; the ids lookAt, wink and setEmotion act on when the call names none).

sourceKinds.description: The kinds of procedural source by id, over those the kit ships as data (spring): { owner, phase, schema: { <param>: { type, default, min, max, doc } }, presets: { <name>: { <param>: value } }, native: { godot, unity, unreal, bevy }, calculator: { engines } } (the schema gives the defaults and the limits of each param of a source, tunable hot and shown by the debugger; native is the engine solver each engine uses, calculator.engines where our own code runs it). What is given here changes only what it names of a shipped kind. A kit, a mod (the sourceKinds data registry) or a game adds its own (registerSourceKind, or provide_registerSourceKind in the engine language).

states.description: The action states the game or a mod declares (registry states), by name: { "<name>": { layer?, owner? } } (layer body by default, owner game), or a list of { id, layer?, owner? }. Held from setup, before the registerState of the kits (a state already held keeps its layer and owner).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.animation (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

nodeSection.description: What core.animation reads on a node.

element.description: Which element of core.animation this section is (clips when left out).

then.title: Clips of a state
then.description: The clip of the node follows a business state of its game.engine instance (the entity says sitting, the kit plays the clip; never a clip name in the entity), or loops one clip (a prop without states). Written as the section kits.core.animation of a node, or as a child node of type animation ({ type: animation, animation: { state, clips, loop, speed } }) that animates its PARENT (a model, an entity) and is never an entity itself. A neutral value takes the rule of the node's game.engine archetype (config archetypes.<archetype>), else the kit's default (nothing).

element.description: Which element of core.animation this section is (clips when left out).

state.description: The name of the business state of the instance that picks the clip (pose, door…); empty: the archetype's.

clips.description: State value to clip: { "sitting": "Sit_Idle", "standing": { "clip": "Idle", "fade": 0.3, "speed": 1 } }; laid value by value over the archetype's (this node's win); null: the archetype's.

loop.description: A clip looped from the pose when no value picks one (a windmill, a flag); empty: the archetype's.

speed.description: The playback rate; 0: the archetype's, else 1.

then.title: Clips of a state
then.description: The clip of the node follows a business state of its game.engine instance (the entity says sitting, the kit plays the clip; never a clip name in the entity), or loops one clip (a prop without states). Written as the section kits.core.animation of a node, or as a child node of type animation ({ type: animation, animation: { state, clips, loop, speed } }) that animates its PARENT (a model, an entity) and is never an entity itself. A neutral value takes the rule of the node's game.engine archetype (config archetypes.<archetype>), else the kit's default (nothing).

element.description: Which element of core.animation this section is (clips when left out).

state.description: The name of the business state of the instance that picks the clip (pose, door…); empty: the archetype's.

clips.description: State value to clip: { "sitting": "Sit_Idle", "standing": { "clip": "Idle", "fade": 0.3, "speed": 1 } }; laid value by value over the archetype's (this node's win); null: the archetype's.

loop.description: A clip looped from the pose when no value picks one (a windmill, a flag); empty: the archetype's.

speed.description: The playback rate; 0: the archetype's, else 1.

animation.title: Clips of a state
animation.description: The clip of the node follows a business state of its game.engine instance (the entity says sitting, the kit plays the clip; never a clip name in the entity), or loops one clip (a prop without states). Written as the section kits.core.animation of a node, or as a child node of type animation ({ type: animation, animation: { state, clips, loop, speed } }) that animates its PARENT (a model, an entity) and is never an entity itself. A neutral value takes the rule of the node's game.engine archetype (config archetypes.<archetype>), else the kit's default (nothing).

state.description: The name of the business state of the instance that picks the clip (pose, door…); empty: the archetype's.

clips.description: State value to clip: { "sitting": "Sit_Idle", "standing": { "clip": "Idle", "fade": 0.3, "speed": 1 } }; laid value by value over the archetype's (this node's win); null: the archetype's.

loop.description: A clip looped from the pose when no value picks one (a windmill, a flag); empty: the archetype's.

speed.description: The playback rate; 0: the archetype's, else 1.

moveScale.description: What an action leaves of the movement, one contribution per layer (publish): the smallest wins; a state ended withdraws its own.

gripforge.kit/core.audio.title: core.audio in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.audio.description: What the kit core.audio adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

mixStates.description: The mix states a game may glide to, by name; a game or a mod changes one (config mixStates.<name>).

outOfContext.description: What a voice does while the context on top of game.engine's stack is not one of its contexts (docs/hors-contexte.md): a behaviour (freeze: paused where it is, the default; stop: paused, played again from its start; continue; end: stopped at once), or { behavior, contexts, kinds } (contexts: those of a voice that names none; absent: the context on top when it started; kinds: a behaviour per bus, music and ui continue by default). The options of play take a voice's own contexts and outOfContext. Nothing without game.engine.

outputBus.description: The bus every other bus goes into (it reaches the engine's output).

buses.description: The buses: { gainDb (the game's level, added to the others), chain: [{ id, type, ...params, impulse }] (in order; type one of highpass, lowpass, lowshelf, highshelf, peaking, compressor, limiter, reverb, distortion) }. A scene or a mod changes one bus or one value, the others keep their default.

effects.description: The params of each type of effect: { type: { param: { default, min, max } } }. A param out of its bounds is refused, never corrected.

mixStates.description: The mix states a game may glide to: { name: { buses: { bus: { gainDb (added), effects: { id: { param: value } } } } } }. A state names only what it changes.

mixState.description: The mix state at start ("": none).

mixSeconds.description: The seconds of a glide to a mix state when the caller gives none.

duck.description: The ducking rules: [{ id, when (a bus), buses, db (<= 0), attack, release (seconds), notch: { hz, q, db } }]: while a voice plays on when, the buses are lowered by db, and the notch digs a bell at hz into them.

sliders.description: The player's sliders: { buses (one slider each), default (0 to 1), exponent (the gain is the value to that power), floorDb (at or under it: silence) }.

roles.description: The roles of the sounds: { role: { bus, lufs } }: the bus a sound of the role plays on and the loudness it is brought to (trim = target - measured).

maxTrimDb.description: The largest trim a role applies, up or down, in dB (a sound measured wrong cannot burst).

master.description: The master's integrated loudness target: { lufs }, checked on the output; its true peak ceiling is the master limiter's ceilingDbtp.

spatial.description: The 3D profiles: { name: { minDistance, maxDistance, rolloff (linear, inverse, exponential), rolloffFactor, hrtf, air: { startDistance, endDistance, hzNear, hzFar }, occlusion (a profile name, or "") } }.

occlusion.description: The occlusion profiles: { name: { transmissionClosed (0 to 1), hzClosed, hzOpen } }: through a wall `openness` open, the gain is transmissionClosed..1 and the lowpass hzClosed..hzOpen (in octaves).

sounds.description: The bank: { id: { src: [files] (several: variants, never the same twice in a row), bus, volume (0 to 2), pitch (0.25 to 4), volumeJitter, pitchJitter, loop, spatial (a 3D profile, "": 2D), priority (0 to 100), limit (voices of this sound at once, 0: none), duration (seconds, 0: the speaker tells the end), role, tags, late (what a dated cue of it does when late: drop, play, skip; "": intents.late), lateMax (s; 0: intents.lateMax) } }. A wrong sound is said and the bank refused, never corrected.

maxVoices.description: The most voices at once: one more takes the place of the lowest priority, then the oldest, or is refused.

seed.description: The seed of the variants and the jitter: a replay plays the same.

listenerStep.description: How far the listener moves, in metres, before core.audio.listener is told again (the kits that follow the listener work only then).

speaker.description: What the speaker of each engine reads beside the mix (published in core.audio.mix): { moveStep (metres a listener or a 3D voice moves before the speaker asks hearAt again), moveSeconds (the glide of a voice's gain and cutoff then), meterHz (how often the speaker measures its buses for the debugger; only while the debugger is loaded), fftSize (the analysers' window), loudness: { blockSeconds, overlap, absoluteGate, relativeGate } (the gated loudness of ITU-R BS.1770), web (which web speaker plays: auto, the AudioWorklet mixer where the memory is shared, else the Web Audio nodes with the reason said; worklet; nodes) }.

intents.description: The audio intentions in the zone, read in place by every speaker (docs/design/core-audio-intentions.md): lanes (one per kind of writer: the kit, the page, the physics, the render), cueSlots (rows of one lane of core.audio.cues), boundSlots (held sounds following a value, core.audio.bound), heardSlots (voices whose position heard is published, core.audio.heard), sourceSlots (drawn poses of the sources, core.audio.shown), late (what a dated cue does when its time has passed: drop, play, skip; a sound of the bank may say its own) and lateMax (s: how late a drop may still play).

transition.description: The law of every glide: { settle }: the share of the way done after its seconds (an exponential approach, as Web Audio's setTargetAtTime).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.audio (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.camera.title: core.camera in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.camera.description: What the kit core.camera adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

presets.description: The presets a game may pick, by name; a game or a mod changes the params of one (config presets.<name>).

shakeProfiles.description: The shapes of shake by name (built-in hit, rumble, explosion): the game's config shakeProfiles over them field by field, then registerShakeProfile.

fov.description: Vertical field of view of a new camera, degrees.

near.description: Near clip plane of a new camera, metres: nothing closer is drawn. Applied natively by each engine with the pose (Bevy PerspectiveProjection.near, Godot Camera3D.near, Unity Camera.nearClipPlane, Unreal the camera's custom near clipping plane, the player's lens); setClip changes it on a running camera.

far.description: Far clip plane of a new camera, metres: nothing farther is drawn (beyond near). Applied natively by each engine with the pose (Bevy PerspectiveProjection.far, Godot Camera3D.far, Unity Camera.farClipPlane, the player's lens; Unreal draws to infinity in perspective and has no far plane per view: not applied there, a known limit of the README); setClip changes it on a running camera.

outOfContext.description: What a camera does while the context on top of game.engine's stack is not one of its contexts (docs/hors-contexte.md): a behaviour (freeze: its last pose stays, no look turns it, the default; continue: it goes on drawing and listening; stop and end: read as freeze, a camera has no start to replay), or { behavior, contexts } (contexts: those of a camera that names none; absent: default). Each camera of `cameras` and setOutOfContext(camera, ...) take their own contexts and outOfContext; this is only the fallback. Nothing without game.engine.

presets.description: The presets a game may pick, each with its default params (proposed, never imposed); a scene or a mod changes them (moddable, live).

thirdPerson.description: Behind the target, on its look. height: the pivot above its feet; distance: the arm; shoulder: sideways offset. yawFrom: look (the camera's own look, the default) or target (the heading of the target as drawn: the camera comes back behind it by itself once the look has not moved for followDelay seconds, at followSpeed per second; the mouse and setLook always come first). followDelay and followSpeed only count with yawFrom target (followSpeed 0 never follows).

firstPerson.description: At the eyes of the target. eyeHeight: metres above its feet in the axes of the world (no attach). point: a named point under the target (node, bone, socket of the engine) the camera rides; offset: [x, y, z] in the frame of the point (or of the target); yawFrom: look (the camera's own look, the default) or target (the yaw of the target as drawn, only the pitch from the look: the look's yaw turns the character, read from core.input). All off by default: nothing read or computed.

target.description: The mode target: frames the subjects of setSubjects (1 to N, weighted). height: the pivot above their feet; distance: the shortest arm (from the anchor, the target the camera follows, when there is one); maxDistance: the longest; margin: the room kept around them (1: the farthest one on the edge of half the field of view); pitch: radians when framed from the anchor (with no anchor, the look's); shoulder: sideways offset; turnSpeed: how fast the yaw and the arm come to what the subjects ask, per second (0: at once). The look's yaw does not turn the camera in this mode; its pitch does with no anchor.

walls.description: The defaults of the walls option (off on every camera until the game turns it on with setWalls): clearance, minimum arm, return rate, five rays or one, eye view under eyeBelow and back above eyeBelow + hysteresis, eye drop, glide seconds, what to hide (designated by the game; empty: nothing).

rays.description: Where the rays come from (auto by default): auto = the physics (core.physics, asynchronous) when it is loaded, else a ray on the drawn meshes or shapes, bounding boxes first, stopping at the first wall; physics; mesh = a ray on the drawn meshes by the engine's own way, no physics; combined = both, the nearer wall kept.

fadeNear.description: The defaults of the fadeNear option (off on every camera until the game turns it on with setFadeNear): the general fade of a drawn object (model.fade, applied natively by each engine) posed on what the camera follows, whole beyond start, gone at end (metres from the camera to the object's bounds; 0.7 / 0.6 from gm-3 PR #300); targets: followed, between (also the objects between the camera and its target, faded out over fadeTime seconds) or a list of targets (designated by the game); mode: alpha (a true opacity, 0 at end, the default) or dither (the engine's dithered crossfade).

freeLook.description: The defaults of the free look offset and the zoom of a third person camera (setFreeLook).

lookInput.description: The defaults of the look read from the pointer or a stick (setLookInput).

input.description: Where the look comes from: auto = the actions of core.input when that kit is loaded, else the engine's own pointer; actions; raw = the engine's own pointer or stick. core.input is recommended, never required.

zoomSpeed.description: Zoom of the topDown preset per unit (exp(delta x zoomSpeed)).

cameras.description: Cameras made (or adopted) at start: [{ name, preset, params, target, adopt: { path, tag }, active, enabled, contexts, outOfContext }]. outOfContext: freeze | stop | end | continue, this camera's own behaviour out of its contexts (absent: the kit's outOfContext). contexts: the contexts of game.engine's stack the camera listens and writes in (a name, a list, or all; absent: default, docs/contextes.md).

shakeProfiles.description: The profiles of shake by name (registry, over the built-in hit, rumble, explosion, field by field): { attack, hold, release (seconds), curve (linear | smooth | exp), frequency (Hz), position [right, up, forward] (metres), rotation [yaw, pitch, roll] (degrees), damping (1/s), falloff { near, far } (metres from the source, the at of shake) or null }. Computed at the render on core.camera's cameras, visual only.

shakeCap.description: The cap of the sum of the shakes running: position (metres) and rotation (degrees), lengths of the vectors.

nativeClass.description: The class of a native camera each engine makes when nothing is adopted.

buttons.description: The button intents in bit order: the config buttons (a game or a mod writes the list), then those the kits add with registerButton.

controlled.description: The entities controlled at start: [{ entity | tag, driver, owner, player }] (owner: the genre kit or the kit that drives). Empty: the game or a genre kit calls control.

priorities.description: The priority of each kind of driver: a different owner takes an entity only with a strictly higher priority.

maxEntities.description: At most how many entities hold intents (one row each; nothing is computed for an entity without a driver).

inputActions.description: The action of core.input of a button whose name differs ({ jump: "jump_alt" }); by default a button reads the action of the same name.

gripforge.kit/core.fx.description: What the kit core.fx adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The genres of effects, by id: built in (explosion, smoke, sparks, impact, flash), registerGenre, the config's genres.<id> over both, field by field.

life.description: Seconds an effect lives, its fade included, unless its genre, its emitter or the call says.

fade.description: Seconds an effect fades out over at the end of its life (opacity from 1 to 0, continuous, computed at the render), unless its genre, its emitter or the call says.

maxEffects.description: At most how many effects live at once; one more makes the oldest leave first (it fades out over evictFade). A genre or an emitter may also have its own `max`.

evictFade.description: Seconds an effect fades out over when the cap or stop makes it leave early; it no longer counts against any maximum from then.

genres.description: The genres of effects over the built-in ones and registerGenre, keyed by id, field by field: { description, tags, life, fade, max, parts: { particles: [props of core.material.particles], decal: { texture, size, color }, light: { intensity, color, range, seconds }, sound: { id, volume }, shake: { profile (a profile of core.camera: hit, rumble, explosion, or the game's), strength, radius (metres, the far end of its falloff), seconds }, tint: { color, intensity, seconds } } }.

emitters.description: What an emitter (who plays the effect) changes, keyed by entity id, then tag, then free key: { life, fade, max, scale, minInterval }. Also set in code: core.fx.emitter(key, settings), over this.

lightTag.description: The tag (the group of a light of core.light) the game puts on the lights core.fx may borrow for a flash. A light is never made: with none free, the flash part is skipped (counter noLight).

triggers.description: Effects played on an event of the bus, as data: [{ on: topic, genre, at: entity | position, opts }]. at: entity plays on the entity the event names, position at its payload's position (else the entity's place).

scene.description: The scene the nodes of the effects are made in; empty: the current scene of game.engine.

seed.description: The seed of the effects: an effect's particles take seed + its handle, so a replayed game gives the same particles.

translations.description: The translation tables by id (a kit, the game or a mod adds or overrides one; declare hands a kit its own table without game.engine).

language.description: The choice when the player made none: auto follows the system language. The player changes it in the settings (core.settings) or the game by setLanguage.

fallback.description: The language of the messages missing in the language in use, and the one shown when the system language is not offered.

languages.description: The languages offered to the player, in this order; empty: every language that has a table.

timeZone.description: The time zone of {d, date} and {d, time}.

strings.description: Texts of the game in code or in project.gripforge, by language: { "fr": { "game": { "title": "Le village" }, "story.quest.journal.title": "Carnet" } }. They go over the kits' own texts and the translations collection.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. config.description: The settings of core.i18n (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

id.description: Document id; the language code when lang is absent (en, fr, de, pt-BR…).

lang.description: Language of the table (BCP 47); default: id.

name.description: Name of the language in itself (Deutsch); default: the CLDR name.

gripforge.kit/core.input.title: core.input in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.input.description: What the kit core.input adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

actions.description: The actions of the game, by name; a mod adds or rebinds one.

contexts.description: The contexts, by name; a mod adds one or maps an action its own way.

actions.description: The actions the game declares: { name, kind: button|axis|vector|position, bindings[], contexts?, hold?, tap?, double?, threshold?, deadzone?, curve?, sensitivity?, invertX?, invertY?, label? }. position: where the pointer is on the screen (bindings MousePosition, Touch<n>Position; centre 0, y up, half the screen height = 1, x -aspect..aspect), read as the host reports it, never a press. contexts: the input contexts it is read in (absent: default; all: every one, read even in a context muted by game.engine's stack, as the debugger's key). Moddable.

contexts.description: The contexts: { name, mode: exclusive|additive|overlay, cursor?, bindings?: { action: [bindings] }, contexts? }. The default context is always there. contexts: the game.engine contexts it is read in (docs/contextes.md: a name, a list, or all); absent: the engine context of its own name when game.engine declares one, else default. With game.engine contexts, an input context named like one on the engine stack is put on and taken off with it.

stack.description: The context stack at start, bottom first.

timings.description: Seconds of a long press, the longest tap, the gap of a double tap; the threshold of an analog control driving a button.

response.description: The analog response of every action (an action's own keys over it).

players.description: How many players and how devices find theirs: shared, join, manual.

remap.description: Rebind conflicts (ask, swap, allow), the controls never taken, and the Controls tab (core.input.remap): the actions it hides (exclude) or the only ones it shows (actions, empty: all), its gamepad and secondary columns.

pointer.description: When the cursor is locked: off, click, play, manual; a context with cursor: true, or a kit's showCursor (a menu open), frees it. In click, a lock held (or taken back by the host) when the cursor is freed is asked again when it is no longer freed (Resume).

events.description: The phases told as core.input.action events (only when someone listens).

language.description: The language of the labels when none is asked (core.i18n for others).

mirrorToEngine.description: Off by default: the actions stay in core.input only. On: the table is also handed to the engine's own input (Godot InputMap, Unity InputActionAsset; Unreal not yet), with the player's rebinds, so the game's native code sees them. Read once at the start.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/core.light.title: core.light in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.light.description: What the kit core.light adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

presets.description: The presets a game may pick, by name; a game or a mod changes one (config presets.<name>).

lights.description: The lights the game declares, made or adopted at start, in order: [{ name, kind, params, adopt: { path, tag }, attach, main, active, enabled, group }]. Empty (the default): the kit lights nothing.

preset.description: The preset applied at start to the lights the game declared (empty: none).

presets.description: The presets a game may pick (proposed, never imposed): each sets the main directional light, the active ambient, sky and fog, and the exposure, on the handles that exist (it makes none). A scene or a mod changes them (moddable, live).

kinds.description: The default params of each kind of light, under what create, adopt and set give. Units: lux for a directional light, lumens for a point or spot light, cd/m² for the ambient light and the sky (1000 is one unit of the former Three.js looks).

exposure.description: The exposure of the frame, a multiplier over the engine's own (1: as the engine).

tonemapping.description: The tone curve of the frame (engine: left as the engine has it).

shadows.description: The shadows of the lights: how far the main light's shadows reach, its cascades and bias, the size of a shadow map, and at most how many lights cast shadows at once (the nearest to the camera keep them).

lights.description: At most how many lights cast shadows on any backend, the main light first (null: what the backend can). Usually set by the player's level of shadows (shadowLevels); the code may set it (setShadows).

shadowLevels.description: What each level of the player's setting core.light.shadows lays over the config shadows (any of its keys); the code (setShadows) has the last word. A level with no line, or an empty line, changes nothing. Without the settings kit, no level: the config alone.

fallback.description: What becomes of the lights a backend does not draw at once. Degraded mode by default (everywhere false): WebGPU and native draw everything; WebGL2 (one directional light, one shadow) keeps the main light's shadows and draws the others without; Unity shadows one directional light, the main one. Unified mode as an option (everywhere true): WebGL2's limits on every backend, the same frame everywhere. A directional light beyond the limit becomes a far lamp without shadow (lamp), is folded into the ambient light (ambient) or is not drawn (off). Each fallback is said once with its reason (core.light.failed, shown by the debugger). Only the first state: the code sets the mode with setFallback.

budget.description: Off by default (null). On: at most maxPoint point lights and maxSpot spot lights draw, the nearest to the camera within activation metres, faded out over fade metres (the web's WebGL2 bounds the lights it draws).

maxLights.description: At most how many handles the kit keeps.

rootNode.description: Where the lights the kit makes go (a path in the game's tree); empty: the current scene.

adoptScene.description: true: every native light of the scenes the game loads is adopted as it enters (a text: only those tagged with it); false (the default): only what the game names.

nativeClass.description: The class of a native light or environment each engine makes when nothing is adopted, by kind then engine.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.light (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

sceneSection.description: What core.light reads on a scene.

element.description: Which element of core.light this section is (ambience when left out).

then.title: Ambience
then.description: The light ambience of a scene: a preset of core.light, the exposure and the tone curve, given back when the scene is left.

element.description: Which element of core.light this section is (ambience when left out).

preset.description: A preset of the config presets (daylight, golden_hour...); empty: none.

exposure.description: A multiplier over the engine's own exposure; 0: left as the preset or the game has it.

tonemapping.description: engine, aces, agx, filmic, neutral or none; empty: left as it is.

seconds.description: The seconds over which the preset and the exposure are reached.

then.description: The light ambience of a scene: a preset of core.light, the exposure and the tone curve, given back when the scene is left.

gripforge.kit/core.locomotion.title: core.locomotion in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.locomotion.description: What the kit core.locomotion adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

modes.description: The movement modes by id (config modes.<id>, registerMode): a kit adds its own (climb, mount), a game or a mod changes one.

profiles.description: The movement profiles by name (config profiles.<name>): a player, a heavy NPC, a small animal.

Movement profiles by name: walkSpeed, runSpeed, defaultGait (walk|run), acceleration, deceleration, turnRate, pivotAngle, turnKeepSpeed, turnSmoothing, faceMovement, the feel of a turn (turnGrip m/s² held sideways, pivotSpeed m/s under which the body pivots on its feet, pivotTurnRate rad/s, pivotAligned rad, pivotCreep m/s, stillSpeed m/s, pivotHysteresis rad, pivotBrake × deceleration, faceSmoothing s), turnSpeed, jumpImpulse, gravity, airJumps, airJumpImpulse, crouch, crouchSpeed, crouchHeight, and the platform helps coyoteTime (s), jumpBuffer (s), jumpCut (0..1, 1: no cut), wallJump, wallJumpSpeed, wallJumpImpulse (all off by default). The preset profile platform (every help on, a double jump) is registered by the kit under the game's: take it with movers[].profile or setProfile, change it with profiles.platform. Today's character settings, moved as they are (turnSpeed, radians per second at a full control.turn, is new: it is what turns the body under A / D). default is the fallback of every profile; a genre kit registers its own (registerProfile), the game's config stays over it value by value.

modes.description: The movement modes by id over the built-in ones (the registry of the former controller kits, copied with provenance: walk always on; fly, swim, glide, space; climb, ledge, slide, mount, parachute, dash, grapple, grind, held for kits): enabled, speed, runSpeed, gravity, accel, drag, vertical, verticalSpeed, buoyancy, maxFall, jump, surface, enter / exit triggers (air, ground, action:<button intent of core.control>, volume:<tag>), driver. A genre kit or a game overrides a mode field by field; a custom mode is a new id. No clip names: the mode publishes the states <mode> and <mode>.move. The base modes climb, ledge, slide and dash are driven by the laws with a behavior, off until enabled; their tuning numbers (modeInfo(id).tune) are set here too, e.g. {"climb": {"enabled": true, "minSlope": 50, "cost": 6}}. driver: "kit" hands a mode to a kit of the game instead. features: { <function>: { <field>: value } } composes a mode from the functions of the registry (grab: delay, regrabDelay, group; transition: to, time, pastMargin, maxTimeFactor; see features() and featureInfo(name)), field by field over its own.

facing.description: What the body faces: movement (where it goes), intent (control.wanted_dir, e.g. the camera through a binding), free (only face / teleport turn it). A profile or setFacing changes it per entity.

movers.description: The entities moved at start: [{ entity | tag, profile, bodyNode, originOffset }]. Empty: the game calls add.

capsule.description: The capsule made when the game gives no body (bodyNode): radius and height in metres.

states.description: How the body action state is chosen from the movement: stillSpeed (below: idle), fallSpeed (falling faster: fall, not jump.loop), ledgeGrace (seconds off a ledge before leaving the ground state). The variants (hard landing, running jump) are rows of the animation table, not states.

stamina.description: The stamina reserve every base mode spends from (climb, its jump, a dash with a cost): max, regen (points per second), regenDelay (seconds without spending before it refills), recover (share of max to refill before an exhausted body may spend again). Per entity, in place in locomotion.stamina@1.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.locomotion (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

speedScale.description: A factor of the speeds of the intents: each kit lays its own (game.engine.contributions.contribute(entity, "speedScale", 1.2, { by, reason })), they multiply; withdrawn, the others stay.

accelScale.description: A factor of the accelerations, laid like speedScale.

gravityScale.description: The gravity scale of the entity: the factor of its mode (laid by core.locomotion) times every kit's (a low-gravity zone): game.engine.contributions.contribute(entity, "gravityScale", 0.5, { by, reason }).

speedCap.description: A cap of the horizontal speed (m/s): every kit lays its own, the smallest holds; none laid: no cap.

blocked.description: The movement is blocked while any kit blocks it (game.engine.contributions.contribute(entity, "blocked", true, { by, ticks })): no wanted move, no jump, no dash.

gripforge.kit/core.material.title: core.material in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.material.description: What the kit core.material adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

presets.description: The presets a game may pick, by name; a game or a mod changes one (config presets.<name>).

intents.description: The declared render intentions, by id: the kit's defaults (core.material.hit_flash), then data (renderIntents), then config intents.<id>; a later one replaces an earlier one, null removes it. Played by name (playIntent) or started by their condition (when).

materials.description: The materials the game declares, made or adopted at start, in order: [{ name, kind, params, adopt: { path, tag, surface }, target, group }]. Empty (the default): the kit makes and adopts nothing.

presets.description: The presets a game may pick (proposed, never imposed): each is a material in the fields of the contract (color, metallic, roughness, emissive, emissiveStrength, alphaMode, alphaCutoff, unlit, doubleSided, uvRepeat, texture), with opacity. A scene or a mod changes them (moddable, live).

instanceMode.description: How an object gets its own instance of a material: native, the engine's own per object way (Godot instance shader parameters, Unity MaterialPropertyBlock, Unreal MaterialInstanceDynamic, Bevy a copy of the asset made once); copy, a copy of the material everywhere.

maxHandles.description: At most how many handles (materials and instances) the kit keeps.

surfaces.description: The surfaces and the behaviours they have (catalogue of surface behaviours, provisional names): { <tag, material or region name>: { region?: { shape: everywhere|rect|disc|path, min/max | center/radius | points/width }, <genre>: { parameters } } }. A surface named by a tag or a material is an OBJECT (the entities that carry the tag, or whose material has that name, take it, as adoptAll takes by tag); one with a region is a REGION (a footprint, no mesh: a lake; its level, waves and flow are parameters of the genre, as the fluid genre of FluidDesc). A genre is what a kit registered (registerSurfaceBehavior); a declaration for a genre not registered yet waits for it. The parameters are given over the defaults of the genre. Empty (the default): no surface.

intents.description: The game's own declared render intentions by id, over the project's collection renderIntents and the kit's defaults (a whole declaration replaces the one of that id; null removes it): { <id>: { params, tracks, loop, mode, layer, priority, weight, when } }, the form of a document of renderIntents (README « Les intentions déclarées »). A scene or a mod changes them (moddable).

nativeClass.description: The class of a native material each engine makes for a kind, by kind then engine (a custom material is the class of the shader the kit that owns it names).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.material (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

nodeSection.description: What core.material reads on a node.

element.description: Which element of core.material this section is (sprite when left out).

then.title: Sprite
then.description: A sprite node, child of the node it marks (as a Sprite3D or a Label3D in an engine): an image, a text or a bar on a quad that faces the camera, posed by each engine's own way (Godot Sprite3D / Label3D, Unity SpriteRenderer / TextMesh, Unreal billboard and text render components, Bevy and the players a camera-facing quad of core.material). Bound to a value of the business state of its parent entity (bind: a health bar, a name, a counter), shown again only when that value changes; the render side changes a material parameter, never a mesh.

element.description: Which element of core.material this section is (sprite when left out).

kind.description: image (the asset image), text (text, or the bound value through format) or bar (fill = the bound value / max, from 0 to 1).

image.description: The IDENTIFIER of the image asset (resolved by asset.meta when it is loaded), never a path; empty: a plain quad of color.

text.description: The text shown by a text sprite without bind.

bind.description: The key of the business state of the parent entity whose value is shown (hp, name…); empty: none.

format.description: The text of a bound text sprite: {value} is the bound value, {max} the max.

max.description: The value of a full bar (fill = value / max, from 0 to 1).

size.description: [width, height]: metres (sizeMode world) or pixels on the screen (sizeMode screen).

sizeMode.description: world: a size in metres, smaller far away; screen: a size in pixels, the same at every distance.

face.description: camera: always faces the camera; axis: turns about +Y only; fixed: the orientation of the node.

offset.description: A shift from the node's place, metres (local to the parent entity when there is one: above a head).

color.description: The colour of the image, the text or the bar (#rrggbb or #rrggbbaa).

back.description: The colour of the back of a bar.

colors.description: The gradient of a bar [[threshold, colour], …]: the colour of the highest threshold the fill reaches (0..1); null: color.

occlude.description: true: hidden behind the walls (depth test); false: always seen.

then.title: Sprite
then.description: A sprite node, child of the node it marks (as a Sprite3D or a Label3D in an engine): an image, a text or a bar on a quad that faces the camera, posed by each engine's own way (Godot Sprite3D / Label3D, Unity SpriteRenderer / TextMesh, Unreal billboard and text render components, Bevy and the players a camera-facing quad of core.material). Bound to a value of the business state of its parent entity (bind: a health bar, a name, a counter), shown again only when that value changes; the render side changes a material parameter, never a mesh.

Bound to a value of the business state of its parent entity (bind: a health bar, a name, a counter), shown again only when that value changes; the render side changes a material parameter, never a mesh.

gripforge.kit/core.net.title: core.net in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.net.description: What the kit core.net adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

link.description: The link: auto picks UDP natively, WebTransport then WebSocket in a browser; memory joins endpoints of the same process (tests).

host.description: Server: the host name told to clients in the endpoints (publicHost of listen overrides it).

port.description: Server: the one port number, UDP (raw protocol and WebTransport) and TCP (WebSocket); 0 picks a free one.

path.description: Path of the WebTransport session and of the WebSocket upgrade.

listenWebSocket.description: Server: serve the WebSocket fallback on TCP.

listenWebTransport.description: Server: serve WebTransport on the UDP port (a self-signed certificate of 10 days when none is given).

ticketKey.description: Server: the 32-byte key (base64url) shared with the room service that opens the tickets. Never in a client.

matchId.description: Server: the match a ticket must name (empty: any).

anonymous.description: Server: accept hellos without ticket (dev and tests only; nothing sealed).

maxPendingHandshakes.description: Server: hellos waiting for the game's answer (0: maxPeers × 4 + 16).

heartbeatMs.description: Client ping period (clock and round trip); every side sends at least one packet each 250 ms or this, whichever is shorter.

timeoutMs.description: Silence before the other side is lost.

handshakeMs.description: Server: a hello not answered by then is dropped.

connectTimeoutMs.description: Client: time a link has to answer before the next one is tried (and before the connect fails).

resumeMs.description: A lost peer keeps its seat and its reliable streams this long for a resume; 0: no resume.

maxMessageBytes.description: Largest message; above the datagram size it is fragmented on a reliable path.

unreliableTtlMs.description: An unreliable message that could not leave by then is dropped (counted).

bytesPerSecond.description: Byte budget per second towards each peer; the packet is filled by priority (late reliable first, then the channels' priority accumulator).

bytesBurst.description: Bytes the budget holds when idle.

enabled.description: Resume by itself after a loss.

jitter.description: Each delay times a draw in [1 - jitter, 1 + jitter].

from.description: Who may send on it: server (a message a client sent is refused, from_server_only), seat (a client sends for its own seat only, the seat being the one core.net knows for the peer; refused from a peer without a seat, no_seat), any. Checked by the server; refusals counted and shown by debugNet.

channels.description: Channels declared in data (id prefixed by the kit or the game); a kit may declare its own by channel().

statuses.description: Statuses the game adds to offline, online, in_room, in_match.

sim.description: core.net.sim: the bad network on the way out, for tests and test rooms; never on by default.

pumpMs.description: Server: time the WebTransport side may take per pass (0: a quick pass).

httpTimeoutMs.description: Server: an HTTP head (WebSocket upgrade) must arrive by then.

maxPendingConnections.description: Server: TCP connections before their HTTP head, in total.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.net (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.physics.title: core.physics in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.physics.description: What the kit core.physics adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

materials.description: Named physical materials { friction, restitution, footstep } (config materials.<name>); a body takes one by name.

layers.description: Named collision layers in bit order (config layers); layerMask gives their mask.

archetypes.description: The collision of each archetype for the collision nodes (config archetypes.<archetype>): what every node or entity of that archetype gets unless it says otherwise.

watchKinds.description: The watch kinds of the game or of a mod (config watchKinds.<kind>): a base (around, contact, traverse, stay, sight) and its defaults.

supportKinds.description: Presets of support nodes (config supportKinds.<kind>): strength, fall, impulse, breakWhen, anchor; a node of that kind takes them.

fieldKinds.description: The field kinds of the game or of a mod (config fieldKinds.<kind>): a base (uniform, point, magnet, wind, vortex, custom) and its defaults.

interactions.description: Who interacts with whom, by a tag of the element (config interactions.<tag>): only, ignore.

outOfContext.description: What the physics world does while the context on top of game.engine's stack is not one of its contexts (docs/hors-contexte.md): a behaviour (freeze: the host stops stepping it, every body keeps its place and its speed, the default; stop: frozen, and every body at rest when it comes back; continue; end: read as stop), or { behavior, contexts } (absent: default). The world is the default of its bodies; `bodies` { entity: behaviour | { contexts, outOfContext } } gives a body its own rule (each body decides alone, held by the physics one by one). Nothing without game.engine.

character.description: Defaults of the character controller (a character created with explicit options keeps them).

snapDistance.description: Ground snapping distance (m) when walking down slopes and steps.

skinRatio.description: Gap the controller keeps from what it touches, as a fraction of the capsule radius (at least 1 cm); 0.05 keeps the fixed 5 cm gap of the Rapier controller.

originOffset.description: The first offset of every character (m), from the origin of the followed object to the point the service takes and gives: absent, 0 (the origin as it is, on every engine). A game changes one live with setCharacterOffset; a value it computed is one it writes.

maxContactsPerBody.description: Contact events reported per body per step (contactEvents); the first ones are kept.

maxOverlapResults.description: Results of one overlap query (pollFound); the first ones are kept.

gravity.description: The gravity of the world [x, y, z] (m/s²), declared: set at the start of the game, changed by the game's config or a mod (the hook core.physics.step asked at each tick is gone, #655); setGravity changes it while the game runs.

defaultMass.description: Mass (kg) of a dynamic body created without one.

fluidLevel.description: PROVISIONAL name: a flat fluid of water everywhere at this height (m), the fallback the floating bodies (buoyancy) float on when no fluid source is given. Absent: no fluid, nothing floats, nothing costs.

materials.description: The registry of named physical materials (one for the whole game: world.ground and footstep sounds read it): { <name>: { friction, restitution, footstep } }. A body described with material: <name> takes its friction and restitution. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

layers.description: The registry of named collision layers, in bit order (at most 32); layerMask(names) gives the mask the query filters take.

archetypes.description: The collision of the archetypes, for the collision nodes (scene element core.physics.collision): { <archetype>: { shape, type, size, radius, height, mass, material, layers, collidesWith, asset, heights, joint } }, the same fields as a collision node. A collision node's field left neutral (empty, 0, [0,0,0], null) takes its archetype's (its parent's game.engine archetype). An entity of game.engine whose archetype is here gets its body when it spawns (heard only when this registry is not empty). A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

watches.description: The watches the game declares (docs/design/core-physics-surveillances.md): [{ id, kind, element, at, yaw, radius, height, range, angle, lineOfSight, eye, size, direction, seconds, mode, minForce, once, cooldown, topic, tags, notTags, kinds, layers, group }], the same spec as addWatch(spec). Nothing runs for a watch until one of its signals has an audience. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

watchKinds.description: The registry of watch kinds beyond the five bases (around, contact, traverse, stay, sight): { <kind>: { base, ...defaults of any field of a watch } }; a watch of that kind takes these defaults, its own fields win. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

fields.description: The fields of gravity and force the game declares (docs/design/core-physics-champs.md): [{ id, kind, base, volume, at, on, priority, blend, enabled, lifetime, topic, tags, notTags, kinds, layers, group, ...the fields of its base }], the same spec as addField(spec). Moddable.

fieldKinds.description: The registry of field kinds beyond the six bases (uniform, point, magnet, wind, vortex, custom): { <kind>: { base, ...defaults of any field of a field } }; a field of that kind takes these defaults, its own fields win. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable): a law of its own is a kind of base custom whose value the hook core.physics.field.apply gives.

interactions.description: Who interacts with whom, by a tag (or the group of a watch) of the element: { <tag>: { only: [tags], ignore: [tags] } }. Read by every watch, search, focus and use whose element bears the tag: only lets through only the others with one of its tags, ignore stops the others with one of its tags; noPush: the others with one of its tags cannot push the element (pickUp, canPush). Which pairs push each other stays the layers of the bodies (layers, collidesWith). A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

bodyStates.description: Physical properties bound to a state of game.engine, as the rendering is (docs/design/rendu-par-etat.md): [{ tags?, entity?, when: { <state>: value }, set: { mass, friction, restitution, linearDamping, angularDamping, gravityScale, kind } }]; while the state of the entity matches when, its body takes set (the rules that hold, in order); out of it, the body gets its own back. game.engine.state.changed is heard only when the list is not empty. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

detachStates.description: Parts detached by a state of game.engine: [{ tags?, entity?, when: { <state>: value }, part: { ...spec of detachPart } }]; when the state of the entity comes to match when, the part is detached, once per entity and part. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

pieceLife.description: Seconds a detached piece lives before it fades, when its emitter says nothing (setPieceLife, pieceLives); below 0: pieces stay.

pieceFade.description: Seconds a detached piece takes to fade out (opacity down to 0, continuously) before it goes, when its emitter says nothing.

piecesMax.description: Detached pieces kept at most: over it, the oldest starts its fade first (never removed at once).

pieceLives.description: The life of the pieces per emitter, in data: [{ tags?, entity?, life?, fade? }]; the first rule that names the entity a piece comes from wins (setPieceLife in code wins over it). A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

supports.description: Support graphs (docs/design/core-physics-surveillances.md, « Le graphe de soutien »): [{ id, strength? (N·s, the default of its links), nodes: { <name>: { kind? (a preset of supportKinds), entity? (an entity or a game.engine instance), body? (a body id, else the entity's), part? (a spec of detachPart: the node is that part of the entity), anchor? (held by the ground), strength? (N·s: a hit that hard breaks the node), breakWhen? ({ <state>: value } of game.engine), fall? (dynamic | detach | remove | none; detach for a part, dynamic otherwise), impulse? ([x, y, z] N·s when it falls as a body) } }, links: [{ id?, a, b (a rests on b; b may be ground, which always stands), strength? (N·s), joint? ({ kind: fixed, … } as addJoint, between two bodies; anchors not given keep them where they are) }] }]. When a node or a link breaks, what no longer rests on an anchor falls, once. Nothing runs while nothing breaks. A game or a mod adds or changes one (moddable).

supportKinds.description: Presets of support nodes (a registry): { <kind>: { strength, fall, impulse, breakWhen, anchor } }; a node kind: <kind> takes them, its own fields win (a brick, a glass pane).

carry.description: Carrying a body (pickUp, putDown, launch): offset [x, y, z] where it is held in the holder's frame (+Z forward), throwSpeed (m/s along the heading), lift (m/s upward when launched), maxMass (kg, heavier bodies are not picked up).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.physics (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

nodeSection.description: What core.physics reads on a node.

element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (collider when left out).

then.title: Fixed collider
then.description: A fixed collider at the node's resolved place (a wall, a floor, a crate that never moves), its size times the node's scale.

element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (collider when left out).

size.description: The full size of a box, metres.

radius.description: The radius of a sphere or a capsule, metres.

height.description: The total height of a capsule, metres.

material.description: A physical material of the registry (friction, restitution, footstep); empty: default.

then.title: Fixed collider
then.description: A fixed collider at the node's resolved place (a wall, a floor, a crate that never moves), its size times the node's scale.

element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (collider when left out).

size.description: The full size of a box, metres.

radius.description: The radius of a sphere or a capsule, metres.

height.description: The total height of a capsule, metres.

material.description: A physical material of the registry (friction, restitution, footstep); empty: default.

then.title: Collision
then.description: A collision node, child of the node it makes collide (as a collision shape in an engine): every collision child of a node makes one body, a compound of their shapes at their places; the body is the parent's game.engine entity when it has one (a kinematic one follows its pose), else a body of its own (a group without model nor entity: an invisible wall). A field left neutral (empty, 0, [0,0,0], null) takes the one of the archetype (config archetypes.<archetype>), else the kit's default.

element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (collider when left out).

shape.description: box, sphere, capsule, cylinder (radius, height, along +Y), cone (radius of its base at -height/2, apex at +height/2), triangle (points: 3 points), wedge (a ramp: size, its floor x by z, its slope rising from -Z to +Z up to y), pyramid (size, apex at the top), tetrahedron (size, apex at the top), hull (points: 4 or more; none: the parts of the asset's passport, as mesh), plane (normal, an endless fixed ground, type static only), mesh (the collision parts of the asset's passport, through asset.meta) or heightmap (a fixed ground of the grid heights, type static only, the one collision node of its parent); each alone or with the other collision nodes of its parent in one compound; empty: the archetype's, else box (any other value is refused).

type.description: static, kinematic (follows its parent entity), dynamic or sensor (a trigger volume that tells who enters and leaves, a body of its own); empty: the archetype's, else static (any other value is refused). The body takes the type of its first collision node.

size.description: The full size of a box, a wedge, a pyramid or a tetrahedron, metres, times the node's scale (a heightmap: its scale [x, y, z], 1 = as given); [0,0,0]: the archetype's, else 1 m.

radius.description: The radius of a sphere, a capsule, a cylinder or a cone (its base), metres, times the node's largest scale; 0: the archetype's, else 0.5.

height.description: The total height of a capsule, a cylinder or a cone, metres, times the node's largest scale; 0: the archetype's, else 1.

border.description: The radius a box, a cylinder, a cone, a wedge, a pyramid or a tetrahedron is rounded by, inside its size (a hull and a triangle: added around them), metres, times the node's largest scale; 0: the archetype's, else sharp.

points.description: The points [[x, y, z], ...] of a triangle (3) or a hull (4 or more), in the node's frame, times its scale per axis; null: the archetype's (a hull without points: the parts of its asset's passport).

normal.description: The normal [x, y, z] of a plane in the node's frame, solid under it; null: the archetype's, else up [0, 1, 0].

mass.description: Its share of the mass of a dynamic body, kg (the body's is the sum); 0: the archetype's, else config defaultMass for the body.

material.description: A physical material of the registry; empty: the archetype's, else default.

layers.description: The collision layers the body is on (names of config layers); null: the archetype's, else the first.

collidesWith.description: The layers the body collides with (names); null: the archetype's, else all.

asset.description: The asset whose passport gives a mesh; empty: the parent's model, else its archetype's.

heights.description: The grid of a heightmap, the form of world.terrain's relief.grid: { n (cells a side), size (metres), centre [x, z] (optional, in the node's frame), heights ((n + 1)² metres, row by row along +X then +Z) }, centred on the node; null: the archetype's.

joint.description: Optional joint of the body { kind: hinge|ball|fixed|slider|spring|cone, anchor [x,y,z] and axis [x,y,z] in this node's frame, limits [low, high] (hinge: degrees, slider: metres), swing, twistMin, twistMax (cone: degrees; the twist of this node's body about +axis), to (another body's entity; empty: the world, a fixed anchor made and removed with the body), stiffness, damping, restLength, collide }; null: the archetype's, else none.

then.title: Watch
then.description: A watch node, child of the node it watches (docs/design/core-physics-surveillances.md), several per node: the parent's game.engine entity when it has one, else the watch node's place and heading; its signals core.physics.watch.* (entered, left, touched, released, crossed, stayed) are ready for the bindings of the scene. Nothing runs until one of them has an audience.

element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (collider when left out).

kind.description: around, contact, traverse, stay, sight, or a kind of the registry watchKinds.

radius.description: around, stay: the radius, metres.

lineOfSight.description: sight: something in the way hides.

seconds.description: stay: how long inside before stayed.

cooldown.description: Seconds between two signals for a same other.

topic.description: A prefix of the game: the signals are also told on <topic>.<signal> (room.door.entered), a binding plugs into it as is.

tags.description: The other bears one of these tags.

notTags.description: The other bears none of these tags.

then.title: Field
then.description: A field of gravity or force (docs/design/core-physics-champs.md), child of the node that carries it: the parent's game.engine entity carries it (on), else it stands at the node's place. Its volume is detected by an internal watch.

element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (collider when left out).

kind.description: uniform, point, magnet, wind, vortex, custom, or a kind of the registry fieldKinds.

strength.description: uniform, point: m/s² (0: weightlessness); magnet: N at 1 m (negative pushes).

priority.description: The higher gravity wins where several hold.

then.description: The physics of a scene: its gravity, given back to the declared one (config gravity) when the scene is left.
