element.description: Which element of core.physics this section is (world when left out).

collision.title: Collision
collision.description: A collision node, child of the node it makes collide (as a collision shape in an engine): every collision child of a node makes one body, a compound of their shapes at their places; the body is the parent's game.engine entity when it has one (a kinematic one follows its pose), else a body of its own (a group without model nor entity: an invisible wall). A field left neutral (empty, 0, [0,0,0], null) takes the one of the archetype (config archetypes.<archetype>), else the kit's default.

shape.description: box, sphere, capsule, cylinder (radius, height, along +Y), cone (radius of its base at -height/2, apex at +height/2), triangle (points: 3 points), wedge (a ramp: size, its floor x by z, its slope rising from -Z to +Z up to y), pyramid (size, apex at the top), tetrahedron (size, apex at the top), hull (points: 4 or more; none: the parts of the asset's passport, as mesh), plane (normal, an endless fixed ground, type static only), mesh (the collision parts of the asset's passport, through asset.meta) or heightmap (a fixed ground of the grid heights, type static only, the one collision node of its parent); each alone or with the other collision nodes of its parent in one compound; empty: the archetype's, else box (any other value is refused).

type.description: static, kinematic (follows its parent entity), dynamic or sensor (a trigger volume that tells who enters and leaves, a body of its own); empty: the archetype's, else static (any other value is refused). The body takes the type of its first collision node.

size.description: The full size of a box, a wedge, a pyramid or a tetrahedron, metres, times the node's scale (a heightmap: its scale [x, y, z], 1 = as given); [0,0,0]: the archetype's, else 1 m.

radius.description: The radius of a sphere, a capsule, a cylinder or a cone (its base), metres, times the node's largest scale; 0: the archetype's, else 0.5.

height.description: The total height of a capsule, a cylinder or a cone, metres, times the node's largest scale; 0: the archetype's, else 1.

border.description: The radius a box, a cylinder, a cone, a wedge, a pyramid or a tetrahedron is rounded by, inside its size (a hull and a triangle: added around them), metres, times the node's largest scale; 0: the archetype's, else sharp.

points.description: The points [[x, y, z], ...] of a triangle (3) or a hull (4 or more), in the node's frame, times its scale per axis; null: the archetype's (a hull without points: the parts of its asset's passport).

normal.description: The normal [x, y, z] of a plane in the node's frame, solid under it; null: the archetype's, else up [0, 1, 0].

mass.description: Its share of the mass of a dynamic body, kg (the body's is the sum); 0: the archetype's, else config defaultMass for the body.

material.description: A physical material of the registry; empty: the archetype's, else default.

layers.description: The collision layers the body is on (names of config layers); null: the archetype's, else the first.

collidesWith.description: The layers the body collides with (names); null: the archetype's, else all.

asset.description: The asset whose passport gives a mesh; empty: the parent's model, else its archetype's.

heights.description: The grid of a heightmap, the form of world.terrain's relief.grid: { n (cells a side), size (metres), centre [x, z] (optional, in the node's frame), heights ((n + 1)² metres, row by row along +X then +Z) }, centred on the node; null: the archetype's.

joint.description: Optional joint of the body { kind: hinge|ball|fixed|slider|spring|cone, anchor [x,y,z] and axis [x,y,z] in this node's frame, limits [low, high] (hinge: degrees, slider: metres), swing, twistMin, twistMax (cone: degrees; the twist of this node's body about +axis), to (another body's entity; empty: the world, a fixed anchor made and removed with the body), stiffness, damping, restLength, collide }; null: the archetype's, else none.

watch.title: Watch
watch.description: A watch node, child of the node it watches (docs/design/core-physics-surveillances.md), several per node: the parent's game.engine entity when it has one, else the watch node's place and heading; its signals core.physics.watch.* (entered, left, touched, released, crossed, stayed) are ready for the bindings of the scene. Nothing runs until one of them has an audience.

kind.description: around, contact, traverse, stay, sight, or a kind of the registry watchKinds.

radius.description: around, stay: the radius, metres.

lineOfSight.description: sight: something in the way hides.

seconds.description: stay: how long inside before stayed.

cooldown.description: Seconds between two signals for a same other.

topic.description: A prefix of the game: the signals are also told on <topic>.<signal> (room.door.entered), a binding plugs into it as is.

tags.description: The other bears one of these tags.

notTags.description: The other bears none of these tags.

field.title: Field
field.description: A field of gravity or force (docs/design/core-physics-champs.md), child of the node that carries it: the parent's game.engine entity carries it (on), else it stands at the node's place. Its volume is detected by an internal watch.

kind.description: uniform, point, magnet, wind, vortex, custom, or a kind of the registry fieldKinds.

strength.description: uniform, point: m/s² (0: weightlessness); magnet: N at 1 m (negative pushes).

priority.description: The higher gravity wins where several hold.

held.description: The body is held: fixed and solid for the others, its speeds kept aside (out of context). Written in play by contributions (core.physics.hold), applied by core.physics only; carried wins.

carried.description: The body is carried: out of the world, no contact, no query (a vehicle's seat). Written in play by contributions (core.physics.hold), applied by core.physics only; wins over held.

restOnRelease.description: Let go, the body starts from rest (a stop out of context). Laid for one tick by the kit that lets go.

gripforge.kit/core.player_ai.title: core.player_ai in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.player_ai.description: What the kit core.player_ai adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

playbooks.description: The playbooks (player_ai.*): shipped with the kit, then the game's config, then the project's data collection `playbooks` (a mod), then code (registerPlaybook); a later one of the same id wins, `extends` lays one over another.

players.description: The player AIs: [{ seat, team, squad: [entity | #tag…], playbook: <id> | <playbook>, difficulty: easy | normal | hard | { aggression, accuracy, reaction }, params: { … }, every (seconds between two thoughts; the playbook's, else 1), standIn: { peer | player, brain, active } (held for a human: the AI comes in on core.net.peer.left, goes out on peer.joined) }].

playbooks.description: The game's playbooks by id, over the shipped ones (player_ai.skirmish, player_ai.moba, player_ai.rts, player_ai.racer, player_ai.coop): { extends, every, params, difficulty: { <preset>: { aggression, accuracy, reaction } }, vars: { <name>: { from, pick: first | nearest | farthest | random, near, keep: while_alive | always | never } }, counts: { <name>: <#tag | ids | { from, near, within }> }, orders: { <kind>: <core.ai order in data> } (given to core.ai only when no one declared the kind), cases: [{ id, if: <condition of game.engine; roots team.*, vars.*; $param>, assign: [{ who: all | rest | { count, pick, near, tags, if, keep }, order: <kind> | <spec> | [alternatives…], params }] }] }.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.player_ai (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.render.title: core.render in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.render.description: What the kit core.render adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

interpolate.description: The global default of `interpolate` (props.interpolate of an archetype or an instance wins): read at the render tick, told to the player only for an instance that differs. Moved as it was from the config of game.engine (to rename: Q8 of docs/design/core-render.md).

auto.description: The automatic placement of the models by kind: true | false | { enabled?, kinds?: { kind: mode | null } } (present/src/size.rs `Auto`). Moved as it was from the config of game.engine.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.render (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.settings.title: core.settings in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.settings.description: What the kit core.settings adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The behaviours of a domain over a group's final values (the caps of the machine for graphics, brought by settings.graphics), by name: the method <kit>.<method> of the kit that owns the domain, given in the config key genres (a game or a mod) or registered at run time (registerGenre), named by the group in data (genre, given with the group's presets). core.settings knows no domain: no base entry.

editors.description: The genres of editor a derived kit (settings.*) gives the menu for a structured value (the key capture of settings.input), by name: the method <kit>.<method> that takes the setting, given in the config key editors or registered with registerEditor, named by a setting (editor).

folder.description: Reserved for a host without its own store (a file <folder>/settings.json): the kit module writes to the host's store (save) and does not read it yet.

presets.description: The preset a game starts a group on, by group (over the group's default and under the first-launch rules).

lang.description: The language of the menu's labels; when the game gives none, the platform's language.

patches.description: What the game changes in the declarations, by target (a setting id, group:<id>, category:<group>.<id>): presets (mode → value tables, of any kit), default, bounds, choices, labels, order, category, visibility (hidden: out of the menu; game: imposed by the game, its default wins over modes and the player's file; player: shown); for a group, the list of its modes and its default. A mod does the same.

context.description: The context of game.engine's stack the settings screen pushes when it opens (declared first with game.engine.contexts.create) and pops when it closes. Without game.engine nothing is pushed.

launch.description: Values given at launch, each <kit>.<setting>=<value> (the value read as JSON, else as a word): the page hands the address's ?set= entries here, a gateway its command line. Only a declared setting not imposed by the game is taken, as an override over the player's value for this run, never saved; every refusal is said (log, debugView).

launchSet.description: Whether the values given at launch (launch, ?set=) are taken; the game turns them off with false (each is then refused, with its reason).

genres.description: The genres of the domains (registry genres), by name: the method <kit>.<method> that adjusts the final values of the groups naming it ({ "<name>": "<kit>.<method>" } or { "<name>": { call } }, or a list of { id, call }). Asked (facts, values) and answers { values?, notes? }. A kit registers its own with registerGenre, over these.

editors.description: The genres of editor (registry editors), by name: the method <kit>.<method> that takes a setting naming it ({ id, editor, value }), as genres. Without one, edit emits core.settings.edit_requested. A derived kit registers its own with registerEditor, over these.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.settings (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.shader.title: core.shader in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.shader.description: What the kit core.shader adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

enabled.description: Off: nothing is drawn nor played for a precompilation (precompile answers 0); the count of what builds is still told.

drawFrames.description: Frames an adapter keeps an element of a precompilation drawn under the loading screen, so the engine builds its pipelines and shaders before the game shows it; 0: nothing is drawn (engine collections are still played).

concurrency.description: Elements of the precompilations an adapter draws or plays at once (takeNext): fewer keeps each frame light.

perFrame.description: Unity: shader variants or graphics states warmed up per frame (WarmUpProgressively); the other engines ignore it.

collections.description: The engine's own collections played at start: Unity GraphicsStateCollection or ShaderVariantCollection (path of the asset), Unreal pipeline cache (its name); the other engines ignore them.

cache.description: Use the engine's own cache of compiled shaders and pipelines (read, checked, saved where the engine lets it); off: the adapter does not open nor save it.

batch.description: Unreal: how fast the pipeline cache precompiles (FShaderPipelineCache batch mode); auto: fast while a precompilation or a burst is under way, background otherwise.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.shader (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

path.description: A file of the game to draw once (a model, a scene) or the path of an engine collection.

kind.description: What the adapter does with it: draw a file or a scene, play a collection. Absent = file.

remove.description: True: out of what is precompiled at start.

gripforge.kit/core.weapon.title: core.weapon in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.weapon.description: What the kit core.weapon adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

weapons.description: The weapons { id, kind, ...fields } over their genre chain; the game or a mod adds or overrides one, define does it at run time.

weaponKinds.description: The weapon kinds (genres) a weapon names; the game or a mod adds or overrides one.

tracks.description: The baked tracks of a socket for a clip; defineTrack does it at run time.

weapons.description: The weapons of the game: [{ id, kind, damage, fire, magazine, reload, spread, recoil, range, pellets, groupPellets, pierce, muzzle, projectile, thrown, area, anim, life, fade }] (docs/design/core-weapon.md § 4). Each field has its default (the genre's, else the kit's).

weaponKinds.description: Genres the game adds or changes: { name: { base: <base or genre>, …defaults } }. A shipped genre given again is merged field by field. Bases: hitscan, projectile, thrown, melee, unarmed, beam, custom.

equip.description: Weapons put in hands at the start: [{ holder (player, an id, { tag }), weapon, ammo?, reserve? }].

hudHolder.description: The holder whose hand the HUD view (core.weapon.hud.view) shows: player, an entity id, or { tag }. The kit hears no action of core.input: the game binds its actions to trigger, aim, reload, nextMode.

autoReload.description: An empty magazine starts a reload by itself.

maxProjectiles.description: The projectiles in flight or planted at most; the oldest goes first.

maxThrown.description: The thrown bodies under way at most; the oldest is spent first.

seed.description: The seed of the spreads; null: the project's seed.

tracks.description: The baked tracks of the sockets for the strikes' clips: { clip: { socket: { dt, frames: [[px, py, pz, qx, qy, qz, qw], …] } } } (the socket's place and turn in the holder's frame, written by tools/weapon-tracks from the model). Without a track, a strike sweeps its fixed arc (melee.sweep).

subSteps.description: The places of the iron asked per tick of an active strike (at least 1, at most 16).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.weapon (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/core.webui.title: core.webui in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/core.webui.description: What the kit core.webui adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

fragments.description: The HUD fragments: the game declares its own, each presentation module its kit (declareFragments, kept when the mods policy of game.engine allows it); a mod adds or overrides one.

page.description: Folder of the BUILT page (index.html): web = URL relative to the game page, Godot = res://<page>, Unity = StreamingAssets/<page>, Unreal = Content/<page>.

namespace.description: Namespace of the page globals; must match jsNamespace of gf-webui.js.

devPort.description: devws: WebSocket port the engine listens on (the page runs in a browser next to the game).

devUrl.description: Load this URL (a dev server) instead of the built page.

rebuildOnRun.description: Engines: run the page build (incremental) when the game starts from the editor / before Play / on compile.

autoState.description: Push the GameState variables to the page when they change (rare values; per-frame values go in frames).

stateHz.description: At most this many automatic state pushes per second.

forwardEvents.description: Bus topics (patterns like mission.*) forwarded to the page as events.

mount.description: Web: load the page into the document above the game canvas (false = service only).

kit.description: The kit the fragment belongs to.

ui.description: File of the package: ui.mjs (components and/or templates) or a .html template.

views.description: Views of the module given to the fragment.

vars.description: State vars given to the fragment (rare changes; a value that changes often goes in frames).

shared.description: Keys the module publishes (Cmd::Share) given to the fragment.

emits.description: Named events the fragment may send back (webui:emit); anything else is refused.

calls.description: Methods of the kit's own service the fragment calls directly (webui:call), a kit's own fragment only.

frames.description: Values the fragment reads at every frame, in place in the frame_values region (never as messages): camera.yaw|pitch|x|y|z, a state var of that name, a column of the focused entity (<column>@<major>, e.g. combat.health@1), or what the game writes itself (setFrame).

slot.description: Its named place in the kit (a kit may show several fragments); its key on the bridge is <kit> for main, <kit>/<slot> otherwise.

i18n.description: The fragment has translations (i18n/<lang>.json beside its ui): the page translator reads them.

bind.description: Bindings of the fragment, by name: a refHook (frame:, col:, var:, view:, shared:, call:, event:) or { refHook, every } (ticks, change or frame); the page checks each reference.

on.description: Triggers of the fragment, by name: call:<kit>.<method>, emit:<event> or action:<action>.

when.description: The condition on variables that shows the fragment.

refHooks.description: The fragment has components on the hooks of the page (refHooks of an asset HUD).

contexts.description: The contexts of game.engine's stack it is shown in (all: every context). Default: default.

scenes.description: The scenes it is shown in (ids or kinds of scenes). Default: every scene.

visible.description: Shown (true) or hidden (false) whatever the scene and the context; absent: the rules decide.

layer.description: hud, menu, or loading (above everything, the whole pointer while shown).

origin.description: kit: an official asset (reaches its own kit only). game: the game's own interface (templates, the developer's HUD): it reaches the kits it names in `uses` (web page; the native list does not carry it yet). mod:<id>: the mods policy of game.engine applies.

uses.description: origin game only: the other kits this interface may call and follow (the web bridge, kits.mjs mayReach). An official asset (origin kit) has none.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file, checked when given.

fragments.description: Fragments declared by the game, before those the presentation modules declare (one per kit, the last wins).

frames.description: Per-frame values the game itself wants in the frame_values region, beside those of the fragments.

theme.description: Send the game theme (ui.theme, and its --gf-* CSS variables) to the fragments.

backend.description: Desktop way: auto = cef (embedded browser, shared GPU texture, no copy) everywhere, wry (system web view composed over the game) as the named fallback, copy as the last resort, warned. Overridden by --webui / GRIPFORGE_WEBUI.

strict.description: No fallback: a forced way that cannot work fails clearly (tests, measures). Overridden by --webui-strict / GRIPFORGE_WEBUI_STRICT.

cefOnD3d12.description: Windows hosts drawing with D3D12: cef first (the shared texture is drawn by the Present overlay, no copy); false = wry first, cef as its fallback. Overridden by --webui-cef-d3d12 / GRIPFORGE_WEBUI_CEF_D3D12.

engineSource.description: Where the web engine comes from: the system's (WebView2, WKWebView), shipped with the game, or downloaded once (cached by version, checksum checked). auto = system for wry, download for cef.

engineUrl.description: Where the engine archives are fetched from first: https://, file:///folder/ or a folder (offline), http:// of this machine only; empty = the GripForge distribution. The SHA-256 of the module is always checked.

engineDir.description: Where a fetched engine is kept: a folder shared by several projects. Empty = the project (<project>/webui-engine/) from the editor, the user cache of the system for an exported game. Overridden by --webui-engine-dir / GRIPFORGE_WEBUI_ENGINE_DIR.

bundleEngine.description: Desktop exports: put the web engine of cef beside the exported executable, for the platforms the export targets only; off = nothing shipped, a shared install, else wry, else fetched at the first start (reason in the debugger).

bundleEnginePlatforms.description: With bundleEngine: only these export targets carry the engine; empty = every desktop target exported.

fps.description: Desktop cef: pictures per second of the interface at most (a page at rest makes none).

transparency.description: auto: blended over the game, a page painted opaque by mistake is hidden with a warning, a page declared opaque (data-gf-opaque on <html>) is shown opaque; always: always blended; never: opaque.

clickThrough.description: What the page does not claim goes to the game.

bodyEvents.description: A press on the empty document (body, html) is the page's (full-screen menus).

overlayOnly.description: The page takes no input event (a HUD that only shows).

hudRoot.description: CSS selector: only what is inside it is claimed; empty = anything but the document.

gameKeys.description: Keys that stay the game's even while the page has the keyboard (the debugger's toggleKey, display.fullscreen's key); the page still sees them. Empty = none reserved.

input.description: How the pointer and the keyboard are shared between the page and the game (the same rule on every way).

mixNativeUi.description: Godot / Unity / Unreal: also keep the native UI of the engine for HUD and menus. Default: one way per game. Under Bevy the HUD and menus are always core.webui.

asset.description: The asset shown, <name>[@<range>] (asset.preload.preloader@^1): replaces the kit's default; required for a slot the game declares itself.

file.description: The game's own folder of the asset (hud/hero.stamina/), instead of kit-modules.json hud.

props.description: Props given to the asset, under its own names.

bind.description: Bindings added to the kit's, one by one: a refHook (frame:, col:, var:, view:, shared:, call:, event:) or { refHook, every } (ticks, change or frame).

on.description: Triggers added to the kit's, one by one: call:<kit>.<method>, emit:<event> or action:<action>.

when.description: The condition on variables that shows it (replaces the kit's).

contexts.description: The contexts of game.engine's stack it belongs to (replaces the kit's; all: every context). Default: default.

scenes.description: The scenes it belongs to: ids, kinds or roles of scenes (replaces the kit's). Default: every scene.

visible.description: Shown (true) or hidden (false) whatever the scene and the context; absent: the rule decides.

position.description: Where a free asset sits: { anchor, x, y, w, h } (the nine anchors of the HUD studio); null: the asset's own place.

layer.description: The layer of a slot the game declares itself (a kit's slot keeps the kit's layer).

version.description: The version of the structure of a slot the game declares itself (hudAssets version).

hud.description: The game's choices on the asset HUD slots, by <kit>/<slot>: false or null cuts a kit's slot, an object replaces its asset, adds props and overrides bindings and triggers one by one; a key no kit recommends declares the game's own slot (asset required). Read by the rule hud_plan (docs/assets-hud.md).

file.description: The folder of the game's styleguide.

styleguide.description: The game's styleguide, which replaces the official core.webui.styleguide whole: its folder (<folder>/, with its passport.json and ui.mjs) or { file }; null: the official one. The shorthand of hudLibraries["core.webui.styleguide"].file, and wins over it (with a warning). setStyleguide wins over both; loadStyleguide() follows it (present/web/hud-libs.mjs).

file.description: The folder of the game's library (<folder>/, with its passport.json and ui.mjs).

hudLibraries.description: The game's replacement of an asset HUD library, by its id (core.webui.styleguide): { file }. Absent: kit-modules.json hudLibraries. Read by planLibraries (present/web/hud-libs.mjs, docs/assets-hud.md).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of core.webui (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/debug.inspector.title: debug.inspector in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/debug.inspector.description: What the kit debug.inspector adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

debug_modes.description: The debug modes the inspector offers besides its own (a kit, a game or a mod adds one); the entries the kits expose (debug.expose@1) are filed here too.

enabled.description: The developer's switch for the whole inspector (the key, the panel, the page and agent API): false closes it to everyone, the team included. The kit can also be removed from the game.

toggleKey.description: The one global key of the inspector, opening and closing the panel (KeyboardEvent.code; F9 is free in every control scheme). null: no key, the panel opens only with ?debug=1 or the API. Declared to core.input (the only source of the actions: action debug_toggle of every context `*`, not listed) when the inspector is enabled and the viewer allowed, and read in place in its record of the zone; without core.input there is no key. No other global key and no fallback chord.

panelShortcuts.description: The shortcuts of the open panel only ({ <name>: KeyboardEvent.code | null }: record, measure, report, replay…), read by the panel while it is open, never global. Empty by default: the panel has buttons.

team.description: The owner, the members of the workspace and a local build of the game may open it.

players.description: Public players may open it. false (the default): the team only; true: the game opens it to its players.

query.description: The query parameter that opens it at start for those allowed (debug → ?debug=1); empty: none.

access.description: Who may open the inspector and the query parameter that opens it at start.

refreshFrames.description: Frames between two snapshots the open panel reads, counted at 60 frames a second and never more than 4 snapshots a second.

treeDepth.description: Levels of the scene tree the panel asks for.

treeMaxNodes.description: Nodes of the scene tree at most: the tree is cut beyond it and says so.

wireframe.description: Every mesh drawn as lines when the panel opens.

colliders.description: The colliders the physics holds drawn when the panel opens (mode physics.colliders).

bounds.description: The bounding box of every drawn mesh shown when the panel opens.

startModes.description: The modes on when the panel opens.

side.description: The side of the screen the panel sits on.

layer.description: top: above every other HUD; hud: with the HUD of the game.

width.description: The width of the panel in CSS pixels.

startTab.description: The tab shown when the panel opens: perf, gpu, scene, replay or tab:<id> (a tab below, a tab a kit declares with `tab` of debug.expose@1, or tab:misc). Empty, or a tab that is not there: perf.

filters.description: The chips at the head of a tab of entries (the tabs below, the kits' own tabs and Divers), in their order: all, settings (entries with actions), measures (counters, info), favorites (the viewer's stars, kept by the page), modified (a value that is not its default). []: no chips. The search box is always there.

icon.description: The icon of the tab in the rail: a name of the styleguide's vector registry (`camera`, `gauge`, `brain`; a kit or a game adds its own), an image of the kit or `asset:<name>`. Without it: the icon the first kit of the tab declares, else its family's default (`debugger.families` of debug.inspector), else a folder.

labels.description: The label by language ({ "fr": "Monde" }): the panel writes the one of its language, else label.

tabs.description: The tabs the game adds to the panel's own (Perf, GPU, Scene, Replay); they have the last word over the `tab` a kit declares (debug.expose@1): each shows the debugger entries (debug.expose@1) of the listed kits or sections, with their actions as buttons. A tab with nothing to show is not drawn. Default: Camera (core.camera), Quality (render.quality, world.lighting) and Editor (debug.inspector, dev.builder: the scene editor, its entry debug.inspector.edit, and « Apply to the project »).

panel.description: Where the panel sits, how wide it is, and the tabs it adds for the kits.

refreshHz.description: Reads a second of the open panel: the counter windows closed (means and extremes of the kits' counters, in place), the modes and exposed entries that are on read again (an entry with an epoch only when it changed). Between two reads nothing is read or copied, and the kit rests.

modeFrames.description: When given, ticks between two reads of the open panel instead of refreshHz (a test that reads at every tick).

samples.description: Values kept per counter by the panel for its curve (every value written comes through the pipes; the panel keeps the last ones).

detail.description: Records of each pipe kept by the panel for the detail around a peak (what every kit wrote at that tick, in order).

hz.description: Redraws a second of the panel's curves (frame time, the kits' counters).

freezeOnPeak.description: A curve that shows a peak stays as it is (not redrawn) until it is clicked: the peak can be looked at.

peakFactor.description: A sample beyond the mean of its series times this factor (or divided by it, for a counter whose peaks are low: peak "low") is a peak, marked on its curve; a counter's own peakAbove / peakBelow (expose values) wins.

series.description: The curves of the panel: every value comes through the pipes, emptied by the page and drawn at a low rhythm (hz), so a one-tick peak a mean hides shows.

threads.description: The writing threads that get a pipe (one writer each); tick is always first (the kits' counters, the events).

slots.description: Records of 32 bytes a pipe holds between two reads of the panel (rounded up to a power of two); beyond, the newest are dropped and counted, the writer never waits.

pipes.description: debug.expose@1 pipes: one circular queue per writing thread in shared memory, one writer and one reader, made at the first opening of the panel (nothing while it was never opened, nothing written while it is closed).

eventsKept.description: Recent events kept per exposed events entry, while the panel is open (debug.expose@1): the fixed slots of its ring, written in place.

eventBytes.description: Bytes of an event's payload (as JSON text) one slot of a ring holds; a longer payload is kept cut (cut: true).

probeSeconds.description: Presentation module (blank player): seconds between two reads of the render counters while someone looks.

limit.description: Presentation module: objects of the scene table at most (the table is cut beyond it and says so).

objects.description: The object table of the presentation module.

maxEdges.description: Presentation module: edges of the wireframe at most (0: the module's default).

wireframe.description: The wireframe of the presentation module.

snapshotWatchTicks.description: Ticks the kits keep counting after a snapshot asked while the panel is closed (word 0 of their counter blocks), so the next snapshots of an agent are live; 0: a closed panel never makes them count.

tolerance.description: The gap a replay accepts as close: the verdict gives the gap measured and this tolerance (close under it, different beyond).

ignore.description: Parts of the paths of the final state a verdict leaves out (the inspector's own variables by default).

maxEvents.description: Inputs a recording keeps at most; beyond, it counts the ones it drops (dropped).

replay.description: The recordings of a game (gripforge.replay/1) and their replay, by the panel's buttons or the API.

maxSamples.description: Step times a measure keeps at most (an hour at 60 ticks a second).

measure.description: The measures of the host's recorder and their report (gripforge.perf/1).

fovStep.description: Degrees one press of the field-of-view keys changes the camera that draws.

fovMin.description: The narrowest field of view the keys give, degrees.

fovMax.description: The widest field of view the keys give, degrees.

topCount.description: Objects listed by the top (the most triangles).

wireframe.description: Lets the wireframe key work on the web page. On by default (the web player keeps the skin of a mesh since #1135); a game that does not want the key sets false: the key then says so.

refreshMs.description: Milliseconds between two reads of the scene tree while the top or the lights are on.

keys.description: KeyboardEvent.code of each tool: ACTIONS declared to core.input (debug_view_<name>, every context), so a game remaps them like any action. F2 is the editor's, not here.

wireframe.description: Every mesh as lines (the panel's wireframe mode).

top.description: The most expensive objects; a click flies the free camera to one.

lights.description: The lights the player draws, with their distance to the camera.

cutNext.description: Hides the next group of the scene, to compare with and without.

timePause.description: Holds the game or lets it run again (the host's time operation); the screen says « pause ». The time keys are keys of the page, not core.input actions: a held game plays no tick, so core.input would never hear the key that lets it go.

timeStep.description: Plays one tick, the game held.

timeSlower.description: Slows the game down one step (x0.1, x0.25, x0.5, x1).

timeFaster.description: Speeds the game up one step (x1, x2, x4).

viewTools.description: The view tools of the page (present/web/view-tools.mjs): numbers and keys, over their defaults.

sensitivity.description: Radians of turn per pixel of the pointer, in free flight.

speed.description: Metres a second at the start of a flight (the wheel then sets it).

fast.description: The factor of the fast key.

wheel.description: The wheel's effect on the speed: speed times exp(-delta times this).

pitchLimit.description: Radians the camera may look up or down (short of the vertical).

maxStep.description: Seconds of clock one frame may fly (a stalled page does not throw the camera away).

eyeHeight.description: Metres under the camera where the player is put when the ray down finds no ground.

groundRay.description: Metres of the ray down that finds the ground under the camera.

focusDistance.description: « Camera on it »: distance from the object, in radii of its box.

focusMin.description: « Camera on it »: the nearest the camera stands, metres.

focusPitch.description: « Camera on it »: radians the camera looks down at the object.

context.description: The exclusive core.input context pushed while flying: it blocks the game's keys (the character keeps still).

keys.description: KeyboardEvent.code of each control (physical keys: on an AZERTY keyboard KeyW is Z and KeyA is Q, so ZQSD flies like WASD).

toggle.description: Flies or lands (the kit's own free camera action).

teleport.description: In flight: puts the player on the ground under the camera.

hideUi.description: Hides or shows the interface (a clean capture).

freeCamera.description: The free camera the page flies for the debugger (present/web/free-flight.mjs): numbers and keys, over its defaults.

edit.description: The capability edit (debug.inspector.edit; docs/design/f9-edit.md): select an object, move, turn it with the gizmo, undo. It works with the panel closed (the editor of the site calls it without F9).

enabled.description: Editing on. false: every method that changes something answers false and says refused { reason: export } once; reading (state, objects, positionOf, links, gizmo) stays. An exported game is off whatever this says (the mark build.export of the lowered project).

toggleKey.description: A key of its own that opens and closes the editor (KeyboardEvent.code), declared to core.input as the action debug_inspector_edit_toggle of every context, not listed. null by default: F9 is the only debugging key and the editor opens from the Editor tab of its panel (the entry debug.inspector.edit), from the API (debug.inspector.edit.setActive) or from the page.

rotateStepDeg.description: One notch of a rotation (the key R, the wheel), degrees.

gizmo.description: The handles on the selected object (arrows and squares to move, rings to turn, lines ending in a square to scale). Everything the page draws and every key is data here.

enabled.description: Show the handles. false: only the click and the drag stuck to the ground of stage a.

mode.description: The handles at the opening of the editor.

space.description: world: the arrows and rings follow the world; local: they follow the object (turned with it). A scale always follows the object.

scaleStep.description: The step of a scale factor while the snap key (Ctrl) is held.

sizePx.description: How long the arrows are on the screen, pixels (the same at any distance).

gridM.description: The grid of a move while the snap key (Ctrl) is held, metres.

notchDeg.description: The notch of a turn by a ring while the snap key (Ctrl) is held, degrees.

deadZone.description: Where the arrows start, as a fraction of their length. A click nearer the middle of the object is a click on the object (it drags it stuck to the ground), not on a handle.

snapByDefault.description: true: the grid and the notches are on, and Ctrl frees them.

rotateAxes.description: The rings that may turn an object. A ring turns the engine node of the object (3 axes, the render); the game's entity linked to it keeps only its heading. An object that is an entity alone (no engine node) turns about the vertical only: its other rings are drawn dim.

colors.description: CSS colours of the axes, of the lit handle and of a ring that cannot be dragged.

move.description: The handles that move (action debug_inspector_edit_move), e.g. KeyW.

rotate.description: The rings that turn (debug_inspector_edit_rotate), e.g. KeyE.

scale.description: The squares that scale (debug_inspector_edit_scale), e.g. KeyS.

turnAxis.description: An axis that turns by notches, its sign (debug_inspector_edit_turn), e.g. Wheel.

keys.description: The bindings of the editor's actions, declared to core.input in the context debug.inspector.edit (taken from the game while the editor is open). Data only: the game or its template gives them; none is written in the code, an action without one is declared unbound (rebindable).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of debug.inspector (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

kit.description: The kit the mode belongs to (default: the id without its last part).

kind.description: overlay: lines and marks in the scene; info: rows in the panel; scene: nodes beside the scene tree.

section.description: debug.expose@1: where the panel files the entry (gives the kind when it has none).

call.description: The service call that gives its data while it is on (<capability>.<method>), read panel open only.

epoch.description: The call whose answer changes with the data: the entry is read again only then.

state.description: The call that answers the real values of the actions.

on.description: On when the game starts (an exposed entry is on unless it says false).

actions.description: The direct options of the mode: { <name>: { label, kind: button | toggle | number | select, call, args?, options?, value?, from? } }, run on the op action ($value in args is the value sent).

description.description: What the entry shows (a tooltip of the panel).

values.description: debug.expose@1, section counters: the counters the kit writes in place in its block (counters(kit, names)); its curve marks a peak above peakAbove / below peakBelow, else beyond series.peakFactor of its mean, high (default) or low (peak).

topics.description: debug.expose@1, section events: the topics kept in a ring while the panel is open.

gripforge.kit/dev.builder.title: dev.builder in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/dev.builder.description: What the kit dev.builder adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

lights.description: Places the light nodes of the scenes through core.light when it is installed. Off: they are only read and shown.

cameras.description: Places the camera nodes of the scenes through core.camera when it is installed. Off: they are only read and shown.

lookAhead.description: Metres ahead of a camera node, along its -Z axis, of the point its fixed preset looks at.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of dev.builder (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/game.construction.title: game.construction in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/game.construction.description: What the kit game.construction adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

pieces.description: The catalogue: data (collection pieces), config pieces, code (declare), mods; field by field over the kind.

pieceKinds.description: The kinds of piece: none by default; data, config, code (declare); extends another kind.

socketKinds.description: Which kinds of socket accept which.

gridKinds.description: free, square, snap and the kinds made on them (base).

ruleKinds.description: reach, collision, ground, support, zone, limit and the kinds made on them (base).

pieces.description: The catalogue: [{ id, kind, name?, maxHp?, model?, instanced?, supportKind?, clearScenery?, components?, …fields of its kind overridden }]. Empty by default: the game names its own. Moddable.

pieceKinds.description: Kinds of piece (none by default: the game declares its own, the template construction-house a small house): { id: { shape: { box }, grid, sockets, rules, anchor?, supportKind?, instanced?, clearScenery?, extends? } }, field by field. Moddable.

socketKinds.description: Kinds of socket (none by default): { id: { accepts: [kind…] } }. Moddable.

gridKinds.description: Kinds of grid over free, square and snap: { id: { base, cell?, height?, rotateStep?, frame? } }. Moddable.

ruleKinds.description: Kinds of rule over reach, collision, ground, support, zone and limit: { id: { base, …fields } }. Moddable.

clearScenery.description: A piece placed asks world.scenery and world.natural (optional) to keep its footprint clear (keepClear) and gives it back when it goes (release). A kind of piece or a piece cuts it with clearScenery: false (a fence in the grass).

snapDistance.description: How far from the point aimed at a free socket of a placed piece snaps the new piece (metres).

groundY.description: The ground plane the rule support reads for a piece that may stand on the ground (orGround, anchor) when no ground probe answers.

dismantleMode.description: cascade: what rested on a piece dismantled falls by its support graph (core.physics loaded) and is removed; refuse: a piece that holds another is not dismantled (reason supporting).

support.description: Each structure is a support graph of core.physics (optional), sent again only when it changed.

instanced.description: The pieces of one model are drawn as one set by the presentation module (instancing: one draw per part of the model, whatever the number of pieces). A kind or a piece with instanced: false (a door that opens, a piece whose reflect changes) keeps the model of its entity.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of game.construction (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

kind.description: Its kind of piece (pieceKinds).

pieceKinds.description: A `kind of piece` document of data.pieceKinds.

socketKinds.description: A `kind of socket` document of data.socketKinds.

gridKinds.description: A `kind of grid` document of data.gridKinds.

ruleKinds.description: A `kind of rule` document of data.ruleKinds.

gripforge.kit/game.craft.title: game.craft in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/game.craft.description: What the kit game.craft adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

recipes.description: The recipes: data (craftRecipes), config recipes, code (defineRecipe), mods; field by field, with origins; extends.

stations.description: The station kinds: hand by default, data (craftStations), config stations, code (registerStation).

conditions.description: Condition kinds written as a rule: { id: { rule } }.

outputs.description: Output kinds a game gives itself on game.craft.completed.

handCrafting.description: Recipes that name no station are made by hand.

queueSize.description: The queue size of an owner (5).

refund.description: Share of the inputs given back when a queued job is cancelled (1).

refundStarted.description: Share given back when a running job is cancelled (1).

onFull.description: What is done with outputs that do not fit: owe (given as soon as there is room), drop (a pickup at the station), hold (the job waits in its slot).

missingCondition.description: A condition whose kit is absent: fail (not met, warned once) or ignore.

defaultDiscovery.description: The discovery kind of a recipe that names none.

knownScope.description: Who knows a discovered recipe: the entity, or every entity of its player.

pauseInContexts.description: Contexts of game.engine in which the queues freeze.

toolWear.description: The tools wear (false): each craft adds its wear to the key game.craft.wear of the tool's stack in game.inventory; a tool is taken at its durability.

defaultWear.description: The wear of a tool whose recipe gives none (1).

durability.description: The durability of a tool by item: { <item>: <points> }.

defaultDurability.description: The durability of a tool durability does not name (100).

context.description: The context pushed while the panel is open (craft).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of game.craft (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

name.description: Text or a table by language, for the HUD.

category.description: Groups the recipe in the HUD; a station kind may allow a whole category.

inputs.description: Taken from the crafter's inventory when the job is queued (paid at the start).

kind.description: An output kind (item by default, placeable).

outputs.description: Given at the end, each by its output kind.

seconds.description: How long it lasts (0: at once), turned into ticks of game.engine.

tools.description: Held while crafting, not taken unless consume.

stations.description: The station kinds it is made at; empty: by hand (handCrafting).

kind.description: A condition kind: level, state, var, rule.

discovery.description: A discovery kind: known, unlock, ingredient, craft (default: defaultDiscovery).

extends.description: Inherits another recipe, field by field.

reach.description: How far a crafter uses it, in metres.

queueOwner.description: station: one shared queue per instance; crafter: one per crafter.

gripforge.kit/game.engine.title: game.engine in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/game.engine.description: What the kit game.engine adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

archetypes.description: Every kind of thing a scene places; { id, extends: "<archetype>" } inherits one and changes or adds what it writes (an interactable on a crate, another model).

nodeTypes.description: The types of the nodes of a scene tree, in data: the base ones (core/scene-format/src/node_types.json, never removed: their properties with type, default and description, the bindings they accept, what game.engine makes of them), those a kit declares (nodeType on an expose entry for scene of its kit.api.json, read by that kit), then the project collection nodeTypes (a game or a mod adds a type or changes a base one, key by key). game.engine owns the tree; dev.builder and the compiler read this registry. Served by game.engine.scenes.nodeTypes().

revisionKeys.description: The keys of revision of the parts of an entity (core/kit-api revision_keys, docs/registres.md): the table stays the block the threads read in place, this collection fills it at the mount; action and physics are given by default and never removed.

kinds.description: The entity kinds (docs/design/game-engine-kinds.md): kits and the game register kinds with kind properties (collection kinds, registerKind at run time); contributions merge property by property.

startScene.description: Scene to start in (default: the first scene, or the implicit scene of a project without scenes).

startEntry.description: Entry of the start scene (default: its first entry).

title.description: on: wait on the ui.menu title screen (Play) before entering the start scene.

shapes.description: The values a simple shape (model.shape) takes for a size it leaves out; a scene or a mod changes them like any config.

material.description: The material of a simple shape for a field it leaves out (over a model file, a material only replaces what it gives).

texture.description: Texture keys of the game (a path of its assets, or a slot it binds): color, normal, metallicRoughness (glTF: metal blue, roughness green).

materials.description: Named materials, reused by name (asset.material, model.material, set_material).

texture.description: Texture keys of the game (a path of its assets, or a slot it binds): color, normal, metallicRoughness (glTF: metal blue, roughness green).

placement.description: Spawn placement queries active engine collisions. The legacy baked setting is accepted but no longer samples terrain or uses cached coordinates.

enabled.description: false: no mod is applied to this game.

order.description: Application order (the others follow in document order); a mod always comes after the mods it depends on.

deny.description: What the mods of this game may not touch, among what the kits declare moddable.

story.description: Story flags: { "lantern_found": false } → story.lantern_found variables, saved with the game.

contexts.description: The contexts of the game over default (docs/contextes.md): ["dialogue", "menu", "pause"]. A mod adds some by its config patch, code by game.engine.contexts.create. all is not a context: it is what a listener declares to hear in every one.

priorities.description: Named priorities of the takes, over the defaults game 200, dialogue 600, cinematic 800, editor 850, debug 900 (a name added here is usable by take and take_over).

menu.description: scene: the title screen of ui.menu is a scene of its own, entered first with no world behind it (the project's role: menu scene, else one synthesised: menu); Play leads to the start scene. overlay: the title is drawn over the start scene (before 1.7). Every project gets scene once it is opened (autoUpdateProject) and every new game is made with it.

menuScene.description: The menu scene, when several interface scenes exist.

loading.description: How a scene whose files are not in yet waits: ui.menu's loading screen, the loading scene, nothing, or background (the scene left stays until the next one is ready).

loadingScene.description: Id of the scene of kind loading shown between two scenes when loading is scene (default: the first such scene, else one synthesised).

loadTimeout.description: Seconds a scene waits for its files before it is entered anyway.

minLoadingMs.description: Shortest time a loading screen stays, in milliseconds (0: only while files load).

unload.description: release: leaving a scene frees its instances and the memory of the files only it used (never the disk cache, never a preload asked elsewhere).

transition.description: How a scene comes in when neither it nor the call says: replace (the scene left is unloaded) or add (it stays loaded under the new one).

showAfterMs.description: A loading screen comes up only when the files of the next scene are still not in after this many milliseconds (preloaded or cached files: no screen at all, no flash).

onFail.description: A file of the next scene failed: retry (up to retries, then enter), enter (go on without it) or wait (until game.engine.scenes.retry() or cancelLoading()).

retries.description: How many times onFail retry asks the files that failed again.

image.description: An illustration shown while the scene loads.

tips.description: Tips shown one at a time (i18n.text keys preferably).

image.description: An image filling the loading screen.

video.description: A muted video looping behind the loading screen.

color.description: The colour behind the loading screen (#rrggbb).

background.description: The backdrop of the loading screen.

title.description: The title shown (default: the title of the scene loading).

loadingScreen.description: 1.7: the dressing of a loading screen (overlay or loading scene).

hz.description: The logic tick in Hz, the game maker's choice (strategy 10-20, action 30, twitch shooter 60): kit logic, actions and timers run at this fixed rate, decoupled from the frame rate (the render loop interpolates between the last two ticks) and from the physics step (its own loop, tick.physicsHz, 60 Hz by default; a change of one never touches the other). Live: a change (config, runtime.core.tickAdjust({ hz }), the F9 panel) takes effect at the next tick boundary, nothing reset. Not moddable: every peer of a match plays the same tick; in a match only the authority changes it.

maxCatchUp.description: Optional cap on the ticks one frame may catch up. 0 (default): no cap, every due tick is played (one frame hands the clock 0.25 s at most, so a stall never spirals). A number: past it the rest of the time is dropped. Only the tick fed from the frame (source "frame") accumulates ticks; on the physics step of an engine the engine's own catch-up applies (Godot max_physics_steps_per_frame).

source.description: Who counts the action tick. "independent" (default, every engine and network included): the TickClock runs on real time, so the actions keep their pace if the physics slows down; the ticks due are played at the first callback the engine offers (Godot _process), with no cap unless maxCatchUp is set. "engine-physics": the action tick is counted from the physics loop of the engine (Godot _physics_process, Unity FixedUpdate), with its fixed step, never the frame time; it slows down with the physics. Characters move correctly in both (they use the step of the loop they run in).

physicsHz.description: The physics step in Hz, its own loop, not correlated with the action tick (tick.hz never changes it). 0 (default): 60 Hz on a host that owns the physics clock (the web, the Rapier of core.physics), the engine setting otherwise. A number (1..240): the host sets it (Godot physics_ticks_per_second, Unity fixedDeltaTime with the engine-physics source, Bevy Time<Fixed>). Live: runtime.core.tickAdjust({ physicsHz }), the F9 panel (null: back to the default). The characters move with the physics step, never with the frame time.

interpolate.description: Render interpolation between two ticks (alpha, tick_alpha()). Off: the latest tick is shown as is.

catchUpSteps.description: With the physics on a loop of its own (a Worker): under this many physics steps of drift between the physics clock and the frames, the drawn time catches up gently (5 %); above, faster. 0 (default): 2 steps.

snapAfter.description: With the physics on a loop of its own: over this drift in seconds, the render interpolation is cut and the drawn time set at once (a load, a held time, a stalled Worker). 0 (default): 0.25 s.

smoothing.description: Render smoothing by time of the poses a physics on a loop of its own owns (as Godot's physics interpolation): every pose drawn at one physics instant per frame, one step in the past. On by default; false (or the address ?render.smoothing=0): the newest published pose, between the two photos of the tick.

systems.description: Every-N periods of the kit systems, by "<kit>.<system>": a number of ticks, or { every, offset, hz } (offset: the phase, spread by name by default). Example { "npc.core.decide": 3, "stealth.detection.perceive": 2 }. Combat hit resolution stays every tick.

tick.description: The logic tick (docs/game-engine-contract.md « Boucle de tick et boucle de rendu »).

thread.description: Where the action loop (the TickClock and the ticks of the kits) runs. "main" (default): on the main thread of the engine, in its callbacks (Godot _process). "own": on a thread of its own on a computer (a Web Worker with shared memory on the web): the main thread reads the presented state in place and never waits for a tick; the physics stays the engine's, on its own thread when it can, and is asked through the ordered queue and the tickets of the physics (ask_move_character / poll_moved); what must run on the main thread (scene, nodes, _action_process, signals) is played at the next callback of the engine with its tick number, at most one frame later. When the host cannot (no threads, a page that is not cross-origin isolated, a GDScript service or tap the kits call during the tick, tick.source engine-physics) it stays on "main" and says why (F9 TICK, tick_info().threadWhy). Godot today; Unity, Unreal and Bevy keep "main".

action.description: The action loop (docs/game-engine-contract.md « Boucle de tick et boucle de rendu », action.thread).

Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

layouts.description: The layouts by name: one_stick (move + buttons) and twin_stick (move on the left, look on the right) shipped; a game or a mod adds or replaces one in data (config layouts.<name>) or in code (registerLayout), then picks it (config layout, useLayout).

layout.description: The joypad in use: the name of a layout of `layouts` (a registry), or a layout itself { sticks: [{ id, action, control?, mode: floating|fixed, zone: { x, y, w, h }, center?, radius?, deadzone?, portrait? }] (one or two), buttons: [{ id, action, control?, label?, icon?, size?, position?: { x, y }, shape?: round|square|pill, mode?: press|hold|toggle, group?, contexts?, when?, opacity?, portrait? }], arc?: { center, radius, from, to, portrait? } }. layouts.description: Named layouts added to (or replacing by name) the shipped ones, `one_stick` and `twin_stick` (registry `layouts`, registerLayout).

display.description: When the joypad shows: auto (on a touch screen, hidden as soon as a keyboard or a pad is used), on, off. The player's setting input.virtual_joypad.display; the game imposes one with core.settings (visibility: game) or here.

size.description: The scale of every control (player setting input.virtual_joypad.size).

pilots.description: The entities piloted at start: [{ entity | tag, player, mover }] (player: the core.input player index; mover: the options of core.locomotion.add). Empty: the genre player, the game or core.control.possess gives one.

lookSensitivity.description: Radians the body turns per unit of core.input's look (a pointer pixel at gain 1); also the pitch of the camera (core.camera setLookInput): one scale.

lookTurnSpeed.description: Radians per second the body turns at the full right stick (the stick binding of the look action the kit declares when the game has none).

pitchLimit.description: The most the look pitches up or down (radians), for the camera and control.look@1.

camera.description: The camera of the genre, applied to the camera the game designates (cameraNode, else the one that draws, else one made): params of the firstPerson preset (eyeHeight, point, offset; yawFrom is target) over the kit's, transition (seconds of the blend when the kit takes the camera over).

keys.description: The actions the kit declares to core.input, by name: { kind, bindings, label? } over the default of the same name (move_x, move_y, move_pad, sprint, jump, crouch, look). A game's own declaration of an action is kept; the player rebinds them in core.input.

profile.description: The movement profile of the genre registered in core.locomotion as first_person (walkSpeed, runSpeed, defaultGait, acceleration, deceleration, turnRate, pivotAngle, turnKeepSpeed, faceMovement, jumpImpulse, gravity, airJumps, airJumpImpulse, crouch, crouchSpeed, crouchHeight): every value overridable by the game, except turnSmoothing (0: the yaw is the look's).

modes.description: The mode settings of the genre laid over core.locomotion's registry (by id).

animationTable.description: The core.animation table the piloted entities read (the default table when the game registered none of that name).

player.description: The genre player: the factory of the entity kind player (tag player, model slot player_character); at start, when no pilot is given, the entity of kind player already there (a row of data.spawns) is piloted, else one is made; a scene entry puts it at the entry (hook locomotion.first_person.respawn). false: the game or core.control.possess gives the entities (a game that loads both genre kits keeps the player of one).

spawnZone.description: Where the player appears when nothing says (no pilot given, no row of data.spawns): zone, the id of a zone of the optional kit world.zones, the player standing gap metres before its edge on -Z. Empty zone (the default), no such zone or no world.zones: the origin.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/locomotion.pointer.title: locomotion.pointer in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/locomotion.pointer.description: What the kit locomotion.pointer adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

pilots.description: The entities piloted at start: [{ entity | tag, player, mover }] (player: the core.input player index; mover: the options of core.locomotion.add). Empty: the genre player, the game or core.control.possess gives one.

style.description: The style of the buttons, a name of styles: click (the left button or a finger goes and acts; the middle button drags the camera), moba (the right button or a finger goes; the left one is the game's). Live: setStyle. The player's choice, the variable settings.input.pointer_style of core.settings, takes over when it names a style (read in place; absent: this default).

styles.description: The game's styles, by name, over the kit's: { <name>: { go: [bindings], drag: [bindings] } }.

arrive.description: Closer than this to the point (m), the order is done (locomotion.pointer.arrived).

reach.description: Closer than this to the entity aimed at (m), the kit acts on it; a rule of targets may give its own.

repath.description: A target that moved this far (m) gets its goal written again to ai.navigation.

follow.description: The go button held: the order follows the pointer (points only; a target of the press stays).

followEvery.description: Seconds between two rays of the held go button.

navigation.description: auto: the path of ai.navigation when it is loaded; off: always the straight line.

blocked.description: A route that cannot be made (unreachable, outside, unavailable): stop (locomotion.pointer.blocked, the marker blocked) or walk the straight line.

stall.description: Ticks without getting nearer before the order is dropped (locomotion.pointer.blocked, reason stalled).

turn.description: The angle (degrees) the direction must turn before the kit sends it again to core.control (setIntent); a stop or a start is always sent. A few calls per order, never one per tick.

targets.description: What a click on an entity does, the first rule that takes it: [{ tags?, kinds?, action, reach? }] (no tags nor kinds: any entity). action use: core.physics.use at the reach; any other: told by locomotion.pointer.acted for the kit that does it (a combat kit for attack).

seconds.description: The longest life of a marker (s).

fade.description: The fade of its opacity at the end (s), at the render.

ring.description: The kit's presentation module draws a ring on the ground (and no stand-in for the entity); false: the model of the slot locomotion_pointer_marker the game fills, whose opacity the module fades.

radius.description: The outer radius of the ring (m).

opacity.description: The opacity of a living marker, faded to 0 over the column's fade once it is gone.

colors.description: The colour of each state (#rrggbb): move, target, blocked; gone keeps the last one while it fades.

look.description: The look of the marker at the render (the presentation module of the kit reads it; the logic never does).

marker.description: The marker of the destination: an entity of kind locomotion.pointer.marker (model slot locomotion_pointer_marker), its state in the column locomotion.pointer.marker@1 [state atom move|target|blocked|gone, ended at (s), fade (s)]; one per pilot, a new order fades the old one. look: how the render draws it.

transition.description: Seconds of the blend when the kit takes the camera.

camera.description: The camera of the genre (cameraNode, else the one that draws, else one made): the params of the topDown preset of core.camera (distance, minDistance, maxDistance, yaw, pitch), the zoom by camera_zoom, the drag by camera_drag (the framed point moves; camera_recenter frames the body again).

keys.description: The actions the kit declares to core.input, by name: { kind, bindings, label? } over the default of the same name (pointer, pointer_go, camera_drag, camera_zoom, camera_recenter). A game's own declaration of an action is kept; the player rebinds them in core.input.

profile.description: The movement profile of the genre (core.locomotion profile pointer) over the kit's: walkSpeed 5, faceMovement, turnSpeed 14, no jump. The speed of the walk lives here, one place.

modes.description: The mode settings of the genre laid over core.locomotion's registry (by id).

animationTable.description: The animation table of core.animation for the entities piloted (the default table when the game has none of that name).

player.description: The genre player: the factory of the entity kind player (tag player, model slot player_character); at start, when no pilot is given, the entity of kind player already there (a row of data.spawns) is piloted, else one is made; a scene entry puts it at the entry (hook locomotion.pointer.respawn). false: the game or core.control.possess gives the entities (a game that loads both genre kits keeps the player of one).
