gripforge.kit/locomotion.third_person.title: locomotion.third_person in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/locomotion.third_person.description: What the kit locomotion.third_person adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

pilots.description: The entities piloted at start: [{ entity | tag, player, mover }] (player: the core.input player index, 0 by default; mover: the options of core.locomotion.add for it, bodyNode, originOffset...). Empty: the game or core.control.possess gives one.

mouseMode.description: capture: the pointer is captured, the mouse turns the camera, the body walks where it looks; the right button released recenters the camera behind the body in camera.returnTime. mmo: the pointer stays free; left button held orbits the camera only; right button held aligns the body on the camera and walks where it looks (A / D step aside); both held walk forward; no button: A / D turn the body (control.turn) and the camera follows its heading, back behind it in camera.returnTime when the left button is released. Live: setMouseMode, a player picks it in the options.

facing.description: What the body faces outside the mmo steering: where it goes (movement), or the camera (camera: the kit writes control.wanted_dir from the heading of the camera). In mmo the body faces the camera while the right button is held, and keeps its own heading otherwise.

turnRate.description: Radians per second the body turns at a full control.turn@1 (A / D in mmo): the turnSpeed of the third_person profile, unless profile.turnSpeed says its own.

camera.description: The camera of the genre, applied to the camera the game designates (cameraNode, else the one that draws, else one made): params of the thirdPerson preset (height, distance, shoulder, yawFrom, followDelay, followSpeed) over the ones the mouse mode chooses, followHeading (capture only: the camera comes back behind the body once the look is still), look (the settings of core.camera.setLookInput; the sensitivity is core.camera's own, lookInput.sensitivity: one scale for the pitch and the yaw, the kit has none), walls (true: the walls option with its defaults; an object: its settings; false: off), fadeNear (true: the body the camera follows fades out when the camera comes close, as against a wall where the camera goes to the eyes: core.camera fadeNear whole beyond 1.2 m and gone at 0.8 m, measured from the camera to the centre of each mesh as the engines do; an object: its settings; false: off), transition (seconds of the camera blend when the kit takes the camera over), returnTime (seconds the camera takes to come back behind the body).

keys.description: The keys of the actions the kit reads, by name: { kind, bindings, label? } (move_x, move_y, move_pad, sprint, jump, crouch, orbit, steer; the mouse buttons are the web codes, Mouse0 left, Mouse2 right). The kit declares them WITHOUT keys: the game (its template) gives them here or declares them in core.input. A game's own declaration of an action is kept; the player rebinds them in core.input.

profile.description: The movement profile of the genre registered in core.locomotion as third_person (walkSpeed, runSpeed, defaultGait, acceleration, deceleration, turnRate, pivotAngle, turnKeepSpeed, turnSmoothing, faceMovement, turnSpeed, jumpImpulse, gravity, airJumps, airJumpImpulse, crouch, crouchSpeed, crouchHeight): every value overridable by the game.

modes.description: The mode settings of the genre (swim, fly, glide... speed, gravity, triggers), laid over core.locomotion's registry: every value overridable by the game.

animationTable.description: The core.animation table the piloted entities read (setTable, when core.animation is loaded). Its content comes with core.animation (D4, from the states of today's stance.rs).

player.description: The genre player (#655: this kit declares the player): the factory of the entity kind player (tag player, model slot player_character); at start, when no pilot is given, the entity of kind player already there (a row of data.spawns) is piloted, else one is made from that row or at the default place (the zone spawnZone names, else the origin); a scene entry puts it at the entry, a player gone with the previous scene is made again. Each player is piloted (core.control possess), moved by core.locomotion (profile third_person) and animated by core.animation when the game has them. false: the game or core.control.possess gives the entities, as in 0.1.0.

spawnZone.description: Where the player appears when nothing says (no pilot given, no row of data.spawns): zone, the id of a zone of the optional kit world.zones, the player standing gap metres before its edge on -Z. Empty zone (the default), no such zone or no world.zones: the origin.

lock.description: The locked mode (services lock / lockNext / unlock, bound by the game: the kit reads no key): search = the query of core.physics.search (radius 15, cone 140, sort score, limit 16, tags [lockable]; from and exclude set by the kit; tags, notTags, kinds, layers, sight as in core.physics); breakDistance (20 m): beyond, the target is released; noTarget: recenter (the camera back behind the character, the heading held with side steps) or none; camera: the params of core.camera's preset target (height, distance, maxDistance, pitch, margin, shoulder, turnSpeed); weights: [character, target] among the subjects framed ([1, 1]); transition: seconds of the camera blend into and out of the lock (0.3).

freeLookReturnPitch.description: mmo: the left button released (the free look ends) brings the camera back to the default pitch as well as behind the body, over camera.returnTime, interrupted if the button is pressed again. False: the pitch the player chose stays. The right button (steering) always keeps the pitch the player aims with.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of locomotion.third_person (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/locomotion.vehicle.title: locomotion.vehicle in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/locomotion.vehicle.description: What the kit locomotion.vehicle adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The vehicle genres by id; the game or a mod adds or changes one, registerGenre does it at run time. car, the default genre, is a base entry.

support.description: What carries it: wheels on a suspension, floats on water, hover pads, nothing (space).

mass.description: kg of the body the kit makes when the vehicle has none.

size.description: Half sizes [x, y, z] of that body (m).

centerOfMass.description: Where its mass sits in its frame (low keeps a car on its wheels).

gravityScale.description: Gravity on its body (0: a ship).

damping.description: { linear, angular } damping of its body.

engine.description: { force (N), maxSpeed, reverseSpeed (m/s), boost (factor of force and top speed while sprint) }.

brakes.description: { force (N per braked wheel), handbrake (N; 0: none, the brakes instead), rolling (N while coasting) }.

suspension.description: { restLength, travel (m), stiffness, compression, relaxation, maxForce (N) } (wheels).

grip.description: { friction (how much a tyre holds before it slips), side (side grip) } (wheels).

steering.description: { maxAngle (degrees), rate (degrees/s), speedFalloff (0..1: less angle at top speed) } (wheels).

thrust.description: { forward, reverse, vertical (N), yaw (N·m), autoLevel (pull back upright) } (floats, hover pads, space).

hover.description: { height (m), stiffness, damping } of the pads.

float.description: { buoyancy (times its weight the floats carry fully under), drag, waterLevel (m, when no water kit says it) }.

sideDrag.description: Damping of the sideways slide on water and air cushions.

wheels.description: Its points (wheels, floats, pads), 8 at most: [{ at [x, y, z] (+Z forward, +X left), radius, steer, drive, brake, handbrake (shares 0..1; steer -1..1) }].

seats.description: Its seats: [{ id, at, driver (the first by default), exit (where it gets out; 2 m on its side by default), exitYaw (rad from the vehicle's heading, 0 by default), eject (m/s added when thrown out; 3 m/s on its side and 4 up by default) }] in its frame.

bend.description: How it lays the grass of world.natural down (the component world.natural.bend put on each vehicle once; world.natural optional): false / true, or { enabled, strength (0..2), spread (a factor on the radius taken from the hull and the wheels), radius (m, instead), offset (m from the origin down to the ground, instead) }. Car 1, kart 0.8, hovercraft 1.5 and 1.4 wider, boat and spaceship off.

genres.description: The registry of vehicle genres, by name, over the shipped ones (car, kart, boat, hovercraft, spaceship; field by field over the genre of the same name, else over the car).

defaultGenre.description: The genre of a vehicle that names none (or an unknown one).

vehicles.description: The vehicles at start: [{ entity | tag, genre, bend }] (bend: the vehicle's own, over its genre's).

drivers.description: The entities whose buttons (move, sprint, jump…) the kit watches from the start: [entity | { entity | tag }]. The kit reads no button to board or get off: the game calls it.

parkBrake.description: A vehicle nobody drives holds its handbrake.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/menu.main.title: menu.main in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/menu.main.description: What the kit menu.main adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

entries.description: The entries of each screen (title, pause): the defaults, the entries the kits declare (expose for menu.main, field entry with its screen, origin kit:<id>), the config entries that overlay them by id and screen, code (add, remove, move, enable), the hook menu.main.arrange before each publication.

actions.description: The genres of action an entry runs: play, continue, resume, settings, quit, scene, call, emit (base, never removed nor replaced); each says when its entry is visible (a kit it needs is absent: hidden, said to the debugger; quit: native only; continue stays hidden: the game declares its own entry). A game or a mod adds its own in the config key actions, each run as call or emit with its fields.

title.description: The title of the game shown by the menu (variable menu.main.title); empty: the asset's own title prop.

context.description: The context of game.engine's stack the menu declares and pushes while it is open, on both screens (docs/contextes.md).

open.description: scene: the menu opens when game.engine enters a scene of role menu (its menu scene) and closes when the game leaves that scene; manual: only by the service open(). Without game.engine it opens at the start.

playScene.description: The scene play leads to; empty: the first scene of role level (game.engine.scenes.levels()), else game.engine's start scene.

invite.description: Ask for a first gesture (click, key, touch) before the entries, once per launch: the variable menu.main.invite is true while the menu is open until begin(). On the web the gesture also unlocks the browser's sound. false: the entries at once.

id.description: Entry id, unique on its screen; the id of a default entry or of an entry a kit declares, on the same screen, overlays it field by field.

action.description: The genre of action the entry runs (the registry of actions; needed for a new entry).

order.description: Place in the menu, smallest first (default 0).

enabled.description: Shown but not choosable when false (default true).

hidden.description: Not shown (default false): { "id": "save", "screen": "pause", "hidden": true } turns off the entry of game.save.

label.description: The label in English; without it the asset reads its translation entry.<id>.

call.description: call: the method called, <service>.<method> of any kit.

args.description: call: the arguments of the method.

emit.description: emit: the event of the game emitted.

payload.description: emit: the payload of the event.

screen.description: The screen of the entry: title (the title screen, default) or pause (the pause panel).

entries.description: Entries laid over the default ones (title: continue, play, settings, quit; pause: resume, settings, quit) and over the entries the kits declare: a new id adds an entry to its screen, an existing id on the same screen overlays it field by field.

blockedIn.description: The contexts of game.engine's stack on top of which the pause panel refuses to open (said to the debugger).

pauseOnPointerLoss.description: In game, the pause panel opens when the host frees the cursor locked by core.input (core.input.pointer_lock.released with reason host: on the web, Escape frees the lock and the browser keeps the key). Not when a menu is open, nor in the contexts of blockedIn, nor when the cursor is freed by a kit (the menu's own context, a cursor context: another reason).

pauseEnabled.description: The pause menu is on: togglePause, the cursor freed by the host, toggle() and open("pause") open the pause panel. false: nothing opens it (refused, said to the debugger), the title screen is unchanged. Changed live by setPauseEnabled(on) (the debugger's switch « Menu pause actif »); variable menu.main.pause.enabled.

actions.description: The genres of action a game or a mod adds (registry actions), by name: { "<genre>": { as: call | emit, call?, args?, emit?, payload? } }; an entry of that genre runs as, the genre's fields under its own ("openShop": { as: call, call: "game.shop.open" }). The eight base genres are never replaced (said as a problem).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/net.authority.description: What the kit net.authority adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

kinds.description: The kinds of writer { id, rule, by?, about? }; a net.mode.* kit (registerKind at ready), the game or a mod adds one. server, the default kind, is a base entry.

role.description: `server`: this side moves the writers (a match server, a listening host, a game alone). `client`: it takes the table the server tells. `auto` (the default): from core.net's events (connected = client, serving = server; nothing = a game alone, server).

defaultKind.description: The kind of an entity the data does not name (`server` by default; a kind of a net.mode.* kit once that kit registered it).

byTag.description: The kind of the entities that carry a tag: { "player": "owner", "prop": "claim" }. The first tag of the list an entity carries wins.

byEntity.description: The kind of named entities (the objects a scene places on both sides): { "crate": "claim" }; over byTag.

kinds.description: Kinds a game adds by data: { "<id>": { rule: server|host|owner|managed, by?, about? } } (registry kinds).

onOwnerLeave.description: What the server does with the entities a peer wrote when it leaves: `revert` (back to the server, where they are) or `destroy`.

netService.description: The service that carries the table (channel, send, receive, status).

channelPriority.description: The priority of the channel net.authority in core.net's byte budget.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/net.mode.claim.description: What the kit net.mode.claim adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

leaseMs.description: A holder silent this long (no state, no keep-alive) loses its entities: back to the server.

stickyMs.description: Minimum hold before another peer may take an entity (anti ping-pong).

maxHoldMs.description: Longest hold of one claim (0: none); the hook net.mode.claim.request may change it per claim.

reclaimMs.description: A claim without an answer is sent again after this long.

stealPolicy.description: A claim on an entity another peer holds: never (the first keeps it), priority (a strictly higher priority takes it), always (the latest takes it).

maxClaimsPerPeer.description: Entities one peer may hold at once.

maxPriority.description: The highest priority a claim may ask (above: denied priority).

optimistic.description: A client drives what it claimed at once, before the answer; denied, it gives the hand back (driving).

sleepKeyframeMs.description: A holder keeps its entities alive this often even when it publishes nothing (0: min(1000, leaseMs / 3)); below leaseMs.

autoClaimRadius.description: Client: claims the entities tagged autoClaimTag within this distance of the player (0: only explicit claims); gives them back beyond releaseFactor × the radius.

releaseFactor.description: The automatic claim gives back beyond the radius × this.

autoClaimTag.description: The tag of what the automatic claim may take.

playerTag.description: The tag of the local player's entity (the centre of the automatic claim).

autoClaimEvery.description: The automatic claim looks every this many ticks.

antiCheat.description: The server checks what a holder publishes (observe): speed, angular speed; false trusts the holders (the world limit stays).

maxSpeed.description: Plausibility: highest speed of a published entity (m/s, 0: off).

maxAngularSpeed.description: Plausibility: highest angular speed per axis (rad/s).

plausibilitySlack.description: Plausibility: tolerance factor on maxSpeed (jitter, bursts).

plausibilityMarginM.description: Plausibility: distance always allowed on top (m).

plausibilityMinDtMs.description: Plausibility: the elapsed time counts at least this (two states arriving together).

netService.description: The service that carries the claims (channel, send, receive).

channelPriority.description: The priority of the channel net.mode.claim in core.net's byte budget.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/net.rooms.description: What the kit net.rooms adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

role.description: `client`: the lobby. `server`: a match server launched by the rooms service. `host`: a native client that also serves the match, with no service (host(spec)). `auto` (the default): server when a launch is given (`launch`, or the variable `launchVar`), else client.

service.description: The base address of the rooms service (https://rooms.example.org). Empty: relative addresses, the engine resolves them against its own origin (a web page served by the service); setService changes it live.

socketPath.description: The path of the service's WebSocket (room.* messages), opened when the client enters a room or the queue.

autoConnect.description: Whether the ticket and the addresses are handed to core.net (connect) as soon as the service says the match is ready. Off: the game connects from net.rooms.ready.

netService.description: The service asked to connect, listen, sign an invitation (issueTicket) and drop a refused peer (kick).

context.description: The context of game.engine pushed while the lobby is open (queued, in a room, starting); empty: none.

report.description: How a match server tells the rooms service: one line per report on the standard output (GF_NET_READY, GF_NET_MATCH_END… as the launcher reads them), or only the event net.rooms.report (an engine that sends it its own way). The event is told in both cases.

launch.description: The launch of a match server given in data (tests, a game that reads it its own way): { match, room, mode, seats: [{ seat, player }], ticketKey, listen, endpoints, tls, config, heartbeatSeconds }. Null: the variable `launchVar`.

launchVar.description: The environment variable naming the match config file the launcher writes (native only: a web page has no environment); its `launch` is read.

heartbeatSeconds.description: Seconds between two heartbeats of a match server (0: none; the launch's own heartbeatSeconds goes over it).

endWhenEmptySeconds.description: A begun match left with no player this long ends with the result { abandoned: true }; 0 (the default): never, the game decides.

inviteSeconds.description: How long an invitation of a listening host is valid (the ticket's expiry).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

gripforge.kit/net.state.title: net.state in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/net.state.description: What the kit net.state adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

syncModes.description: The sync modes: snapshot (runs in net.state), predict and rollback (built in, run once net.mode.predict or net.mode.rollback provides them): the base, never removed. A game or a mod adds its own on a base that runs, in the config key syncModes (registered at ready) or with registerSync at run time; the config key sync names the mode by default.

sync.description: The sync mode by default (registry of net.state): snapshot; predict and rollback come with net.mode.predict and net.mode.rollback, a game's mode with registerSync.

authority.description: Who writes by default: server (the only kind without net.authority; host and owner come with net.authority, claim with net.mode.claim).

tag.description: The tag of the entities the server replicates (game.engine's tags).

components.description: The components of a replicated entity that travel beside its pose, sent when they change, applied by steps; by default game.engine.state, its stored states (game.engine never writes a derived one there). Never a derived component.

columns.description: The columns of the shared zone (the entity's variables, read and written in place) that travel beside its pose; the game schema must let net.state write them on the clients. Never a derived column.

replicate.description: What is replicated: the stored pose (x, y, z, yaw) of the tagged entities, and beside it the components and columns named here (stored state only: never a derived one).

sendEvery.description: Server: a frame to each peer every this many action ticks.

delayTicks.description: Client: how far behind the newest tick the play head runs (room for late and lost frames).

keyframeEvery.description: Server: a full frame each this many frames to a peer (0: only when no acknowledged base is held).

history.description: The views kept per peer (server) and received (client), in ticks: an acknowledgement older than that gives a full frame.

kind.description: all: every replicated entity to every peer; radius: those within radius of the entity the peer follows (focus).

radius.description: Metres, on the ground plane.

interest.description: Which entities each peer receives; the hook net.state.relevant decides case by case.

quant.description: The quantization of a pose on the wire; both sides must use the same (a frame of another codec is refused).

syncModes.description: The sync modes a game or a mod adds (registry syncModes), by id: { "<id>": { base } } or { "<id>": "<base>" } (base: snapshot by default, or predict and rollback once their net.mode.* kit provides them: the mode waits for it). Registered at ready, before the default mode sync is checked, as registerSync does at run time.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of net.state (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/render.lod.title: render.lod in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/render.lod.description: What the kit render.lod adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The genres of objects by id, in data (config genres.<id>, registerGenre): how far each level reaches (distances or screen sizes), the cull distance, the band, the transition. A kit, a mod or the game adds its own or changes one field by field.

passports.description: Read the kits.lod section of each entity's passport (asset.meta): the trigger of LOD. Off: only the entities given in code (manage, managed) are managed.

interval.description: Ticks between two choices of levels (a level never changes faster than this; the render side plays the transition between).

bias.description: Multiplies every threshold, on top of the quality setting: above 1 the fine levels reach farther. The developer's knob; the player's is the render.lod.quality setting.

fov.description: Vertical field of view (degrees) the screen metric assumes.

defaultGenre.description: The genre of an object whose passport names none.

transition.description: How the render side goes from a level to the next, interpolated at the render (never at the tick): instant, fade (cross-fade) or dither (screen-door cross-fade, the engines' own when they have one). A genre may carry its own.

keepFollowedFull.description: The followed character always shows its finest level (LOD is for the other copies). Off: it is chosen like the others.

followPlayer.description: The entity tagged player is followed.

followed.description: Entity ids followed besides the player (kept at full detail).

managed.description: Entities managed without a passport: [{ entity, asset, levels: [part | { part }], genre, radius, distances }] (the passport is an optional initial state).

additionalProperties.description: A genre of object, field by field; a field left out falls through to registerGenre, then to the built-in genre (logic/genres.json), then to the code's default.

genres.description: Genres of the game by id, merged field by field over the built-in ones (prop, character, vegetation, vehicle, structure, screen) and those of registerGenre (the config has the last word).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

gripforge.kit/render.mesh_transform.title: render.mesh_transform in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/render.mesh_transform.description: What the kit render.mesh_transform adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

deformGenres.description: The genres of transformation an impact names: notch, hollow, hole (the kit's, base, never removed), then those a game or a mod gives in the config key deformGenres (taken over the kit's of the same name).

techniques.description: The techniques that apply a genre, by name: their appliers { render?, physics? } (a service method each, asked with the job), given in the config key techniques or registered with registerTechnique (an engine adapter, a game).

maxImpactsPerPart.description: Impacts alive on one part at most; over it, the oldest alive starts its fade (whichever kit asked for it).

impactLife.description: Seconds an impact lives before its fade, turned into ticks with the tick of game.engine (below 0: until removeImpact).

impactFade.description: Seconds an impact takes to go, evaluated at the render.

defaultTechnique.description: The technique of a genre that names none (a genre with a negative depth, a bump, is always displaced: carve only removes matter).

fallbackTechnique.description: The technique a carve impact takes when carve cannot run (core.material absent), said once by render.mesh_transform.refused { reason: "carve_unavailable" }.

deformGenres.description: The genres of transformation by name (registry deformGenres): { technique?, radius?, depth?, life? (seconds), fade?, lodLevels?, lodMaxLevel?, applyTo?, …fields the technique reads }; each one given here is taken over the kit's of the same name (notch, hollow, bump, crush, hole: base, kept when the game writes others).

targets.description: Which parts take which genres, and their options: [{ tags?, entity?, parts?, genres?, lodLevels?, lodMaxLevel?, applyTo? }]; empty: every part takes every genre.

lodLevels.description: The levels of detail a transformation touches: a level (number N: levels 0 to N; or its name in kits.lod.levels of the passport: up to it), an array of levels (exactly those), or -1 (every level). Read in the cascade: the impact, its genre, targets[], this config, configs["*"], then 0.

lodMaxLevel.description: The coarsest level allowed to the entity while an impact lives (a number or a name of the passport); absent: render.lod chooses alone. Same cascade.

applyTo.description: The targets: "render", "physics" or both. The physics target goes only through the physics applier of the technique (registerTechnique); the kit depends on no physics. Same cascade.

techniques.description: The techniques a game or a mod names (registry techniques), by name: { render?: "service.method", physics?: "service.method" }, registered at setup as registerTechnique does at run time.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of render.mesh_transform (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/render.post.title: render.post in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/render.post.description: What the kit render.post adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

level.description: The quality level of the effects. auto: the player's setting render.post.level (core.settings, which follows the mode of settings.graphics), low when it is not loaded. On the web the look of the image is drawn: colour grading (low and above), vignette (medium), film grain (high).

tonemapping.description: The tone curve (level: the profile's, AgX). agx, tonyMcMapface and blenderFilmic need the lookup tables of the Bevy build (tonemapping_luts); without them the curve is aces and the fallback is said.

tune.description: Numbers moved over the level's (the same as the service tune): bloomIntensity, volumetricDensity, mistHeight, aoRadius, aoThickness, evMax, exposureOffset (EV before the tone curve), contrast, saturation. A value past its range is brought into it.

tables.description: The player of the game carries the lookup tables of the AgX, TonyMcMapface and Blender filmic curves (its build has the Bevy feature tonemapping_luts). The game says it, the kit cannot see the build; false: those curves fall back to ACES, said.

disabled.description: Effects turned off whatever the level (the false bits of settings.graphics' effects come here): never turned on above the level.

context.description: What the frame is for. game: depth of field off, or very light at ultra; cinematic and photo: depth of field strong, the focus distance and the aperture coming from the shot.

profiles.description: Profiles over kits/render_post/data/profiles.json, by level: { "high": { "bloomIntensity": 0.2, "dofShot": { "mode": "gaussian", "aperture": 2, "maxCoc": 40 } } }. A value not written is the shipped one.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of render.post (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/render.scoped_display.title: render.scoped_display in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/render.scoped_display.description: What the kit render.scoped_display adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The genres of display by id, in data (config genres.<id>, defineGenre): a kit, a mod or the game adds its own or changes one field by field.

The genres of display by id (the registry `genres`): { <id>: { distance, fade, mode, priority, always, sleep, radius } }. distance: metres beyond which the object is not drawn (0: no limit); fade: metres over which it fades out before it; mode: alpha or dither; priority: higher kept first when a view's budget is full; always: never hidden by distance, budget nor context; sleep: metres beyond which a drawn object is refreshed less (0: never); radius: of its bounding sphere. Empty (the default) and no passport section nor display component: nothing is managed, everything is drawn as the engine draws it.

tags.description: A tag or a kind of entity → the genre of the entities that carry it ({ "crate": "prop" }); the first tag found wins, then the kind.

scenes.description: The rules of a scene of game.engine, laid over the genres while it is the current scene: { <scene>: { genres: { <genre>: <rule> }, budget } }.

component.description: The component of an entity that carries the rule of its node in the scene tree (`{ genre, distance, … }`, written by the scene file or the game), laid over its genre and its scene's rule.

followed.description: The tags of the followed character(s): never hidden, never put to sleep.

budget.description: Objects a view draws at most (0: no budget). A scene's or a view's own budget goes over it.

margin.description: Metres an object hidden by distance must come back within before it shows again (no flicker at the edge). Also the default margin of isVisible: a box out of the pyramid but within this many metres of it is at the edge.

hideDelay.description: Seconds what leaves the visible stays visible before it is hidden: an object leaving the camera's field or its distance waits this long before its fade, and a box of isVisible stays visible this long after it left (by its id). A camera going back and forth changes nothing. isVisible takes its own in its options.

poseStep.description: Metres (and the same in tenths of a radian of turn) the camera moves before the render side gives its pose again (report): the pose isVisible sees, said rarely.

fadeSeconds.description: Seconds an object the budget or a context hides (or brings back) takes to fade, at the render (0: at once). The distance fade is the engines' own, in metres (a genre's `fade`).

distanceScale.description: The scale of every display distance: the value of the player's setting render.scoped_display.distance (core.settings, settings.graphics' presets) when core.settings is loaded, else this one.

views.description: The views (one per camera that draws): [{ id, budget, contexts, inactive }]. contexts: the contexts of game.engine it shows in (a name, a list or "all", the default); inactive: what it does out of them, `hold` (keeps its last decisions, the default), `show` (everything) or `hide` (everything but the followed character). Empty: one view `main`, in every context.

reportSeconds.description: Seconds between two counts the render side gives back (`report`, for the debugger): rare, never per frame.

areas.description: The display areas declared as primitive blocks (gripforge.display-areas/1): { <id>: { shape: box | polygon | none, center, size, rotation | points, bottom, top, members: [<entity> | "part:<entity>/<node or glTF scene name>"], priority } }. A view shows the area its eye is in and the areas reached through open links up to `depth`; an entity member of areas none of which is reached is hidden through game.engine's shared property `hidden` (this kit's contribution, reason `area`; a part through its bound node). A scene of game.engine adds its own (`data.displayAreas`, and `data.displayArea`: the scene itself as an area, its instances as members); the code lays `setArea` over both. Empty everywhere: no area filter.

links.description: The links between display areas: { <id>: { a, b, state: open | closed | always } } (`outside`: whatever is in no area). `always`: a bay window, an opening without a door.

depth.description: Links crossed at most from the area of the view's eye (0: its area only).

eye.description: Whose area a view shows: the camera's (the default) or the followed character's.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of render.scoped_display (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

hidden.description: Hidden in play while any kit hides it (game.engine's shared property, docs/decisions/contributions.md): this kit lays its contribution (reason area) on an entity whose display areas are all out of reach, and withdraws it when one comes back.

gripforge.kit/settings.graphics.title: settings.graphics in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/settings.graphics.description: What the kit settings.graphics adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

profiles.description: The profiles by name; a game or a mod changes one (config profiles.<name>).

platforms.description: The platforms by id with their caps; a game or a mod changes one (config platforms.<id>).

platform.description: The platform whose caps apply. auto: the host says (a page on WebGL2 or WebGPU, a phone, a computer).

profile.description: The profile the game picks (layer 3). auto: none, the platform and the detection decide.

targetFps.description: The frame rate the game aims at; the adaptive quality reads it.

ceiling.description: The highest profile the platform default and the detection may give (the game choice; the player choice is free).

settings.description: Values the game sets over the profile (layer 3), by the names of a profile (renderScale, antialiasing, shadows, effects...). The player overrules them.

detect.description: The detection of the first launch (settings.graphics.detect): the GPU name gives the start, a calibration after the loading corrects it.

base.description: Every value before any profile. Moddable.

profiles.description: The profiles by name: levels and factors, never a value of one engine. A game or a mod changes one (config profiles.<name>).

platforms.description: The platforms by id: the profile a first launch gets and the caps (what the target cannot do: a request over a cap is brought back and said).

adaptive.description: The adaptive quality (settings.graphics.adaptive). auto: whether it runs in each mode when the player leaves it on auto (the default: on in low and medium, off in high and ultra; the player forces on or off with the setting settings.graphics.adaptive). levers: the least visible first, each a list of settings (by id) or categories of the group graphics; one step takes one lever one mode down, each kit saying what that mode means for it. measure: the sliding window of the frame times, its quantile against the target frame rate, how long a lateness lasts before a step down, the margin and time before a step up, the settling after a step.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of settings.graphics (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/settings.input.title: settings.input in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/settings.input.description: What the kit settings.input adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

schemes.description: The schemes of controls the player picks from: config schemes (the defaults without it), code (addScheme, removeScheme), the hook settings.input.scheme before one is applied. A scheme swaps controls (keys, sticks) from the game's controls, or gives exact values.

devices.description: The devices the editor shows, one page each: the slots of core.input.remap it edits, whether the sticks, or a page of settings of core.settings (touch). Config devices (keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch without it).

context.description: The context the editor declares (game.engine, and core.input: exclusive, free cursor) and pushes while it is open, over the settings screen's.

lang.description: The language of the editor's labels; empty: core.settings' language, else the platform's.

slots.description: The slots of core.input.remap this device edits (none for a page of settings).

sticks.description: Shows the stick rows (source, inversion, dead zone).

kit.description: The kit that declares these settings; without it loaded the page has no tab and its view says why (unavailable: missing). Empty: always shown.

categories.description: The categories of that group shown (empty: all of them).

settings.description: A page of settings instead of bindings: the settings of core.settings in this group and these categories, with their value, set through core.settings (never stored here).

devices.description: The devices the editor shows (a registry): which slots and whether the sticks, or a page of settings (settings). Default: keyboard and mouse (primary, secondary), gamepad (pad, sticks), touch (the settings of input.virtual_joypad: display, size, opacity, side; shown only when that kit is loaded).

tabs.description: The tabs of the editor: all (one table of every device's bindings, the default) or device (a tab per device of slots); then a tab per page of settings whose kit is loaded.

stickThreshold.description: While a stick row waits, how far a stick is pushed (a fraction of its full tilt, from where it rested when the capture began) for the asset to take it.

keys.description: Controls swapped both ways from the game's controls, { "KeyW": "ArrowUp" }: a generic layout that fits any game.

values.description: Exact values of core.input.remap ({ rows, sticks }) over the game's controls, for a scheme made for one game.

schemes.description: The schemes of controls the player picks from (a registry, in the setting settings.input.scheme): the game's controls, arrows for WASD, sticks swapped. Picking one puts its bindings in place of the player's.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of settings.input (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/story.cinematic.title: story.cinematic in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/story.cinematic.description: What the kit story.cinematic adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

kinds.description: The kinds of step a cinematic plays: the kit's (camera.play, camera.stop, camera.look, control.claim, control.release, letterbox, fade, title.show, title.hide, subtitle.show, subtitle.hide, hud.film, audio.play, audio.stop, audio.bus, voice.play, light.preset, post.focus, dialogue.start, anim.state, state, layer, actions, shot, and the conductor's names audio.duck, mix.bus, say, voice.stop, subtitle.clear) and the game's (config kinds, a mod or registerKind).

cinematics.description: The cinematics: [{ id, duration, steps (or events): [{ t, do, args, wait }], cleanup: [steps run at the end and after a skip], skippable (true, false or { on, fadeSeconds }), scene (the scene whose entry plays it), once, handover (seconds of the blend back to the game's camera), shots (game.cinematic's shots: { id, duration, from, to, target, targetTo, space (world, player), fov, endFov, easing, title, caption, actors: [{ id, anim, layer, priority }] }) }]. A wrong cinematic is refused with its reason.

kinds.description: The game's kinds of step, by name: { actions: [game.engine verbs, "$arg" replaced by the step's argument] }, { emit: topic }, { call: { service, method } } or { as: another kind, args: defaults }. Overrides a kit's kind of the same name.

scenes.description: { scene id: cinematic id }: the cinematic a scene entry plays (as the cinematic's own `scene`).

autoplay.description: A cinematic played at the first scene entry (game.cinematic's autoplay); `intro` with no `intro` authored plays game.cinematic's default introduction (three shots around the player). Empty: none.

context.description: The context of game.engine's stack pushed while a cinematic plays (declared first).

contexts.description: The contexts the cinematic plays in: its own, and those it lets over it (a dialogue it opens). Out of them `outOfContext` applies.

outOfContext.description: What the cinematic does while a context out of `contexts` is on top (a menu, the debugger): freeze (its clock stands) or continue.

once.description: A cinematic plays once per game (saved), unless played with { replay: true } or its own `once` says otherwise.

handover.description: Seconds of the blend from the cinematic camera's last pose back to the game's camera, at the end.

skipFade.description: Seconds of the fade to black of a skip (a cinematic's skippable.fadeSeconds wins).

hideHud.description: The view says hideHud while a cinematic plays (the game's HUD hides; step hud.film changes it).

camera.description: The name of the cinematic camera story.cinematic makes in core.camera, heard only in the cinematic's context.

hero.description: The entity control.claim takes when the step names none (else the player).

speech.description: audio.speech: its service, its method and the topic of its end ({ service, say, ended }).

voiceBus.description: The bus of core.audio the voices play on.

fastSpeed.description: The rate of the clock while fast(true) holds it (the game binds its held action to fast: pressed true, released false).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of story.cinematic (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/story.dialogue.title: story.dialogue in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/story.dialogue.description: What the kit story.dialogue adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

kinds.description: The kinds of dialogue (conversation, ambient, radio, bark): the defaults of mode, advance, reveal and linger a dialogue of the kind takes. Added by the config (kinds), a mod or registerKind.

dialogues.description: The dialogues: [{ id, kind, mode (blocking, free), advance (input, auto), reveal (letters, all), start, lines (a list, or a map by id: { speaker, text (a string or one by language), voice (a sound of core.audio's bank, or one by language), duration, next, if, else, effects, choices: [{ text, if, effects, next }], mode, advance, reveal, waitVoice, emotion, lookAt }), speakers ({ id: { name, portrait, entity } }), camera (fields of a takeover of the camera), onEnd }]. A wrong dialogue is said and refused, never corrected.

kinds.description: Kinds of dialogue added or overridden: { name: { mode, advance, reveal, linger } } over the shipped ones (conversation, ambient, radio, bark).

defaultKind.description: The kind of a dialogue that names none.

speakers.description: Speakers shared by every dialogue: { id: { name (one by language), portrait, entity } }.

language.description: The language of the game: the fallback of the texts and the voices, and the language when the player chose none.

context.description: The context of game.engine a blocking line pushes.

readingSpeed.description: Letters per second a line without a voice and without a duration lasts.

minSeconds.description: The shortest line without a voice.

bus.description: The bus of core.audio the voices play on (when audio.speech is not there).

showDisabled.description: Shows the choices whose condition is false, disabled, instead of hiding them.

defaultChoice.description: The choice a free line takes at its end.

speech.description: The kit that says the lines: its service, its method say(speaker, line) (it returns the id of the line) and the topic of its end ({ speaker, line }). An empty service: core.audio only.

subtitles.description: The default of the subtitles setting.

textSize.description: The default of the text size setting (small, medium, large, huge).

textSpeed.description: The default of the text speed setting, letters per second (0: at once).

autoAdvance.description: The default of the auto-advance setting.

textLanguage.description: The default of the text language setting (empty: language).

voiceLanguage.description: The default of the voice language setting (empty: language).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of story.dialogue (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/story.quest.title: story.quest in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/story.quest.description: What the kit story.quest adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

quests.description: The quests: data (collection quests), config, code (define, patch), mods (the collection), scenes (elements); each overridable field by field, with its origins.

steps.description: The step genres over six bases: built-in, declared in the config steps, added in code (registerStep).

categories.description: The categories of quests (main, side, daily, tutorial, hidden, technical by default): visibility, order, label; config categories, code registerCategory.

title.description: Title (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

description.description: What the quest is about, in the journal (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

flow.description: One objective after the other (default) or all at once.

id.description: Objective id, unique in its quest.

type.description: A genre of the steps registry: wait, event, go_to, escape_zone, interact, condition, or a declared one (kill, collect, talk, script, or the game's).

label.description: What the player reads (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

optional.description: A failed optional objective is skipped (story.quest.objective.skipped), not the quest.

count.description: event genres: how many matching events (default 1).

visible.description: Shown to the player; wins over the quest and its category.

entity.description: An entity reference of game.engine (id, instance, tag).

label.description: What a marker says (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

targets.description: Spatial targets of the objective while it is armed (reach, escort, markers).

entity.description: escort: the entity to bring to a target.

range.description: escort: how far from the player the entity may be (default 10).

grace.description: escort: seconds the entity may stay out of range before the objective fails (default 5).

conditions.description: Conditions of game.engine's script language: start (all must hold to start), fail and abort (any, read at the tick).

actions.description: Actions of game.engine's script language; a verb another kit registers is written { type: <verb>, … } and must exist when the game loads.

category.description: A category of the registry (default: defaultCategory).

visible.description: Shown to the player (journal, HUD, markers); wins over the category.

entity.description: An entity reference of game.engine (id, instance, tag).

label.description: What a marker says (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

targets.description: Spatial targets of the quest while it runs.

requires.description: Graph: what the quest waits for before it can start, all of it: a quest id (that quest completed) or a condition of game.engine's script language ({ var, op, value }, { type: story.quest.is, … }); read when a run starts or ends and when the quest is asked to start.

locked.description: Graph: the quest waits for an unlock (unlock, the verb story.quest.unlock). A quest that another quest or a branch unlocks waits for it without this field.

unlocks.description: Graph: the quests unlocked when this one completes (their requires still count).

excludes.description: Graph: the quests closed when this one starts, and the other way round (an exclusion goes both ways); a closed quest never starts, a running one is aborted.

id.description: Branch id, unique in its quest.

label.description: What the player reads (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

when.description: A condition of game.engine's script language: at the end, the first branch whose when holds is taken (a branch without when always holds).

choice.description: Taken only when chosen (choose, the verb story.quest.choose), never by itself.

branches.description: Graph: the ways the quest goes on at its end: the one chosen before (choose), else the first whose when holds; the hook story.quest.choose settles it. None taken: choose after the end takes one.

quests.description: Quests declared in the config (origin config), beside the data collection quests.

steps.description: Step genres: { id: { base, defaults, label } }; the defaults are kill, collect, talk and script.

maxActive.description: How many quests may run at once (0: no limit); a start beyond is refused with a log.

autoTrack.description: A quest that starts becomes the tracked one (the variables story.quest.* describe it).

categories.description: Categories of quests: { id: { visible (shown in the journal and the HUD by default), order, label (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… }) } }.

defaultCategory.description: The category of a quest that names none.

language.description: The language the texts are written in: the one shown when a table { en, fr… } lacks the player's, and the player's language when neither setLanguage nor core.i18n says one.

context.description: The context of game.engine's stack the open journal pushes (declared by the kit).

journal.description: The quest journal: { context } (the game binds its journal action to toggleJournal / closeJournal: the kit hears no action of core.input). Open, it pushes its context (the moves of the game stop listening, the world keeps running) and story.quest.journal.open is true.

title.description: Title (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

description.description: What the quest is about, in the journal (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

flow.description: One objective after the other (default) or all at once.

id.description: Objective id, unique in its quest.

type.description: A genre of the steps registry: wait, event, go_to, escape_zone, interact, condition, or a declared one (kill, collect, talk, script, or the game's).

label.description: What the player reads (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

optional.description: A failed optional objective is skipped (story.quest.objective.skipped), not the quest.

count.description: event genres: how many matching events (default 1).

visible.description: Shown to the player; wins over the quest and its category.

entity.description: An entity reference of game.engine (id, instance, tag).

label.description: What a marker says (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

targets.description: Spatial targets of the objective while it is armed (reach, escort, markers).

entity.description: escort: the entity to bring to a target.

range.description: escort: how far from the player the entity may be (default 10).

grace.description: escort: seconds the entity may stay out of range before the objective fails (default 5).

conditions.description: Conditions of game.engine's script language: start (all must hold to start), fail and abort (any, read at the tick).

actions.description: Actions of game.engine's script language; a verb another kit registers is written { type: <verb>, … } and must exist when the game loads.

category.description: A category of the registry (default: defaultCategory).

visible.description: Shown to the player (journal, HUD, markers); wins over the category.

entity.description: An entity reference of game.engine (id, instance, tag).

label.description: What a marker says (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

targets.description: Spatial targets of the quest while it runs.

requires.description: Graph: what the quest waits for before it can start, all of it: a quest id (that quest completed) or a condition of game.engine's script language ({ var, op, value }, { type: story.quest.is, … }); read when a run starts or ends and when the quest is asked to start.

locked.description: Graph: the quest waits for an unlock (unlock, the verb story.quest.unlock). A quest that another quest or a branch unlocks waits for it without this field.

unlocks.description: Graph: the quests unlocked when this one completes (their requires still count).

excludes.description: Graph: the quests closed when this one starts, and the other way round (an exclusion goes both ways); a closed quest never starts, a running one is aborted.

id.description: Branch id, unique in its quest.

label.description: What the player reads (an core.i18n key preferably, or a table { en, fr… } by language: shown in the player's language).

when.description: A condition of game.engine's script language: at the end, the first branch whose when holds is taken (a branch without when always holds).

choice.description: Taken only when chosen (choose, the verb story.quest.choose), never by itself.

branches.description: Graph: the ways the quest goes on at its end: the one chosen before (choose), else the first whose when holds; the hook story.quest.choose settles it. None taken: choose after the end takes one.

Empty (the default): the kit has no clock and rests.

drive.description: Whether a clock with an ambience also applies its stops through the service of core.light (applyPreset). Off by default: the kit publishes the hour, the phase and the stop, and whoever listens (core.light, the audio, a hook of the game) reacts. A clock's own `drive` goes over this one.

gripforge.kit/world.natural.title: world.natural in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/world.natural.description: What the kit world.natural adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The genres the kit generates besides the meadow, by id (config genres.<id>, registerGenre): rock built in (off); a kit, a mod or the game adds its own in data (pebbles, boulders), never in code.

density.description: Tufts per square metre on open ground.

maxCount.description: Ceiling of tufts drawn (the grid is thinned evenly beyond it).

size.description: Side of the ground, metres; 0: 400 on a terrain, else 200 (no ground kit: 1.8).

seed.description: Seed of the placement: the same seed always gives the same meadow.

clearance.description: Metres kept free on each side of a route.

bank.description: Metres kept free along the water.

routes.description: Routes kept free of grass, as lanes.routes gives them: [{ points: [[x, z], ...] }] (two points at least); the path of a level without a routes kit (1.8, from gm-3 MOT-093 step 2).

dirt.description: The bare-earth mask of the ground the meadow follows: n x n bytes over `size` metres centred on the origin (row = z, column = x), 255 = bare earth. Tufts thin out from `from` to `to` (bare share) and are shorter by up to `shrink`. The room computes it once from its data and gives the same numbers to its ground shader (1.9).

lakes.description: Lakes the game declares in data when it has no world.water: [{ at: [x, z], radius }]. The meadow keeps off them and their bank, a genre with water near grows on their shore (2.3, name provisional).

clearings.description: Clearings kept free of grass, as world.clearings gives them: [{ at: [x, z], radius }] (1.8, from gm-3 MOT-093 step 2). A thicket still grows in them.

ground.description: Where the tufts stand without a terrain (1.8): plane (on groundY), physics (the height core.physics answers under each tuft, asked by ticket; a tuft over nothing or on a slope over 40 degrees is dropped), auto (physics when core.physics is in the game, else plane).

groundY.description: Height of the given plane, metres; on physics, the rays start 200 m above it and reach 400 m under it.

height.description: Height of a tuft, metres (thickets are half as tall again).

bladeCount.description: Curved blades per procedural tuft; authored texture cards are unchanged.

bladeSegments.description: Segments per curved blade, including its tapered tip.

lodDistance.description: Read by develop's density levels of detail; the player module of 1.8 draws three geometric levels (84 / 40 / 9 triangles per tuft, at 10 and 20 m) and does not read it.

softShading.description: Upright normals, linear root-to-tip gradient and matte leaves, without artificial root darkening.

variationScale.description: Repeats of the dry-patch texture per world metre.

dryColor.description: Dry tip colour for soft shading; stable broad patches blend it with tipColor.

transmission.description: Native diffuse light transmission; requires host MATERIAL_OPTICS support.

broadWind.description: Advected broad gusts with fine flutter instead of the detailed leaf sway.

windAngle.description: Broad wind direction in radians in the XZ plane (the way the blades lean). With world.weather loaded the presentation follows the direction of world.weather.wind() instead.

wind.description: Sway strength; 0 stops the wind, character contacts still bend the blades. With world.weather loaded the presentation scales it by the speed of world.weather.wind() (0.35 in a calm, 1 at 5 m/s, up to 2 from 10 m/s).

interaction.description: Bend the grass visually around the bodies moving in it (the player, the characters, every body of the physics that is not fixed, entities with world.natural.bend), in the vertex shader; no physics force or persistent gameplay track. false: nothing bends.

interactionBodies.description: The bodies of the physics that are not fixed (dynamic, kinematic) bend the grass with nothing declared: read in place from the shape table of core.physics when its set changes, at their drawn pose; radius from the widest half of their box on the ground, contact at the bottom of the box (a body above the blades bends nothing). At most 16 bodies, the nearest to the eye first.

interactionExclude.description: Kinds that never bend the grass: an entity kind, a tag, or a kind of body (dynamic, kinematic).

interactionPlayer.description: The player bends the grass without declaring anything (its transform as the host gives it every frame). The optional component world.natural.bend { radius, strength, offset, enabled } forces, adjusts or (enabled: false) turns off the bend of an entity.

interactionRadius.description: Metres around the player, and around a body declaring world.natural.bend without a radius, within which the grass bends.

interactionStrength.description: Factor on how far the grass bends (a body's own strength multiplies it); 0 bends nothing.

lodFadeSeconds.description: Seconds a square of the meadow takes to cross-fade from one level of detail to the next, leaf by leaf (no popping); 0 switches at once.

recoverySeconds.description: Seconds for recent contacts to straighten after the body left or moved on (a body standing still keeps its stroke held); bounded to sixteen contact segments.

fadeDistance.description: Metres from the camera beyond which the grass fades out.

thickets.description: Taller, denser grass in the stealth or bush zones the world declares (world.thickets).

coverage.description: Share of the meadow that shows at the start; coverage(share) changes it while playing (grass that spreads or dies back).

everywhere.description: On a terrain, grow on any ground layer (sand, rock, snow), not only on grass, meadow and moss.

genres.description: The other genres than the meadow by id (registry genres, docs/design/world-natural.md), field by field over the built-in ones (rock) and over registerGenre: enabled (false: never generated nor drawn), density (per 100 m2), maxCount, sizeMin, sizeMax, cluster (smaller ones around each, 0 to 8), clusterRadius, variants (procedural shapes, 1 to 32), roughness, flatten, layers (terrain layers it grows on, empty: any), color, colorVariation, sink. Kept off the routes, clearings and water like the meadow; the same seed gives the same elements. 2.3 (names PROVISIONAL, to settle with Damien): shape (stone, or a plant made by code: reed, flower, clover, mushroom, leaf), water (avoid, the default: off the water and its bank; near: only on the shore, from waterInto metres inside to waterReach metres outside; any), routeMargin (metres kept clear beyond the clearance of the routes), patchScale (metres across) with patchCover (share of the ground, 0 to 1) and patchColors (one dominant palette colour per patch) to grow in patches, and for the drawing palette (up to 8 #rrggbb, read by the tint of each element: petals, caps, leaves, seed heads), tipColor, heartColor, wind (0 none, about 0.5 a breeze), drawDistance (metres from the eye past which its squares are not drawn, 0 all).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

gripforge.kit/world.scenery.title: world.scenery in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/world.scenery.description: What the kit world.scenery adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

seed.description: Seed of the placement: the same seed always gives the same pieces at the same places.

size.description: Side of the square of ground placed on, metres, centred on the origin. 0: the relief of world.terrain (info().relief.size), else 100.

groundY.description: Height of the ground without world.terrain (with it, each piece stands on heightAt).

layers.description: What to place: [{ slot, mode: scatter | line | volumes, height, clearance, gap, count?, cluster?, vary?, openings?, volumes? }]. Empty (the default): cliffs, trees, rocks, bushes and flowers on the slots scenery_cliff, scenery_tree, scenery_rock, scenery_bush, scenery_flower.

keep.description: Ground left free of scattered and line pieces: discs { at: [x, z], radius } or boxes { at, size: [width, depth], yaw }.

routes.description: Routes the scatter keeps clear and the line layers run along: [{ points: [[x, z], …] }]. Added to those of lanes.routes when a kit serves it.

clearings.description: Clearings kept free: [{ at: [x, z], radius }] (bases, camps, buildings). Added to those of world.clearings when a kit serves it.

coverage.description: Share of the pieces shown at start.

placeUnbound.description: Place a layer even when its slot has no model bound on the kit side (a game that binds its models on the drawing side only). Off: a slot without a model places nothing.
