gripforge.kit/world.sky.title: world.sky in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/world.sky.description: What the kit world.sky adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

hour.description: The hour the sky shows at start (the game moves it with setHour; world.clock will drive it once it is in the base).

layers.description: The layers the game declares, drawn in order: [{ id, genre, enabled, params }]. Genre `backdrop`: params { skies: { <id>: { image, sun: { azimuth, elevation }, horizon } }, stops: [{ id, hour, sky, preset, skyIntensity, sunIntensity }] } over the `backdrop` defaults. Genre `gradient` (2.2.0, lot 2 of the astres): the sky computed from the height of the sun, drawn by the kit's own dome; params over the `gradient` defaults. Empty (the default): the kit shows nothing and asks nothing.

backdrop.description: The numbers of a backdrop layer when its params leave them out: the brightness of a picture without a preset (cd/m²), the share of its light on the scene, the slow turn (degrees a second, 0: still) and its blend period, the dim before a swap (seconds, share of the brightness) and the fade of the new stop's preset.

lightService.description: The service that makes and blends the sky's pictures and light (core.light).

bodies.description: The bodies of the sky the game declares (names provisional). One is drawn so far: the sun, { id, kind: "star", motion: { mode: "day" }, light: { role: "main", intensity (lux at full height), tint: "atmosphere" | { horizonFade, color, horizonColor, warmUntil } } }: each tick its direction, colour and strength are computed from the hour of the clock and written in place in the live values of core.light's main directional light (no call, no JSON); at rest while the hour does not move. Another body is said once (`world.sky.failed`), not drawn yet. Empty (the default): no sun, nothing written.

latitude.description: Degrees of latitude the sun's course is computed for (0 the equator: the sun climbs to the zenith; the south of the equator sees it cross the north).

northAzimuth.description: Where the north of the world is: degrees around +Y from +Z (core.light's azimuth). The sun rises 90 degrees clockwise from it.

clock.description: The id of the world.clock clock whose hour moves the sun (empty: the first one). Without a clock the sun stays where the hour of the sky (`hour`, `setHour`) puts it.

gradient.description: The numbers of a `gradient` layer when its params leave them out (names provisional): `intensity` (a multiplier of the light of the sky), `horizonTint` (a name of `horizonTints` or a colour #rrggbb that tints the horizon), `atmosphere` (a name of `atmospheres`), `disc` (the sun's disc: `size` its width in degrees, `halo` the strength of its halo, `intensity` its brightness over the sky's, 0 size: no disc), `ambient` (the ambient light of core.light follows the night: `on`, its `color` and `intensity` at night, `dayElevation` / `nightElevation` the heights of the sun where the day ends and the night is complete).

atmospheres.description: The palettes of the computed sky by name (names provisional): `stops`, ordered by the height of the sun in degrees, each with the colour of the zenith and of the horizon, of the glow around the sun and its strength; between two stops the colours blend smoothly, beyond the ends they hold. `earth` is the one a game names by default; `alien` a green sky; `none` has no stop: a sky of nothing (the layer draws nothing).

horizonTints.description: The names a `horizonTint` may take, each a colour #rrggbb that multiplies the horizon of the palette (neutral: #ffffff).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of world.sky (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/world.terrain.title: world.terrain in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/world.terrain.description: What the kit world.terrain adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

relief.description: The relief: { grid: { n, size, centre, heights } } (data: (n + 1)² heights along +X then +Z), else { seed, n, size, centre, heightScale, featureScale, mountains, valleys, cliffs, roughness } (the seeded generator), else a flat ground of size metres (cut into cells of `cell` metres, 0.5 by default, when shapes are given). shapes: [{ kind: plateau | path | flatten | hill | rough, id, enabled, … }] sculpts that relief, laid IN ORDER (names provisional): plateau { points | at + half, height, edge, wobble, wobbleScale } raises a zone to a height with a wall of `edge` metres (steep, never an overhang); path { points, width, shoulder, from, to, maxSlope } levels a band along a line at a constant slope (its slope is in `info`); flatten { at + radius | box, fade, height } levels under an object; hill { at, radius, height } a mound (negative: a hollow); rough { box | at + half, amplitude, scale, fade, seed } bumps. Physics, bake and drawing read the sculpted grid. A bad shape is skipped and said in `info`. basins: true (default) digs the `basin` of the bodies of world.water (when that kit is in the game) in the sculpted relief, AFTER the shapes, the banks shaken by the noise of `seed` (1 by default): false digs nothing. Without world.water, or a body without a `basin`, nothing changes.

shapes.description: The shapes that sculpt the relief, laid IN ORDER (names provisional): each { kind: plateau | path | flatten | hill | rough, id, enabled, ... } with the fields of its kind (see the description of relief).

basins.description: true (default): digs the basin of the bodies of world.water in the sculpted relief, after the shapes; false digs nothing.

cell.description: Metres of one cell of a flat ground cut into cells when shapes are given (0.5 by default).

ground.description: What the ground is made of: { seed, layers: [{ id, texture, tile, ratio, tint, roughness, bump, heightBias, material, depth, occlusion }] (material: a name of core.material: the layer takes that material whole, every map (color, height, normal, metallicRoughness or roughness and metallic, occlusion, emissive) and every number (color and its alpha, roughness, metallic, emissive and emissiveStrength times the emissiveGain, alphaMode and alphaCutoff, opacity, uvRepeat, uvOffset), a change blended over its seconds; depth: metres the height spans; occlusion: 0 to 1), shapes: [{ layer, kind: path | box | patches | disc, … }], rules: [{ layer, slope: { from, full }, height: { from, full }, noise }], blend: { contrast } }. null (the default): no layers, nothing baked.

look.description: How the ground looks beyond its layers (the presentation module): edge { scale, amount }, macro { scale, strength, tint (slow change of brightness and warmth, default 0.12; 0: none) }, random { amount (random offset of each texture per patch, in repeats, default 1; 0: none, one read as before), patch (its size in repeats, default 3), width (of the change from one patch to the next, 0 to 0.5, default 0.2) }, normalFade { from, to, pixel }, textureSize, anisotropy (anisotropic filtering of the layers' textures, 1 to 16, default 16), normalStrength (0 to 4, default 1), triplanar (sharpness on slopes, default 8; 0: seen from above everywhere), parallax { steps (0 default: none, up to 16), grazing, fade }.

bake.description: The extent of the bake: n cells a side over size metres (the relief's by default) centred on centre.

physics.description: The heightfields of core.physics: collide (off: none), tileCells (cells a side of one heightfield), material (a name of core.physics' registry).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

config.description: The settings of world.terrain (its configSchema): the config of its installed entry.

gripforge.kit/world.terrain_destructible.title: world.terrain_destructible in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/world.terrain_destructible.description: What the kit world.terrain_destructible adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

tools.description: The tools by name (logic/tools.json: pickaxe, shovel, builder, grenade, drill, trowel, level, brush), each a kind, a shape and its numbers in metres; a game or a mod changes one or adds one (config tools.<name>), the code by registerTool(name, params).

mode.description: How the volume lives with world.terrain's heightmap: volume, the ground of the region is all volume (the promotion on demand, promote and zones, comes with stage f of the design).

voxelSize.description: Metres between two samples of the grid (a chunk is 32 samples a side: 16 m at 0.5).

seed.description: Seed of the strata's noise; default world.terrain's ground seed, else 7.

region.description: The box of the ground in x and z (air beyond its sides); default the extent of world.terrain's relief.

y.description: The bottom and the top of the volume, metres: under the bottom, rock never edited.

strata.description: What lies under the surface, from the top: a layer of world.terrain by id (@surface: the one world.terrain lays there by its rules and shapes) down to a depth to (metres, its limit broken by noise); the last one without to fills the rest. The top stratum keeps at least one voxel.

materials.description: What the volume adds to a layer of world.terrain, by its id: resistance (0 to 1, the share of a blast it absorbs, default 0.3), indestructible (no operation removes it), material (display only: the name of a material made by core.material that draws the layer whole, through core.material's layered ground: its colour and height, normal, roughness, metalness, occlusion and emissive maps and numbers; each texture key is a texture slot of the game; default the material world.terrain's layer names; without core.material or without that material, world.terrain's texture of the layer).

material.description: Display only: the name of the core.material material that draws the layer (projected triplanar, blended with the other layers by their height).

tools.description: Tools changed or added (merged key by key over the kit's tools.json: pickaxe, shovel, builder, grenade, drill, trowel, level, brush).

kind.description: What the tool does to the ground: dig (subtract), fill (add), blast (subtract, each material resisting), tunnel (a capsule along dir), smooth, flatten (to the plane at its height), paint (the material only), set (the exact shape).

radius.description: Metres.

length.description: Metres along dir: a capsule's or a tunnel's length, a cylinder's height (default twice the radius).

falloff.description: Metres over which the edge is smoothed.

strength.description: A blast's force (its radius times strength times 1 − resistance of each material), the share of smoothing.

noise.description: The edge broken by the integer noise: features of scale metres, pushed by amount metres.

material.description: The layer of world.terrain a fill, a paint or a set lays (by id); without it a fill takes the hook choose_material, else the solid neighbours.

uploadsPerFrame.description: Chunks the drawing meshes and sends a frame at most.

fallbackChunks.description: Without the kit's loop (no shared memory): chunks meshed a tick on the tick.

budget.description: What a frame and a tick may do.

fill.description: Display only: the light of the sky in the shadows of the ground (the bottom of a hole), as a share of its colour, brighter on what faces up. The blank player has no ambient light yet (core.light's ambient is not drawn on Bevy): without it a hole in shadow is black. 0: none.

collide.description: One fixed mesh of core.physics per chunk (entity world.terrain_destructible:<i>,<j>,<k>), replaced when the chunk is meshed again, removed when it is left empty. Nothing without core.physics. Turn world.terrain's physics.collide off over the region, or its heightfield stays under the holes.

normalStrength.description: Display only: how much the normal maps of the layers' materials (materials.<layer>.material) bend the light. 0: flat.

gripforge.kit/world.tracks.description: What the kit world.tracks adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

detail.description: How many prints the player wants: off (nothing is computed or drawn), few, many. The player's setting and the profiles of settings.graphics (profiles) set it.

levels.description: The ring of decals by level: max prints shown at once; the oldest is reused when the ring is full.

profiles.description: The level each display profile of settings.graphics gives, until the player chooses one.

source.description: Where a step comes from: events (core.animation.footstep), stride (the distance walked), auto (stride until the first event is seen, then the events).

rules.description: By layer of the ground: [{ layer, print: mud | snow, opacity, life (s, else `life`), fade (s, else `fade`), genre (steps: the feet, the one there is today), fills (the shoes get muddy), scale (size of the print, 1 = `print`) }]. A layer with no rule leaves nothing, unless the shoes are dirty.

dirty.description: The mud on the shoes: { steps (dirty steps on other ground, up to 64), paleness (0 to 1, how much paler the last one is), opacity, life (s, else `life`), fade (s, else `fade`) }.

life.description: Seconds a print stays, its fade included, unless its rule (or its placer) says.

fade.description: Seconds a print fades out over at the end of its life, unless its rule (or its placer) says. Continuous, computed at the render by the player from the age of the print: nothing is sent again.

placers.description: What a placer of traces (the entity that leaves them: a character, a vehicle…) changes over the rule of the layer, keyed by entity id, tag or kind (that order): { life (s), fade (s), opacity (times), scale (times), dirty: { steps } }. Also set in code: world.tracks.placer(key, settings).

print.description: The size of a print in metres: { length, width, gap (half the distance between the two feet) }. Each surface rule may widen it with `scale`.

stride.description: Metres between two steps when the kit counts the stride itself.

teleport.description: Fallback only, for an entity without a `snap` counter (no game.engine): a move longer than this in one frame is a teleport, not a walk: no step is laid across it. With `snap`, the counter decides, never a distance.

walkers.description: How many characters leave prints (entities of kind or tag player, npc or character).

groundOffset.description: Metres from the origin of a walker down to the ground, used only when no world.terrain says where the ground is (0: the origin is at the feet).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/world.tree.description: What the kit world.tree adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The genres of trees by id, in data (config genres.<id>, registerGenre): a kit, a mod or the game adds its own or changes one field by field.

seed.description: Seed of the shapes and the groves: the same seed always gives the same trees, to the millimetre, on every machine.

groundY.description: Height of the ground a tree given by [x, z] stands on (no ground kit: [x, y, z] gives its own).

lodDistance.description: Metres from the camera beyond which a square of trees is drawn at its far level of detail (main branches and crown balls).

fallbackWork.description: Work a tick spends growing the forest when the kit's loop has no thread (no shared memory on the web): a shape grown counts 4, a tree merged 1 (8: about 2.5 ms natively). With its loop the forest is grown on the loop's thread, a small step at a time.

pieceBytes.description: Bytes of a piece of the forest at most (its near and far meshes; one tree at least): the squares are handed to the player in pieces of this size, one a frame, so that no frame takes a whole square.

additionalProperties.description: A genre of tree, field by field (docs/design/world-tree.md, « Les genres »); a field left out falls through to registerGenre, then to the built-in genre, then to the default of the code.

genres.description: Genres of the game by id, merged field by field over the built-in ones and those of registerGenre (the config has the last word).

trees.description: Trees one by one: [{ genre, at: [x, z] | [x, y, z], yaw, scale, variant, id }].

groves.description: Groves scattered from the seed in a disc, kept spacing metres apart: [{ id, genre, at: [x, z], radius, count, spacing }]. A stand-in until world.scenery places the trees (zones, excluded zones).

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/world.water.description: What the kit world.water adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

genres.description: The genres of water by name (logic/genres.json: lake, river, sea, waterfall, puddle, swamp, muddy, pond), each with its waves and its tint (deepColor, shallowColor, opacity, foam, reflectivity); a game or a mod changes the params of one or adds one (config genres.<name>), the code by registerGenre(name, params), live: the drawing takes the new tint without making the water again.

seed.description: Seed of the swell: the same seed always gives the same waves (each body takes its own from it and its rank, unless it gives one).

wind.description: The wind over the water (with world.weather loaded the swell follows the weather's wind, heard by world.weather.wind.changed): speed in m/s (5 gives each genre its waveHeight; 0 a third of it, 10 and more up to twice), angle in radians in the XZ plane (the main wave runs along it).

genres.description: Genres changed (merged key by key over the kit's data) or added: { <name>: { shape, waveHeight, waveLength, choppiness, waveSpeed, flow, deepColor, shallowColor, opacity, roughness, reflectivity, foam, detail, exitSpeed, gravity, thickness, spread, shore, clarity, shoreFoam } }. shore: metres over which the water thins, its swell dies and its foam runs in at the edge (depth over the body's bed, else distance to the edge; 0: a hard edge); clarity: metres to the deep colour; shoreFoam: 0 to 1.

foamColor.description: PROPOSED name (15/11). #rrggbb of the foam; empty or absent: derived from the water and the sky, never pure white.

foamOpacity.description: PROPOSED name (15/11). How opaque the foam is where it is thickest (0: not seen).

ripples.description: PROPOSED names (15/11). The rings where something moves in the water: height (1: the wave a walker raises, a real displacement of the surface), size (1: the rings scaled), life (seconds), foam (0 to 1: the white they carry, 0: the wave only).

bodies.description: The bodies of water of the game, made at the first tick (add(spec) does the same from code).

id.description: Stable id of the body (else water_<n>).

genre.description: A genre of the registry genres (lake, river, sea, waterfall, puddle, swamp, muddy, pond, or one the game added).

at.description: Centre of an area [x, level, z] (the y is the water level); the lip of a fall.

size.description: Sides of a rectangle of water [x, z], metres (default 20 x 20).

radius.description: Radius of a disc of water, metres (over 0: a disc instead of the rectangle).

seed.description: Seed of the body's waves (default: from the kit's seed and its rank).

params.description: Parameters over the genre's (any key of a genre).

drop.description: A fall: metres from its lip (at) down to its foot (default 6).

angle.description: A fall: the direction it pours to, radians in the XZ plane (0 = +X).

pool.description: A fall: the genre of the pool made at its foot (default lake), or false for none.

tintFrom.description: A fall: the genre whose water it is drawn with (deepColor, shallowColor, opacity, reflectivity, roughness), under the fall's own params. Default: its pool's genre (the sheet is the water it pours into; the fall's own genre when pool is false); false: the fall's own genre.

joins.description: PROPOSED name (16/11, Damien may rename). A river that flows out of and/or into another water: start / end = the id of the body its first / last point lies in, fade = metres over which its opacity fades out at that end (default 3), so the ribbon dissolves into that water instead of stopping in a straight edge. An end is only faded where the named body really covers it. Give both waters the same level (and the same tintFrom, or genre colours) so they meet without a step or a change of colour.

bed.description: The floor under the water: given by the game, sampled once (the kit reads no terrain for it), or, when the body declares a `basin` and world.terrain is in the game, read at the first tick on the ground that dug the basin (world.terrain `bedOf`): { at: [x0, z0], step, count: [nx, nz], heights: [nx * nz numbers, row by row along x] }, at most 128 x 128, bilinear between samples. The shore is then measured as depth, the shallows are clear, and where the floor rises above the level (the rim of a basin, an islet) there is no water: nothing drawn, waterAt and heightAt answer null.

basin.description: PROPOSED name (15/11, Damien may rename). The hollow a ground digs for this water, read by the kits that read bodies() (a terrain, a room's ground; the water draws nothing of it): depth = metres under the level at the deepest, margin = metres of bank (the ground rises from the level at the water's edge to its own height over that width; the floor falls from the level to its full depth over the same width inside). Area bodies (disc or rectangle).

mesh.description: An object to waterise instead of the kit's shape: { positions: [[x, y, z], ...], indices: [...], uvs?: [[u, v], ...] } in world metres. It is drawn with the water of the body's genre (a fall: flow, foam, spray at its foot). Without uvs, v runs from its top to its bottom (the flow) and u around it.

sky.description: The sky the water reflects where the engine gives none (the presentation module of the blank player; world.sky or core.light will give it later): zenith and horizon colours (#rrggbb) and the strength of the reflection.

walkers.description: The walkers (entities tagged character, player or npc) are told when their feet come into a body (world.water.entered) and leave it (world.water.left), at the tick. false: nothing asked, the kit rests.

walkerHold.description: PROPOSED name (hysteresis of the walkers): metres a walker already in a body is kept in it past its edge (bank, width, dry rim of the bed, height over the level) before world.water.left; entering stays at the edge. 0: none, a step back and forth over the edge says entered and left each time.

ripples.description: Display only (nothing saved): the rings where a character (an entity with character.capsule) meets the water, written once each into the water's material and spreading in its shader. contacts: rings alive at once per body (0 to 8; 0: none, nothing computed); stride: metres waded between two rings; strength: their height and foam; wakes (PROPOSED name): bodies that wake a flowing river at once, a collar of foam and a V behind each, as behind a stone (0 to 16; 0: none, nothing computed).

current.description: The current of a river on what stands in it (PROPOSED name, 15/11). push: how hard running water pushes a walker (0 to 2; 0: none, nothing asked of the physics); the push is the river's velocity at the walker's place over the tick, scaled by how deep it stands.

rocks.description: Stones the water flows around, besides world.natural's rocks (read when it is loaded): [{ at: [x, z], radius }]. Foam and eddies form around them, their tops break the surface.

debugger.description: The look of this kit's tab in the F9 debugger, over the kit's own (its expose entries' `debugger`): `icon` of the tab (an icon name, an image of the kit or an emoji), `assets` { name: url }, `entries` { <entry id>: { curve: 'large', actions: { <action>: { view: 'presets' | 'clock', options: { <value>: { icon, label } } } } } }. gripforge.kit/world.weather.title: world.weather in a .gripforge project
gripforge.kit/world.weather.description: What the kit world.weather adds to a project (GENERATED by tools/project-schema/project-schema.mjs from kit.api.json - do not edit).

preset.description: Weather at start: clear, snow, blizzard, rain, storm or fog. Clear by default: nothing falls, no fog, no cover, full grip, until the game picks a weather (here, a scene layer, a rule, the cycle or set()). Only the weather of a game with no core.settings: with it, the weather at start is the player setting world.weather.preset (the game sets it with patches["world.weather.preset"] = { default }), never this config.

intensity.description: Scales falling snow or rain, wind and fog (multiplier 0..1). Also the player setting world.weather.intensity declared to core.settings (group graphics, a value per mode).

cycle.description: Pick a new weather from cyclePresets every cycleMinutes.

cyclePresets.description: Weathers the cycle picks from, every cycleMinutes, when cycle is on.

cycleMinutes.description: Real minutes between two weathers picked by the cycle.

transitionSeconds.description: Seconds a new weather takes to fade in, when the change gives no duration of its own.

windDirection.description: Degrees from +Z towards +X the wind blows to. Also the player setting world.weather.windDirection; wind() gives it and world.weather.wind.changed tells when it moves, for the kits that follow the wind (world.water, world.natural).

lightningEvery.description: Average seconds between two lightning strokes while a storm blows (a stroke comes between 0.4 and 1.6 times this). Also the player setting world.weather.lightningEvery. A stroke is asked at any time by strike().

lightningPower.description: How strong a stroke is, 0..1: the flash of light on the scene and the flare of the sky. Also the player setting world.weather.lightningPower.

clouds.description: How much of the sky the clouds of the dome hide, as a share of what the weather brings (proposed name): 1 = the weather's own cover (a few clouds in clear air, a closed sky in a storm), 0 = no cloud at all. Also the player setting world.weather.clouds.

gusts.description: Random gust strength on top of the preset wind (0..1).

accumulation.description: How fast snow covers the ground (0 = never, 1 = within a minute).

slippery.description: Grip lost on full snow cover or after heavy rain (traction = 1 - slippery x max(cover, wetness x 0.6)).

fogVisibility.description: Fog and blizzard reduce how far enemies see (visibility in the snapshot).

cold.description: Players (entities tagged player) freeze in snow and blizzard and warm up near warmth sources.

coldRate.description: Multiplier of the cold gained per second while exposed.

warmthTag.description: Entities with this tag (braziers, fires) warm everything within warmthRadius.

enabled.description: PROPOSED NAME. No rain, snow, wet ground or snow cover under a roof, bridge, tree or awning, found from the scene itself (a top-down depth picture of the zone around the camera, made once and again only when the scene changes or the camera leaves the zone). Needs a host that can render a height target; without one the sky is open everywhere (declared fallback).

resolution.description: PROPOSED NAME. Texels on a side of the shelter picture over an 80 m zone (256 is about 31 cm a texel, 2048 about 4 cm); one 16-bit channel each.

shelter.description: PROPOSED NAME. The shelter map: where the sky is covered.

warmthRadius.description: Metres around an entity tagged warmthTag within which players warm up.

preset.description: The weather while the condition holds.

priority.description: The highest-priority rule that holds wins (default 0; a tie goes to the first in the list).

minSeconds.description: Seconds the weather it set is held before another rule (or none) may change it (default 0).

rules.description: Weather on conditions, checked four times a second with the kit transition: the highest-priority rule that holds wins (a tie goes to the first); whatever set the weather keeps it minSeconds; no rule holding: the cycle or the fixed preset.

Optional: without it, the kit's defaults (kits/debug_inspector/README.md « Option debugger »).

A zone may carry a field of core.physics: physicsField { kind, ...the fields of a field } becomes core.physics.addField with the zone's shape (sphere, box; a polygon through its sensor), id zone:<id>, removed with the zone; nothing without core.physics (docs/design/core-physics-champs.md).
